- If you need an outbound webhook, register a `WebhookEndpoint` subscribed to the corresponding
  outbox event type instead of listening to the Eloquent/domain event directly.
- If you need a queued side-effect (e.g. send a notification, update a search index), have your
  listener enqueue a job for the relayed webhook/activity payload — i.e. drive it from something
  that already only fires after commit — rather than from `NodeGrantCreated` /
  `NodeGrantRevoked` / `NodeShareCreated` / `NodeShareRevoked` themselves.

**If you cannot make your listener synchronous+idempotent right now**, detach it from these four
events (`Event::forget(...)` in your provider, or remove the listener registration) rather than
leave a queued/non-idempotent listener attached — an unreviewed queued listener on these events
will misbehave under transaction rollback.

No config change, migration, or database schema change is required for this upgrade note; it is a
pure code-contract change on the four events listed above.

### `vaulter-core` split into four Composer packages — require the ones you use (P2 #5 / D1, D2, D3)

**Why.** `vaulter-core` shipped the CAS blob engine, the Drive tree/uploads and the whole document
& collaboration stack in one package, so a host that wanted only a node tree still pulled in TipTap
and Yjs. The engines moved out into three standalone packages. The dependency direction is one-way
(`drive` → `core` + `media`; `documents` → `core`) — there is no cycle, and `vaulter-drive` is not a
runtime dependency of `vaulter-documents`.

**What moved.**

| Package | Namespace | What went there |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `axioma-studio/vaulter-media` | `Vaulter\Media\*` | The CAS engine — `Sha256ContentStore`, `FlysystemStorageDriver`, `BlobStore`, `BlobGarbageCollector`, `BlobReconciler`, `StagedTempObject` (was `Vaulter\Cas\*`) — and the `vaulter:gc-blobs` / `vaulter:reconcile-blobs` commands. |
| `axioma-studio/vaulter-drive` | `Vaulter\Drive\*` | `DriveContext`, `DriveManager`, `StorageManager`, the Drive Actions (`TrashNodeAction`, `UploadFileAction`), the Drive events (`FileUploaded`, `NodeCreated`, `NodeMoved`, `NodeTrashed`, `StorageCreated`, …), the Drive/Storage/Upload HTTP layer, the whole `Uploads\*` subtree (tus + S3-multipart), and the `vaulter:purge-trash` / `vaulter:sweep-uploads` commands. |
| `axioma-studio/vaulter-documents` | `Vaulter\Documents\*` | The document Actions (`CreateDocumentAction`, `UpdateDocumentContentAction`, `CreateNamedRevisionAction`, `RestoreDocumentRevisionAction`, the comment Actions, `PersistCollaborationStateAction`), the `Collaboration\*` drivers, the handlers (`TipTapHandler`, `PreviewHandler`, `DownloadOnlyHandler`, `UniverHandler`), `HtmlExporter` / `MarkdownExporter`, the `NodeComment` / `DocumentRevision` models and the document/collaboration/comment controllers. |

**What stays in `vaulter-core`.** The contracts and schema, so the seams a host implements against
do not move: `Contracts\Cas\*`, the `v_blobs` schema, `Models\Cas\Blob`, `Enums\Cas\BlobStatus`,
`Repositories\Cas\BlobStoreRepository`; `Contracts\Drive\{DriveHandle,DriveHandleFactory}`,
`Support\DriveNameRules`, `Exceptions\Nodes\NodeNameConflictException`,
`Http\Resources\Drive\NodeResource` and the `v_nodes` / `v_upload_sessions` / `v_upload_parts`
schemas; the handler-seam contracts and value objects and the `v_node_comments` /
`v_node_document_versions` schemas.

**What to do.**

1. Add the packages whose behaviour you actually use:
   - node CRUD, `Vaulter::for()` / `forStorage()`, uploads or downloads →
     `composer require axioma-studio/vaulter-drive`
   - file upload/download/versioning (the blob engine behind Drive) →
     `composer require axioma-studio/vaulter-media`
   - document editing, versioning, comments or realtime collaboration →
     `composer require axioma-studio/vaulter-documents`
2. Repoint any direct FQCN references per the table above. If a host referenced only the contracts
   and value objects listed under *What stays in core*, nothing changes.

   > The handler-seam contracts and value objects were renamed **again** later in this same
   > unreleased cycle. Land on `Contracts\Handlers\*` / `ValueObjects\Handlers\*` — see the
   > kind-neutral-rename note above for the final FQCNs.
3. Config: `vaulter.cas.*` and `vaulter.dedup.*` are unchanged. `vaulter.models.{upload_session,
   upload_part}` and `vaulter.models.{node_comment,node_document_version}` are no longer defaulted
   by core — they **guard-throw** when the owning package is absent, which is the intended signal
   that you need to `require` it. `vaulter.exporters` defaults to `[]` in core.

### The legacy `document_id`-bound path (DocVault) is removed (ADR-0014 step 2)

**Why.** Two parallel document models coexisted: the original `document_id`-bound one
(`v_document*` tables) and the node-attached one on `v_nodes`. One canonical path replaces both —
`kind=document` nodes, with comments and versions attached to the node.

**Removed.** The `Document`, `DocumentFolder`, `DocumentVersion`, `DocumentPermission`,
`DocumentComment` and `DocumentShare` models, their `v_document*` tables and migrations, and the
matching repositories, controllers, Actions, events, resources and requests. Also removed: the
`Document`-bound collaboration seam (`Contracts\Collaboration\CollaborationDriver`, its Reverb and
Hocuspocus implementations, and `Vaulter::driver()`); the `Contracts\Access\PermissionResolver`
seam (`Vaulter::resolvePermissionsWith()`, `permissionResolver()` and the
`vaulter.permission_resolver` config key); and the
`vaulter.models.{document,version,folder,permission,comment,share}` config entries with their
table names.

**What to do.** Move to `Vaulter::for()` and the node/document endpoints. Replace a
`CollaborationDriver` implementation with `Contracts\CollaborationDriver` (node-attached, see
the collaboration notes above), and a `PermissionResolver` implementation with the host role driver.
Drop the removed `vaulter.models.*` and `vaulter.permission_resolver` keys from your published
config.

**Data.** A dev-only, idempotent `drop_legacy_docvault_tables` migration drops any pre-existing
`v_document*` tables. It does **not** migrate data. If you carry production rows in `v_document*`,
back them up and port them onto `v_nodes` **before** running migrations — the package ships no
backfill.

### `@vaulter/vue` dropped the legacy document-centric surface (ADR-0014 step 4)

**Why.** The removed client surface called the `/documents`, `/folders` and `/documents/*` HTTP
endpoints that no longer exist after the DocVault excision above; it could only have 404'd.

**Removed → use instead.**

| Removed | Replacement |
|:--|:--|
| client namespaces `documents`, `versions`, `folders`, `permissions`, `shares`, legacy `collaboration` | `client.nodes`, `client.grants`, `client.nodeShares` |
| `useDocuments`, `usePermissions`, `useShares`, `useDocumentExport`, `useCollaboration`, `useVaulterEditor` | `useNodes`, `useNodeGrants`, `useNodeShares`, `useDocumentNode`, `useNodeCollaboration` |
| `VaulterFileManager`, `VaulterEditor`, `VaulterVersionHistory`, `VaulterPermissionsPanel`, `VaulterSharePanel`, `VaulterBreadcrumb` | `VaulterDrive` |
| `createCollaborationSession` transport | `useNodeCollaboration` |

`useComments` and `VaulterCommentsPanel` survive but were **repointed** to the node comment API
(`/nodes/{node}/comments`): the prop is now `nodeId`, not `documentId`.

## Канон PHP API 0.3 (AD03, AD04, AD05, AD11, AD14)

Все следующие FQN переименованы жёстко, без class_alias и deprecated-обёрток.
Имена таблиц, колонок, ключи конфигурации и значения событий на этом шаге остаются прежними;
их переход описывается отдельными изменениями схемы и конфигурации.

title: Architecture
description: The layered architecture of Vaulter, its domain structure, the contracts a host plugs into, and the 13 ADRs that decide it.
outline: deep
---

# Architecture

Vaulter is a strictly-typed, layered Laravel package built to **embed** in an existing
application. The guiding rule is a clean split of ownership:

- **Everything the host must provide is a contract** — authorization, the byte plane, the
  collaboration transport, the share-token shape, the document-format handlers. Each is an
  interface bound in the container and swappable through config.
- **Everything Vaulter owns is `final` and typed** — the effective-permission engine, the
  Drive Actions, the CAS lifecycle, the panel registry. These are not contracts: they are
  the package's guarantees.

The result is one package that drops into a plain Laravel app *and* a multi-tenant CoreX SaaS
without a fork — see [ADR-0003](/adr/0003-embeddability-data-model) and its successors
[ADR-0009](/adr/0009-storage-panels) / [ADR-0011](/adr/0011-id-strategy).

::: tip Where to start
If you just want to use Vaulter, read [Quick Start](/guide/quick-start) and
[Configuration](/guide/configuration). This page is the mental model behind those — useful
when you extend a seam or debug a layer.
:::

## The request, end to end

```
@vaulter/vue  ──HTTP/JSON──►  Controllers ─► FormRequests ─► DTOs (Data\*)
              ──WebSocket──►  CollaborationDriver (Hocuspocus)
       │
  AccessResolver (Vaulter-owned)  ◄── PermissionDriver (host, swappable)
       │                              + v_node_grants ACL
  Actions (final readonly · transactional · dispatch domain Events)
       │
  Repositories (read / store split)
       │
  CAS:  BlobStore ─► ContentStore (sha256) ─► StorageDriver (Flysystem disk)
       │
  Models (swappable via config) ─► Database (v_* tables, one id-strategy)
```

A typical write — say `POST storages/{storage}/uploads` — flows top to bottom:

1. The **controller** route-model-binds the `{storage}` (or `{node}`) through the swappable
   model, then authorizes the action against the [`AccessResolver`](#authorization).
2. A **FormRequest** validates and a **DTO** (`Vaulter\Data\*`) carries the typed payload.
3. An **Action** (`final readonly`, e.g. `IngestFileAction`) opens the transaction, calls the
   **CAS** to stage + dedup the bytes, writes the `v_nodes` / `v_files` rows through **store
   repositories**, and dispatches a domain **Event** after commit.
4. Subscribers (`RecordsActivity`, `RecordsOutbox`) react to the event to write the activity
   feed and stage the transactional outbox — Vaulter never couples the Action to them.

The ergonomic entry point `Vaulter::for($entity)` returns a
[`DriveHandle`](#the-drive-handle) (`Vaulter\Drive\DriveHandle`, shipped by
`axioma-studio/vaulter-drive`) that wraps exactly this pipeline for programmatic use.

## Layers

### HTTP edge — Controllers, FormRequests, Resources

The thin edge. Routes live in `packages/core/routes/api.php`, mounted under
`config('vaulter.route_prefix')` (default `api/vaulter`). Controllers authorize, hand a DTO to
an Action, and serialize the result through a Resource that embeds a computed `abilities`
object so the Vue client renders only allowed actions.

`{storage}` and `{node}` route parameters bind to the **swappable** models
(`config('vaulter.models.storage|node')`) via `Route::bind` registered in the service
provider — so a host can point the config at a subclass and binding keeps working.

### Actions — `Vaulter\Drive\Actions\*` / `Vaulter\Documents\Actions\*` / `Vaulter\Actions\*`

One use case each, `final readonly`. An Action opens the transaction, enforces business rules,
calls repositories/CAS, and dispatches a domain event **after commit**. The Drive write set
(`Vaulter\Drive\Actions\*`, requires `axioma-studio/vaulter-drive`):
`CreateFolderAction`, `IngestFileAction`, `MoveNodeAction`, `RenameNodeAction`,
`CopyNodeAction`, `TrashNodeAction`, `RestoreNodeAction`, `PurgeNodeAction`. Document-node
Actions live under `Vaulter\Documents\Actions\*` (requires `axioma-studio/vaulter-documents`);
core itself only keeps `Vaulter\Actions\{Access,Sharing,Webhooks}\*`.

::: info Authorization placement
Actions perform **no** access checks. Authorization is enforced once, at the HTTP boundary
(`NodeController` + `AccessResolver`), before the Action runs. `DriveHandle` is likewise a
pure delegation surface. This keeps the access decision in exactly one place.
:::

### Repositories — read / store split

Reads (`NodeReadRepository`, `GrantReadRepository`, `DriveReadRepository`, …) build queries;
stores (`NodeStoreRepository`, `DriveStoreRepository`, …) perform writes and never open
transactions or dispatch events — the Action owns that. The tree-descent reads use
`staudenmeir/laravel-adjacency-list` recursive relations scoped by `storage_id`.

### Models — swappable, resolved through `Config`

Vaulter never references a concrete model class directly in domain code; it resolves through
`Vaulter\Support\Config` against `config('vaulter.models.*')`. A host subclasses a model to add
ULID behaviour, tenant scoping, or audit. Models are the one part of the package that is **not**
`final` (they must be extendable); everything else is.

### Value objects, DTOs, enums

`Vaulter\Data\*` are the `final readonly` DTOs Actions consume. `Vaulter\ValueObjects\*` hold
domain values (`FileDescriptor`, `ContentCapabilities`, the ACL
`Subject`/`Decision`/`GrantSet`/`AccessScope`) — kind-neutral only; core does not know the shape of
any handler's content (`TipTapContent` and friends live in `vaulter-documents`, VLT-CANON P0.3).
`Vaulter\Enums\*` are the sealed vocabularies (`Ability`, `NodeKind`, `BlobStatus`, …).

## Domain structure

Since the P2 #5 package extraction split the monolith, `axioma-studio/vaulter-core`
(namespace `Vaulter\`) holds only the cross-cutting seams — authorization, CAS
value-objects/contracts, sharing, panels, webhooks, activity — under `packages/core/src`;
Drive and Documents each ship as their own package:

| Directory (core) | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `Access/` | `AccessResolver` (the effective-permission engine), `PermissionDriverManager`, `HostUserResolver`. |
| `Drivers/Permission/` | The shipped `PermissionDriver` lanes: `database`, `gate`, `spatie`; `azgard` lives in `vaulter-azgard`. |
| `Cas/` | `BlobLock` — the last CAS class left in core; the store engine itself moved to `vaulter-media`. |
| `Profiles/` | `Profile`, `ProfileProvider`, `ProfileRegistry`. |
| `Schema/` | `SchemaBuilder`, `VaulterSchema`. |
| `Engines/` | The format-extensibility registry ENGINE (VLT-CANON P0.4, superseding H.5/T5): `FileHandlerRegistry`, `NodePresenter`, `FileDescriptorFactory`, and the baseline `Handlers/{PreviewHandler,DownloadOnlyHandler}` — always bound, so a drive-only host resolves preview/download with no other package installed. |
| `Schema/` | The id-strategy classes (`AutoIncrementIds`/`UlidIds`/`Uuid7Ids`) + `IdStrategyResolver`, `SchemaBuilder` columns. |
| `Sharing/` | The bearer-link channel: `ShareResolver`, `ShareContext`, `ShareResult`. |
| `Webhooks/` | The reliability layer: `OutboxRecorder`, `OutboxRelay`, `WebhookSigner`. |
| `Activity/` | The append-only activity feed (`ActivityRecorder`, `RecordsActivity`). |
| `Actions/` · `Data/` · `Events/` | Access, Sharing and Webhooks only — Drive and Documents actions/events now live in their own packages (see below). |
| `ValueObjects/Handlers/` | The kind-neutral handler-seam value objects both Drive and Documents depend on: `FileDescriptor`, `ContentCapabilities`, `ViewerDescriptor`, `NodePresentation`. |
| `Contracts/` | Every host-facing seam, including `Contracts/Drive/*` and `Contracts/Handlers/*` (the interfaces the split packages implement). |
| `Models/` · `Repositories/` | Access, Activity, Cas, Drive, Sharing, Webhooks — the shared/read-side pieces; Drive and Documents ship their own write-side models too. |
| `Testing/` | Ship-with-package doubles: `NullPermissionDriver`; `FakeAzgardGuard` lives in `vaulter-azgard`. |

| Package | Namespace | Adds |
|---|---|---|
| `axioma-studio/vaulter-drive` | `Vaulter\Drive\` | `DriveHandle`, `DriveProvisioner`, the Drive Actions (`CreateFolderAction`, `IngestFileAction`, `MoveNodeAction`, …) and their Events. |
| `axioma-studio/vaulter-documents` | `Vaulter\Documents\` | Document-node Actions/Events/Models, the TipTap/Univer format drivers (added to core's registry — the engine itself is core-owned since P0.4), node export, the node-collaboration session service, the TipTap content shapes (`ValueObjects\{TipTapContent,OpaqueDocumentContent,LinkSchemeValidator}`, `Exceptions\InvalidDocumentContentException`). |
| `axioma-studio/vaulter-media` | `Vaulter\Media\` | The CAS engine: `Cas\{BlobStore,Sha256ContentStore,FlysystemStorageDriver,BlobGarbageCollector,BlobReconciler,StagedTempObject}`. |
| `axioma-studio/vaulter-filament` | `Vaulter\Filament\` | The Filament 5 admin plugin. |
| `axioma-studio/vaulter-azgard` | `Vaulter\Azgard\` | The AzGuard permission driver, guard contract, permission map, real adapter and test fake. |
| `@vaulter/vue` | — | The Drive UI + composables (npm). |

All are siblings that build on `vaulter-core`; Drive and document-editing features require
installing the matching package (see [Installation](/guide/installation)).

## The Drive handle

`Vaulter::for($entity, panel: '…')` is the primary integration entry point. It is a thin
facade over `VaulterManager`, returning a `DriveHandle` from `axioma-studio/vaulter-drive`
(the package must be installed for this handle to be usable):

```php
use Vaulter\Facades\Vaulter;

// Get-or-create the storage mounted on $project in the 'default' panel,
// returning an ergonomic DriveHandle.
$drive = Vaulter::for($project);

$folder = $drive->createFolder('Contracts');
$node   = $drive->upload($request->file('doc'), into: $folder);
$drive->rename($node, 'signed.pdf');
$children = $drive->list($folder); // Collection<Node>
```

`VaulterManager::for()` get-or-creates the `v_storages` row through `DriveProvisioner` (the
polymorphic `(owner_type, owner_id, panel)` triple is the idempotency key, guarded by a partial
unique index), auto-provisions a `kind=folder` root node, and returns a `DriveHandle` whose
methods each delegate to one Action or the read repository. The handle adds no business logic —
only a pre-resolved storage and upload-source normalisation (a PSR stream, `SplFileInfo` /
`UploadedFile`, an open resource, or a raw string all normalise to a seekable stream).

::: details VaulterManager
`for()`, `forStorage()`, `profiles()`, `registerDocumentType()`, `documentTypes()`,
`handlers()`, `registerExporter()`, `exporter()`, `exporterFormats()`.
[Facade and manager](/reference/facade).
:::

## Storage Panels — the embeddability axis

A **Storage Profile** is a named config envelope bound to *any* host entity, living over the
**one shared `v_*` schema with no tables of its own** (zero migrations). It is the
isolation/configuration axis, separate from the *storage type* (the policy preset
`private | team | public`).

A panel is built fluently and registered by FQCN only (config-cache-safe — no closures):

```php
use Vaulter\Profiles\Profile;
use Vaulter\Profiles\ProfileProvider;

final class ProjectDriveProfile extends ProfileProvider
{
    public function profile(Profile $panel): Profile
    {
        return $panel
            ->id('project_drive')
            ->host(\App\Models\Project::class)
            ->storageType('team')
            ->feature('document_versions', true);
    }
}
```

Register the provider in `config('vaulter.panels')`. `ProfileRegistry` hydrates profiles
during application boot. Scaffold a provider with `php artisan vaulter:make:profile <name>`.
Profiles share one schema; own tables, model maps, pipelines and resource hooks are removed.
See [Drive profiles](/guide/storage-panels).

## Data model

Everything lives in the prefixed `v_*` schema (`config('vaulter.table_prefix')`, default `v_`),
with one id strategy per install (`config('vaulter.ids.default')`, default `ulid`).

| Table | Holds |
|---|---|
| `v_storages` | One storage per `(owner_type, owner_id, panel)`; carries the disk + root node id. |
| `v_nodes` | The **unified tree** — every folder, file, document, shortcut as one row with `parent_id` + a `kind` discriminator ([ADR-0005](/adr/0005-unified-node-tree)). |
| `v_files` / `v_file_versions` / `v_file_version_blobs` | The binary side tables: a file's head + its version chain + the edges to blobs. |
| `v_blobs` | The CAS: one row per `(scope, sha256)` with a `BlobStatus` lifecycle ([ADR-0006](/adr/0006-content-addressed-blobs-gc)). |
| `v_node_grants` | The per-node ACL with inheritance + deny-veto. |
| `v_node_shares` | Bearer share links — hash-only token storage ([ADR-0013](/adr/0013-two-sharing-channels)). |
| `v_node_document_versions` | Documents: node-attached document version history (gated by `document_versions`). |
| `v_upload_sessions` / `v_upload_parts` | Resumable upload sessions. |
| `v_activity` | The append-only activity feed. |
| `v_outbox` / `v_webhook_endpoints` / `v_webhook_deliveries` | The transactional-outbox + webhook reliability layer. |

The tree is an **adjacency list**: move/rename is a single `UPDATE` of `parent_id` / `name`
(no path rewriting). Descent uses recursive CTEs scoped by `storage_id`; recursive descendant
*aggregation* (`whereHas` / `withCount('descendants')`) is **banned from request paths** (fatal
on MariaDB) and enforced by an arch test — see [Troubleshooting](/guide/troubleshooting#mariadb-cte).

## Authorization

Two lanes, evaluated by the Vaulter-owned `AccessResolver` ([ADR-0007](/adr/0007-pluggable-authorization)):

- **`PermissionDriver`** — the host's pluggable, per-panel role lane. It never sees a `Node` and
  never deals in magic-string actions; it answers `resolve(Subject, Authorizable, AccessScope)`,
  `override(...)` (super-admin / `Gate::before`), `subjectsFor(Authorizable)` (actor → users +
  roles + teams) and `canCreateInWorkspace(...)`. Shipped lanes: `database` (default,
  standalone), `gate`, `spatie`, `azgard`, and the non-prod `null`. Swap via
  `config('vaulter.drivers.permission')`.
- **`AccessResolver`** — Vaulter-owned, `final`, **not** swappable. It runs the canonical
  algorithm over `v_node_grants` combined with the driver.

The algorithm (deny-veto, explicit-beats-inherited):

1. **Host override** (super-admin) is absolute, both directions.
2. Walk ancestors **nearest-first**, bounded to the storage root, collecting direct +
   `scope=subtree` grants for the actor's subject-set; **stop** at the first ancestor with
   `inherit_grants = false`.
3. `aclAllow = max(allow bits)`; `deniedBits = OR(deny bits)`; a **nearer** explicit allow
   pierces a **farther** inherited deny (a same-node deny always wins).
4. `granted = max(aclAllow, roleAllow)` where `roleAllow` comes from the driver.
5. **Final veto**: if `deniedBits` covers the requested ability → DENY, regardless of role.

Abilities (`Vaulter\Enums\Access\Ability`) map to CRUDS bits: `View/Download/Comment → READ`,
`Edit → UPDATE`, `Create/Copy → CREATE`, `Move → UPDATE+CREATE`, `Trash/Restore/Delete → DELETE`,
`Share → SHARE`, `Manage → ALL`.

::: warning No driver = fail-loud in production
The open `null` driver is selectable **only outside production**; `PermissionDriverManager`
throws `MissingPermissionDriverException` if a production app resolves it. Bind a real driver
before you deploy — see [Troubleshooting](/guide/troubleshooting#no-permission-driver).
:::

The identity ACL and the **bearer-link** channel are evaluated as **separate passes, never
unioned** ([ADR-0013](/adr/0013-two-sharing-channels)) — a link cannot escalate via a viewer's
grants, and an identity grant cannot leak through a link.

## Content-addressed storage (CAS)

The binary plane is a content-addressed store, not `spatie/laravel-medialibrary`
([ADR-0008](/adr/0008-media-library-decision)). Three swappable services
(`config('vaulter.cas.*')`):

- **`ContentStore`** (`Sha256ContentStore`) — stages bytes to a seekable temp file and computes
  the `sha256` content address from the staged file (never from a live stream or a client-sent
  hash).
- **`StorageDriver`** (`FlysystemStorageDriver`) — the byte plane over a Flysystem disk, with a
  conditional `put` (`If-None-Match: *` on S3) and `temporaryUrl`.
- **`BlobStore`** — the race-free lifecycle orchestrator. Liveness is the *existence of an edge*
  in `v_file_version_blobs`; `ref_count` is a rebuildable cache. GC is two-phase and lock-first
  (`PENDING → COMMITTED → TOMBSTONED → DELETED`) with resurrection of a tombstoned blob that a
  concurrent upload re-references.

The physical key is **scope-qualified** `<scope>/ab/cd/<sha256>` where `<scope>` follows
`config('vaulter.dedup.scope')` (`tenant` by default), so one scope's GC can never delete
another scope's bytes ([ADR-0012](/adr/0012-dedup-scope)). See the
[blob GC recipe](/guide/recipes#blob-gc) and the
[custom storage driver recipe](/guide/recipes#s3-disk).

## Realtime collaboration

Yjs is the source of truth; TipTap JSON is the derived projection. The transport is swappable
behind `CollaborationDriver` ([ADR-0001](/adr/0001-collaboration-transport)):

- **`hocuspocus`** — an external Node hub (`hocuspocus-server/`). The client connects with a
  signed room JWT; the hub calls back into the `collab/authenticate` + `collab/store` webhooks.

Every seam a host plugs into, and where it is documented:

The reasoning behind every choice above lives in the [ADRs](/adr/). The full set:

| ADR | Decides | Status |
|---|---|---|
| [0001](/adr/0001-collaboration-transport) | Collaboration transport — `CollaborationDriver`, Hocuspocus room JWTs; Reverb Yjs transport removed. | accepted |
| [0002](/adr/0002-authorization-delegation) | Authorization delegated to the host (`PermissionResolver`). | refined by 0007 |
| [0003](/adr/0003-embeddability-data-model) | Embeddability via swappable models + dual key type. | superseded by 0009 / 0011 |
| [0004](/adr/0004-content-format) | TipTap JSON content + append-only bounded version history. | accepted |
| [0005](/adr/0005-unified-node-tree) | One adjacency-list tree (`v_nodes`) for folders/files/documents/shortcuts. | accepted |
| [0006](/adr/0006-content-addressed-blobs-gc) | Content-addressed blobs + two-phase race-free GC. | accepted |
| [0007](/adr/0007-pluggable-authorization) | `PermissionDriver` (pluggable) + `AccessResolver` (owned), deny-veto. | accepted |
| [0008](/adr/0008-media-library-decision) | A custom CAS instead of `spatie/laravel-medialibrary`. | accepted |
| [0009](/adr/0009-storage-panels) | Storage Panels — config-first, zero-migration envelopes. | accepted |
| [0010](/adr/0010-php-npm-monorepo-release) | One repo, two package managers, two release channels. | accepted |
| [0011](/adr/0011-id-strategy) | `bigint | ulid | uuid7` behind an `IdStrategy` seam (ULID default). | accepted |
| [0012](/adr/0012-dedup-scope) | Per-tenant dedup by default + scope-qualified storage keys. | accepted |
| [0013](/adr/0013-two-sharing-channels) | Identity ACL and bearer links evaluated as separate passes. | accepted |

Two supersession chains to keep in mind: **0003 → 0009 / 0011** (embeddability mechanics) and
**0002 → 0007** (authorization delegation).

# Authorization

Vaulter answers exactly one authorization question: **may this actor perform this
ability on this node?** The answer is computed by a single, Vaulter-owned engine —
the `AccessResolver` — that folds together two lanes:

1. the **per-node ACL** (`v_node_grants` rows), Vaulter's own grant store; and
2. a **swappable host-role lane** (`PermissionDriver`) that bridges your application's
   identity and role system in.

The resolver itself is **not** a contract and **not** swappable — only the host-role
lane is. This page documents the engine, its algorithm, and the rules that make a
decision deterministic. The role drivers are covered in
[Permission Drivers](./permission-drivers), and the grant rows themselves in
[Grants](./grants).

::: info Two lanes, one authority
The `AccessResolver` is the single authority every Policy, `DriveHandle`, controller
and Resource asks. It lives at `Vaulter\Access\AccessResolver`. The host plugs into
it through the `PermissionDriver` contract — never by replacing the resolver.
:::

## The public surface

`AccessResolver` exposes a small, stable API. Everything else is private.

| Method | Returns | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `can(Authorizable $actor, Ability $ability, Node $node)` | `bool` | The single yes/no entry point Policies and the `DriveHandle` call. |
| `effectiveGrants(Authorizable $actor, Node $node)` | `GrantSet` | The folded result of the whole algorithm — allow-mask, deny-mask, level. |
| `abilitiesFor(Authorizable $actor, Node $node)` | `array<string, bool>` | Every `Ability` mapped to allowed/denied — fills the UI `abilities` object. |
| `canCreateInWorkspace(Authorizable $actor, Storage $storage)` | `bool` | The create gate for folders/uploads, where there is no existing node. |
| `sharedNodeIds(Authorizable $actor)` | `list<int\|string>` | The candidate node ids the actor has any live allow-grant on. |
| `filterSharedWith(Authorizable $actor, iterable $candidates)` | `list<Node>` | Re-resolves "shared with me" candidates through the full algorithm. |

```php
use Vaulter\Access\AccessResolver;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Ability;

$resolver = app(AccessResolver::class);

if ($resolver->can($user, Ability::Edit, $node)) {
    // the actor may edit this node
}
```

`can()` is sugar over `effectiveGrants($actor, $node)->allows($ability)` — there is one
place the algorithm lives, and every other method reads its result.

## Abilities, levels and the CRUDS bitmask

Vaulter reasons over a single integer. Every grant is reduced to a **CRUDS bitmask**
(`Vaulter\Enums\Access\Permission`), and every ability declares the bits it requires.

```
READ = 1   UPDATE = 2   CREATE = 4   DELETE = 8   SHARE = 16   ALL = 31
```

### Abilities → required bits

`Vaulter\Enums\Access\Ability` is the Drive action vocabulary. `requiredBits()` maps
each ability to exactly the bit(s) that must be in the effective allow-mask:

| Ability | Required bits |
|---|---|
| `View`, `Download`, `Comment` | `READ` |
| `Edit` | `UPDATE` |
| `Create`, `Copy` | `CREATE` |
| `Move` | `UPDATE \| CREATE` (re-parent = update here, create there) |
| `Trash`, `Restore`, `Delete` | `DELETE` |
| `Share` | `SHARE` |
| `Manage` | `ALL` (31) |

An ability is satisfied only when **all** its required bits are present:
`Ability::Edit->satisfiedBy($bits)` is `($bits & UPDATE) === UPDATE`.

### Grant levels → bitmask

A grant row may store a ranked **level** (`Vaulter\Enums\Access\GrantLevel`) instead of
raw bits. `GrantLevel::bits()` normalises a level to its bitmask so the engine always
reasons in bits:

| Level | Rank | Bits |
|---|---|---|
| `Reader` | 1 | `READ` |
| `Commenter` | 2 | `READ` (comment is a view-side capability) |
| `Writer` | 3 | `READ \| UPDATE \| CREATE` |
| `Organizer` | 4 | `READ \| UPDATE \| CREATE \| DELETE` |
| `Owner` | 5 | `ALL` (adds `SHARE` / management) |

A higher rank implies every lower one. A grant row may carry **both** a level and
extra `permissions` bits — they are OR-ed, so an `Organizer` grant plus an extra
`SHARE` bit confers both.

::: tip No orphan delete action
There is no standalone stringly-typed "delete" level or action. Permanent delete folds
into the `DELETE` bit (held by `Organizer`/`Owner`), so `Trash`, `Restore` and `Delete`
all require the same `DELETE` bit.
:::

## The algorithm

`effectiveGrants()` runs the canonical algorithm in five steps. It is implemented
exactly as described here — there is no hidden behaviour.

```
1. Host override (super-admin) — absolute, both directions.
2. Walk ancestors nearest-first, BOUNDED to the storage root, collecting
   direct + scope=subtree grants for the actor's subject-set;
   STOP at the first ancestor with inherit_grants = false.
3. aclAllow = max(allow bits/levels); deniedBits = OR of deny bits.
   A NEARER explicit allow pierces a FARTHER inherited deny.
4. granted = max(aclAllow, roleAllow), where roleAllow comes from the driver.
5. FINAL VETO: if deniedBits covers the requested ability → DENY,
   regardless of any role grant.
```

### Step 1 — host override

The resolver first asks the active `PermissionDriver::override($actor, $scope)`. A
super-admin / `Gate::before`-style override short-circuits the whole walk:

- `Effect::Allow` → `GrantSet::superAllowed()` (full access, both directions);
- `Effect::Deny` → `GrantSet::superDenied()` (no access, both directions);
- `null` → no override; continue to the ACL walk.

The override is **absolute** — it is not affected by any ACL row.

### Step 2 — the bounded ancestor walk

The driver expands the actor into a **subject-set** via `subjectsFor($actor)` (the user
itself plus any host roles/teams). The resolver then walks the node's ancestor chain
**nearest-first** — the node, its parent, … up to the storage root — collecting the
live grants addressed to that subject-set.

Two rules decide whether a grant *applies* at a given node:

- a grant **on the node itself** applies directly, at any scope;
- a grant on an **ancestor** applies only when its scope is `subtree`
  (`GrantScope::inheritsDownward()`).

The walk is **bounded to the storage**: it never crosses `storage_id`, so a decision
can never escape its workspace. Expiry is enforced read-time in the grant query — an
expired row never reaches the resolver, and there is no expiry cron.

#### The inherit_grants cut-off

Each node carries a boolean `inherit_grants`. When the walk consumes an ancestor whose
`inherit_grants = false`, that ancestor's **own** grants still count, but **nothing
above it does** — the walk stops there. This is the inheritance cut-off: a node can be
sealed off so it ignores grants set higher in the tree.

::: warning A deny on a sealed node is an unbreakable wall
Because the walk stops at an `inherit_grants = false` node, a `deny` placed on that
node sits at the farthest reachable depth — no farther allow exists to pierce it. It is
a permanent veto for the subtree below the cut-off.
:::

### Step 3 — the deny-veto fold (explicit beats inherited)

The walk buckets allow-bits and deny-bits **per depth** (nearest = depth 0). The fold
then applies one rule:

> A `deny` at depth *d* is final **except** for the bits allowed at a *strictly nearer*
> depth (`< d`). A same-depth allow does **not** pierce a same-depth deny.

Consequences:

- a **nearer explicit allow** pierces a **farther inherited deny** (you can re-open
  access closer to the node);
- an `allow` and a `deny` on the **same node** ⇒ the **deny wins** (a same-node deny is
  an absolute veto — explicit-beats-inherited applies across depths, never within one).

This is why the resolver cannot fold an unordered grant set in a single pass: a
same-depth allow seen before a same-depth deny must not swallow it. Allow/deny bits are
bucketed per depth, then folded nearest-to-farthest, masking a deny only with bits
allowed strictly nearer.

### Step 4 — fold in the role lane

For each subject the driver's `resolve($subject, $actor, $scope)` may return a
`Decision` (a level + allow + bits). An allow `Decision` is OR-ed into the allow-mask
and its level folded with `max()`:

```
allowedBits = aclAllowBits | roleAllowBits
level       = max(aclLevel, roleLevel)
```

The role lane is folded **before** the deny veto, so it can **raise** access but can
**never resurrect a denied bit**. The `AccessScope` handed to the driver is node-blind: it
carries the panel + workspace coordinates and the node owner, never a `Node`.

### Step 5 — the final veto

The veto lives in `GrantSet::allows(Ability $ability)`:

```php
// Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\GrantSet
public function allows(Ability $ability): bool
{
    if ($this->superDeny) return false;   // override deny wins over everything
    if ($this->superAllow) return true;   // override allow wins over everything

    $required = $ability->requiredBits();

    // Any required bit landing in the deny-mask kills the ability.
    if (($this->deniedBits & $required) !== 0) {
        return false;
    }

    return ($this->allowedBits & $required) === $required;
}
```

A required bit in the deny-mask kills the ability **regardless of the allow-mask** — so
a host-role grant from step 4 can never override an ACL deny.

## The GrantSet

`effectiveGrants()` returns a `Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\GrantSet` — a final readonly
value object carrying the folded decision:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `allowedBits` | the union of every applying allow (ACL + role) |
| `deniedBits` | the OR of every applying deny |
| `level` | the effective `GrantLevel` (max of ACL + role), or `null` |
| `superAllow` / `superDeny` | a host override short-circuit |

It answers `allows(Ability)` with the deny-veto baked in (above). Static constructors:
`GrantSet::none()` (no access), `GrantSet::superAllowed()`, `GrantSet::superDenied()`.

## Ability flags for the UI

The resolver computes a flat ability map so the front-end renders only the actions an
actor may perform — no permission logic duplicated in JavaScript, no extra round-trips.

`NodeResource` fills its `abilities` object via
`Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\NodeAbilities::for($actor, $node, $resolver)`, which calls
`abilitiesFor()`. When there is no acting user, **every flag is false** (the client
shows a read-only shell rather than mis-advertising actions).

```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "01J...",
    "name": "Q3 Proposal",
    "abilities": {
      "view": true, "download": true, "comment": true, "edit": true,
      "create": true, "move": false, "copy": true, "trash": false,
      "restore": false, "share": false, "manage": false, "delete": false
    }
  }
}
```

On the client, every node resource ships its resolved `abilities` map — bind your UI directly
against those flags (a missing ability is falsy):

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { computed } from 'vue'
import type { Node } from '@vaulter/vue'

const props = defineProps<{ node: Node }>()
const canEdit = computed(() => props.node.abilities?.edit ?? false)
const canManage = computed(() => props.node.abilities?.manage ?? false)
</script>
```

## Create gate (no node yet)

Folder creation and uploads have no existing node to resolve against, so they route
through `canCreateInWorkspace($actor, $storage)`, which delegates straight to the
driver's `canCreateInWorkspace($actor, $workspaceType, $workspaceId)` lane. See
[Permission Drivers](./permission-drivers) for how each driver answers it.

## Access-aware listings

The per-action gate above answers *"may this actor do X to this node?"* exactly. Drive
**listings** (the folder index, search, trash, and the Filament table) ask a different,
cheaper question — *"which nodes should this actor even see?"* — and answer it with a
**candidate set**, not the exact algorithm. The distinction matters, so be precise about
what each guarantees.

### Exact visibility

Children, search, trash, shared nodes, folder `show` children and Filament table rows
are filtered through `AccessResolver::evaluateMany()` for every permission driver.
Only nodes with effective `View` are returned. Explicit deny and `inherit_grants`
cut-offs apply before names, sizes or MIME types are exposed. The same batch result
fills each listing item's `abilities`, avoiding a separate ancestor walk per resource.

`evaluateMany()` preserves the rules of `effectiveGrants()`: a nearer allow can pierce
a farther deny; a same-node deny vetoes its allow and the host role lane. Absolute
host overrides retain their existing behavior. Parent `item` grants never inherit.

SQL grant narrowing in `constrainToAccessible()` remains a candidate prefilter for
grant-authoritative drivers. Its result needs exact ACL evaluation before display.
The REST listings scan candidates directly; Filament applies the exact batch filter
to the fetched page and uses simple pagination without totals.

### Cursor and scan budget

REST pages carry `meta.next_cursor`, `prev_cursor` (null), `per_page`, `path` and
`scanned`; they do not carry `total` or numbered page links. A cursor records the
last **inspected** candidate, including denied candidates, and is signed with the
application key. It is bound to the storage, listing kind, parent or search term and
ordering. An invalid signature or mismatched query returns 422 `validation_failed`
with `errors.cursor`; restart that listing without a cursor.

`vaulter.listing.scan_budget` defaults to 1000 candidates per request. A page can be
short or empty while `next_cursor` remains non-null. Follow that cursor until null
to reach later visible nodes. Changing `per_page` does not change the cursor's scope.

## "Shared with me"

`sharedNodeIds()` collects candidates with a live direct allow-grant across storages.
The endpoint scans those candidates in `name, id` order and uses `evaluateMany()` to
apply the same exact visibility rules as other listings.

### The `GET /shared` endpoint

The cross-storage "shared with me" listing is exposed at the top level of the Drive prefix
(default `api/vaulter`) — **not** under a `{storage}`, because the subject index is not
storage-bound:

```
GET {prefix}/shared        # e.g. GET /api/vaulter/shared
```

| Property | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| **Gating** | Registered only when the **`grants`** feature is on. |
| **Auth** | An unauthenticated request gets an **empty** page (never an error). |
| **Exactness** | Each candidate is evaluated through the batch ACL algorithm; an effective deny excludes it. |
| **Pagination** | A signed cursor envelope (`meta.next_cursor`, `per_page`, `scanned`) without `total`; follow the cursor even after an empty page. |
| **Payload** | `NodeResource` items with the owning `storage` eager-loaded (the only cross-storage context the payload carries; the breadcrumb is attached only on `show`). |

On the client, `@vaulter/vue` ships [`useSharedNodes`](./vue) and `VaulterSharedWithMe`
over this endpoint.

## Fail-loud: the null driver

The default driver is `database` — a fully standalone lane with zero host dependency.
For local boot-up there is also an **open** driver, `Vaulter\Testing\NullPermissionDriver`,
which grants every actor full access via an absolute `Allow` override.

The `PermissionDriverManager` rejects the null driver **in production**:

```php
// Vaulter\Access\PermissionDriverManager::driver()
if (is_a($class, NullPermissionDriver::class, allow_string: true) && $this->isProduction) {
    throw MissingPermissionDriverException::nullDriverInProduction($key);
}
```

`isProduction` is wired from `$app->environment('production')`. The exception message
is explicit:

> The open null host-role driver is forbidden in production. Why: it grants every actor
> full access; running it in prod would expose every node. Fix: set
> `config('vaulter.drivers.permission')` to a real driver (`database`/`gate`/`spatie`/
> `azgard`) or bind your own `PermissionDriver`.

::: danger Never ship the null driver
`null` is selectable only outside production and exists purely so a consumer can boot
and exercise Vaulter without wiring a real role system. A missing or `null` driver can
**never** silently open a production install — it fails loud at resolve time.
:::

The `azgard` key requires `composer require axioma-studio/vaulter-azgard`.
Its provider registers the driver and real guard adapter; bridge settings live under
`vaulter-azgard.*`, and the user model must implement `AzgardBackedUser`.

An **unknown** driver key fails the same way, via
`MissingPermissionDriverException::unknownDriver($key, $known)`, listing the registered
keys.

## See also

- [Permission Drivers](./permission-drivers) — the four `PermissionDriver` lanes and how
  to select/configure each.
- [Grants](./grants) — the per-node `v_node_grants` rows, subjects, effects, scopes,
  expiry, and `GrantNodeAccess`.
- ADR-0002 (authorization delegation) and ADR-0007 (the AzGuard seam).

---
title: Configuration
description: A section-by-section walkthrough of config/vaulter.php — models, table names, id strategy, panels, features, permission drivers, CAS, sharing, uploads, webhooks and collaboration.
outline: deep
---

# Configuration

Publish the config with:

```bash
php artisan vendor:publish --tag=vaulter-config
```

It lands at `config/vaulter.php`. This page walks every section. The config is **cache-safe**
— every swappable binding is a fully-qualified class name (FQCN) string, never a closure — so
`php artisan config:cache` works.

::: tip Looking for a single key?
This page is the narrative walkthrough. For an exhaustive, alphabetical lookup table see the
[config-key reference](/reference/configuration).
:::

## Models

Every Vaulter entity is resolved through this map, so you can point any of them at your own
subclass (to add ULID keys, tenant scoping, audit behaviour, …):

```php
'models' => [
    // Vaulter Drive entities
    'storage'    => \Vaulter\Models\Drive\Drive::class,
    'node'       => \Vaulter\Models\Drive\Node::class,
    'file'       => \Vaulter\Models\Drive\File::class,
    'blob'       => \Vaulter\Models\Cas\Blob::class,
    'grant'      => \Vaulter\Models\Access\NodeGrant::class,
    'node_share' => \Vaulter\Models\Sharing\NodeShare::class,
    // …and file_version, file_version_blob, activity, outbox, webhook_endpoint,
    //    webhook_delivery
],
```

::: info Drive/Documents-owned models
`upload_session` / `upload_part` are owned by `axioma-studio/vaulter-drive`; the
node-attached `node_comment` / `node_document_version` models are owned by
`axioma-studio/vaulter-documents`. Neither ships a default here — each package merges
its own entry via its own `config/vaulter-drive.php` / `config/vaulter-documents.php`
and throws if you resolve it without the package installed. The legacy
document-id-attached models (`document`, `version`, `folder`, `permission`, `comment`,
`share`) were fully excised — see [ADR-0014](/adr/0014-legacy-docvault-strangler).
:::

Vaulter route-binds `{storage}` and `{node}` against whatever you put here, so a host subclass
keeps resolving. See [Multi-tenancy](/guide/multi-tenancy) for the tenant-aware-model pattern.

## Table names & prefix

Every table is named `{table_prefix}{canonical_entity}`. Configure a global prefix:

```php
'table_prefix' => env('VAULTER_TABLE_PREFIX', 'v_'), // v_drives, v_nodes, …
```

`Config::table('drives')` returns `v_drives`. Per-entity `table_names` overrides
are legacy upgrade inputs only: `Config::legacyTable()` reads them while migrations
normalize old physical names. Fresh installs ignore them. All core tables exist
regardless of feature flags; runtime routes and behavior still honor those flags.
Back up before upgrading; see [UPGRADE.md](https://github.com/axiomasoft/vaulter/blob/main/UPGRADE.md).

## Primary key strategy (`ids`)

The id strategy decides the column type of Vaulter primary keys and references.
**Default is `ulid`**. Keys owned by the host use the separate `ids.host_keys` setting (AD25).

```php
'ids' => [
    'default' => env('VAULTER_ID_STRATEGY', 'ulid'), // ulid | uuid7 | bigint
    'host_keys' => env('VAULTER_HOST_KEYS', 'string'), // string | bigint | uuid | ulid
    'strategies' => [
        'bigint' => \Vaulter\Schema\AutoIncrementIds::class,
        'ulid'   => \Vaulter\Schema\UlidIds::class,
        'uuid7'  => \Vaulter\Schema\Uuid7Ids::class,
    ],
],
```

| Strategy | Column | Use when |
|---|---|---|
| `ulid` | 26-char ULID string | **Default.** Sortable, ecosystem-aligned morphs. |
| `uuid7` | native Postgres `uuid` | You want native uuid columns. |
| `bigint` | auto-increment big integer | Legacy / integer-key installs. |

::: warning Legacy `id_type`
The old binary `id_type` (`'id'` / `'ulid'`) key still exists for backward compatibility.
When `ids.default` is set, **it wins**; otherwise the strategy is derived from `id_type`
(`id → bigint`, `ulid → ulid`) so existing installs keep working. New installs should use
`ids.default`. See [ADR-0011](/adr/0011-id-strategy).
:::

### Host keys (`ids.host_keys`)

`string` is the default and emits `varchar(64)`. It accepts UUID users, bigint projects,
ULID actors and bigint Spatie roles together, independently of Vaulter's own ID strategy.
The setting applies to storage owners, grant subjects, comment authors, every `tenant_id`
and actor columns such as `created_by`, `granted_by` and `activity.actor_id`.

| Host-key setting | PostgreSQL | MySQL / MariaDB |
|---|---|---|
| `string` | `varchar(64)` | `varchar(64)` |
| `bigint` | `bigint` | `bigint unsigned` |
| `uuid` | `uuid` | `char(36)` |
| `ulid` | `char(26)` | `char(26)` |

Choose a narrower type only when every host key fits it. Unknown settings throw
`InvalidArgumentException`. Host migrations can use `VaulterSchema::hostKey($table, 'owner_id')`;
`actor()` and `tenant()` also use this setting. `key()`, `reference()` and `morphs()`
continue to use Vaulter's entity-ID strategy. Existing installations run upgrade migration
`2026_10_01_000003_host_key_columns`; see `UPGRADE.md`.

## Storage Panels

A panel is a named config-envelope bound to a host entity over the shared `v_*` schema, with
**zero migrations** by default. List your provider FQCNs here:

```php
'panels' => [
    \App\Vaulter\Profiles\ProjectDriveProfile::class,
],
'default_panel' => \Vaulter\Profiles\DefaultProfile::class,

'migrations' => [
    'path' => null, // legacy key; no longer used by profile scaffolding
],
```

Scaffold one with `php artisan vaulter:make:profile <name>`. Deep dive:
[Storage Panels](/guide/storage-panels).

## Features

Install-wide feature flags (a panel may override any of them per-panel):

```php
'features' => [
    'blobs'             => true,
    'versions'          => true,
    'grants'            => true,
    'activity'          => true,
    'uploads'           => true,
    'share_links'       => false,
    'document_versions' => false, // gates v_node_document_versions + document-node API
    'spreadsheets'      => false, // gates the xlsx UniverHandler
    'public_listing'    => false,
    'reliability'       => true,  // gates the outbox + webhook schema and routes
],
```

A flag gates **both** the relevant schema and the routes/subscribers, so turning one off keeps
the migration and the endpoints out of the app entirely.

## Document handlers

The registry that routes a node to the right format handler (mime → extension → capability →
priority), falling back to download-only. Add a format with one class + one line here:

```php
'handlers' => [
    \Vaulter\Documents\Engines\Handlers\TipTapHandler::class,
    \Vaulter\Handlers\Builtin\PreviewHandler::class,
    \Vaulter\Handlers\Builtin\DownloadOnlyHandler::class,
],
```

See [Document types](/guide/document-handlers) and the [custom-handler recipe](/guide/recipes).

## Authorization drivers

The Drive ACL combines the Vaulter-owned `AccessResolver` with a **swappable** host-role
driver. The default `database` driver is fully standalone (zero host dependency):

```php
'drivers' => [
    'permission' => env('VAULTER_PERMISSION_DRIVER', 'database'),
],

'permission_drivers' => [
    'database' => \Vaulter\Access\Drivers\DatabasePermissionDriver::class,
    'gate'     => \Vaulter\Access\Drivers\GatePermissionDriver::class,
    'spatie'   => \Vaulter\Access\Drivers\SpatiePermissionDriver::class,
    'null'     => \Vaulter\Testing\NullPermissionDriver::class, // non-prod only
],
```

Each non-database driver has its own sub-block mapping a Vaulter grant level / ability to a
host permission name (`vaulter.gate.*`, `vaulter.spatie.*`, `vaulter-azgard.*`). The full per-driver config is in
[Host-role driver](/guide/permission-drivers).

The `axioma-studio/vaulter-azgard` provider registers the `azgard` key. Install it with
`composer require axioma-studio/vaulter-azgard`; its permission map, `panel_id` and
`create_permission` live in `config/vaulter-azgard.php`.

::: danger Null driver
`null` is an open driver selectable **only** outside production. Config validation rejects a
panel bound to it in production — bind a real driver before deploying. If you just need a
working smoke-test default, the standalone `database` driver above is the intended path —
note it is fail-closed (an empty `v_node_grants` means no access, not open access), so seed
grants or pick a driver whose host roles broaden access before assuming "it's not working".
:::

## Content-addressed storage (CAS)

The swappable blob pipeline, the deduplication scope, the GC grace window and the default
disk:

```php
'cas' => [
    'content_store'  => \Vaulter\Media\Cas\Sha256ContentStore::class,
    'storage_driver' => \Vaulter\Media\Cas\FlysystemStorageDriver::class,
    'blob_store'     => \Vaulter\Media\Cas\BlobStore::class,
],

'dedup' => [
    'scope' => env('VAULTER_DEDUP_SCOPE', 'tenant'), // global | tenant | storage
],

'gc' => [
    'grace_hours' => env('VAULTER_GC_GRACE_HOURS', 24), // floored at 1h
],

'storage' => [
    'default_disk' => env('VAULTER_DISK', 'local'),
],
```

::: warning Unversioned bucket
The CAS bucket must be **unversioned** — never use S3 lifecycle/versioning as a blob-deletion
mechanism; that fights the two-phase GC. See [Concepts → Blobs](/guide/storage-and-blobs) and the
[blob-GC recipe](/guide/recipes).
:::

## Sharing

Bearer share-links are a separate public channel; only the `sha256` hash of a token is stored:

```php
'share_token_generator' => \Vaulter\Support\RandomShareTokenGenerator::class,

'share' => [
    'token_generator' => \Vaulter\Support\RandomShareTokenGenerator::class,
    'url_base'        => env('VAULTER_SHARE_URL_BASE', '/share'),
    'prefix_length'   => 8,
],
```

Both channels (bearer node links and legacy document shares) are covered in
[Sharing](/guide/sharing); the two-channel design is [ADR-0013](/adr/0013-two-sharing-channels).

## Trash retention

The window before a trashed node's subtree is permanently purged by
`php artisan vaulter:purge-trash`:

```php
'trash' => [
    'retention_days' => env('VAULTER_TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS', 30),
],
```

## Resumable uploads

Large files upload resumably (tus on any disk; S3-multipart on object stores), then assemble
through the same race-free `BlobStore.commit`:

```php
'uploads' => [
    'max_bytes'          => env('VAULTER_UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES', 5_368_709_120), // 5 GiB
    'chunk_size'         => env('VAULTER_UPLOAD_CHUNK_SIZE', 8_388_608),    // 8 MiB
    'session_ttl_hours'  => env('VAULTER_UPLOAD_SESSION_TTL_HOURS', 24),
    'tus' => ['enabled' => env('VAULTER_UPLOAD_TUS_ENABLED', true)],
],
```

The `uploads` feature flag gates the route group; upload tables always exist. Details in
[Uploads](/guide/uploads).

## Reliability — outbox & webhooks

A transactional outbox stages each domain event, then a relay fans it out to signed webhook
deliveries (at-least-once with backoff + DLQ):

```php
'webhooks' => [
    'timeout'                => 5,
    'max_attempts'           => 5,
    'backoff'                => [10, 30, 60, 300, 1800],
    'disable_after_failures' => 10,
    'signature_header'       => 'X-Vaulter-Signature',
    'timestamp_header'       => 'X-Vaulter-Timestamp',
    'event_header'           => 'X-Vaulter-Event',
    'retention_days'         => 30,  // age past which vaulter:prune-webhooks reclaims SETTLED audit rows
    'manage_ability'         => env('VAULTER_WEBHOOKS_MANAGE_ABILITY', 'vaulter.webhooks.manage'),
],
```

Gated by the `reliability` feature flag. `retention_days` (floored at 0) is the window
`vaulter:prune-webhooks` uses to delete *settled* history — dispatched outbox rows and
terminal (`delivered`/`dead`) deliveries — while never touching in-flight rows. See the
[reliability & webhooks recipe](/guide/recipes).

## Documents & versions

```php
'max_versions'           => 50, // legacy document version cap (0 = unlimited)
'enabled_document_types' => ['richtext', 'table', 'markdown', 'template'],
'max_document_size_kb'   => 5120,

'versions' => [ // node-attached document versions (M4a)
    'max'                       => 50,
    'autosave_debounce_seconds' => 30,
],

'drive' => [ // binary Drive upload policy (kept apart from the document limit)
    'max_upload_kb' => null,  // null = falls back to max_document_size_kb
    'allowed_mime'  => [],    // empty = permissive
],
```

## Export

Map a format to a `DocumentExporter` (add PDF/DOCX/your own):

```php
'exporters' => [
    'html'     => \Vaulter\Export\HtmlExporter::class,
    'markdown' => \Vaulter\Export\MarkdownExporter::class,
],
```

See [Export](/guide/export) and the [custom-export recipe](/guide/recipes).

## Routes

```php
'route_prefix' => env('VAULTER_ROUTE_PREFIX', 'api/vaulter'),
'routes' => [
    'middleware' => [
        'authenticated' => ['api', 'auth:sanctum'],
        'public' => ['api'],
        'hub' => ['api'],
    ],
],
```

Protected routes use the `authenticated` stack. Public `share/{token}*` routes use
`public` plus the token resolver; signed `collab/authenticate` and `collab/store`
callbacks use `hub`. Both public surfaces retain `throttle:vaulter-public`, and
resumable uploads retain `throttle:vaulter-uploads`. Request metrics are appended
once to every stack automatically.

Install Laravel Sanctum for the default `auth:sanctum` guard, or replace that entry
with your application's authentication middleware. The legacy `vaulter.middleware`
key overrides only `authenticated` when non-null, including an explicit empty list;
remove it to enable the new default. `Config::middleware()` is replaced by
`authenticatedMiddleware()`, `publicMiddleware()` and `hubMiddleware()` (AD31).
Resource resolution applies only to Vaulter routes; host `{node}` and `{storage}`
parameters keep their own bindings.

## Collaboration

Yjs is the source of truth; the transport is swappable behind `driver`:

```php
'collaboration' => [
    'driver'         => env('VAULTER_COLLAB_DRIVER', 'hocuspocus'), // hocuspocus
    'channel_prefix' => 'vaulter.documents',
    'webhook_secret' => env('VAULTER_COLLAB_WEBHOOK_SECRET'),
    'drivers' => [
        'hocuspocus' => [
            'class'     => \Vaulter\Documents\Collaboration\HocuspocusCollaborationDriver::class,
            'url'       => env('VAULTER_COLLAB_URL', 'ws://localhost:1234'),
            'app_id'    => env('VAULTER_COLLAB_APP_ID'),
            'secret'    => env('VAULTER_COLLAB_SECRET'),
            'token_ttl' => 3600,
        ],
    ],
],
```

- **`hocuspocus`** — an external Node hub; the client connects with a signed room JWT and the
  hub calls back into the collab webhooks.

Full setup in [Collaboration → overview](/guide/collaboration) and
[server](/guide/collaboration). The decision is [ADR-0001](/adr/0001-collaboration-transport).

## Tenancy

When enabled, migrations add a tenant column. Vaulter does **not** scope by it for you —
supply a tenant-aware model:

```php
'tenant' => [
    'enabled' => env('VAULTER_TENANT_ENABLED', false),
    'column'  => 'tenant_id',
],
```

See [Multi-tenancy](/guide/multi-tenancy).

<<<M FILE docs/guide/filament.md>>>
---
title: Filament admin plugin
description: Manage Vaulter storages, nodes, ACL grants, share links and the activity feed from your existing Filament 5 panel — every mutation routed through the core Actions and gated by the AccessResolver.
outline: deep
---

# Filament admin plugin

`axioma-studio/vaulter-filament` is an optional **Filament 5** plugin that adds Vaulter management
to an existing Filament panel. It registers two families of resources:

- the **Drive / permissions** domain — `Drive`, `Node`, `NodeGrant`, `NodeShare`, `Activity`;
- the **legacy document-centric** surface — `Document`, `Folder`, `Share`.

Every write the panel makes flows through a **core Action** (never a raw Eloquent write), and every
row action / visibility check is gated by the core
[`AccessResolver`](/guide/authorization) — so the panel can never bypass the ACL.

::: tip Related reading
The Drive UI for end users lives in the [Vue package](/guide/vue). The authorization model these
resources respect is covered under [Authorization](/guide/authorization).
:::

## Installation

```bash
composer require axioma-studio/vaulter-filament
```

The plugin ships its provider via Laravel package discovery
(`Vaulter\Filament\VaulterFilamentServiceProvider`). Publish the config when you want to toggle
resources or rename the navigation group:

```bash
php artisan vendor:publish --tag=vaulter-filament-config
```

This writes `config/vaulter-filament.php`.

## Registering the plugin

Add `VaulterPlugin::make()` to your panel provider's `plugins()` array:

```php
use Filament\Panel;
use Vaulter\Filament\VaulterPlugin;

public function panel(Panel $panel): Panel
{
    return $panel
        ->plugins([
            VaulterPlugin::make(),
        ]);
}
```

The plugin id is `vaulter`. If you need the concrete plugin instance back from a panel (for its
config / toggles), use the typed accessor instead of an inline cast:

```php
use Vaulter\Filament\VaulterPlugin;

$plugin = VaulterPlugin::current($panel); // returns the VaulterPlugin
```

`register()` calls `$panel->resources([...])` with only the resources whose config toggle is on
(see [Configuration](#configuration)); the Drive/permissions domain is registered first, then the
legacy document surface.

## Configuration

`config/vaulter-filament.php` has two sections:

```php
return [
    // The Filament navigation group every Vaulter resource is listed under.
    'navigation_group' => 'Vaulter',

    // Toggle which resources the plugin registers. Each defaults to true.
    'resources' => [
        // Drive / permissions domain (M1–M4 core).
        'drive'    => true,
        'node'     => true,
        'grant'    => true,
        'share'    => true,
        'activity' => true,

        // Legacy document-centric surface.
        'document'     => true,
        'folder'       => true,
        'legacy_share' => true,
    ],
];
```

Turn a key to `false` to drop the resource from the panel. The plugin reads each toggle via
`config('vaulter-filament.resources.{key}', true)` — an omitted or non-boolean value is treated as
`true`.

::: tip Drive-only panel
If your host app does not use the legacy document tables, set `document`, `folder` and
`legacy_share` to `false` to show only the Drive/permissions resources.
:::

## How authorization works

Every Drive/permissions resource resolves its acting admin through `Vaulter\Filament\Support\PanelActor`
and asks the core resolver whether that admin holds the required
[`Ability`](/guide/abilities) on the target node:

```php
use Vaulter\Access\AccessResolver;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Ability;
use Vaulter\Filament\Support\PanelActor;

$actor = PanelActor::current(); // the authenticated panel user as an Authorizable, or null

if ($actor !== null && app(AccessResolver::class)->can($actor, Ability::Edit, $node)) {
    // the action is offered / allowed
}
```

`PanelActor` provides two things:

| Method | Returns | Used for |
|--------|---------|----------|
| `PanelActor::current()` | `?Authorizable` | the actor passed to `AccessResolver::can(...)`. `null` → an all-false ability map (a read-only shell) |
| `PanelActor::id()` | `int\|string\|null` | the `actorId` stamped on the core Action (`granted_by` / `trashed_by` …). `null` → attributed as "no actor", never a fabricated id |

A row action is only **visible** when the actor holds its ability, so the panel never advertises an
operation the admin cannot perform.

## Resources

### Drive / permissions domain

#### DriveResource

A **read-mostly** view of the ownable, polymorphic disk roots. Drives are provisioned by
`Vaulter\Drive\DriveProvisioner` (get-or-create on a host entity), never minted from the panel — so this resource
**cannot create or edit** a row (`canCreate()` returns `false`); it lists and inspects.

- **Model**: resolved via `Config::storageModel()` (`Vaulter\Models\Drive\Drive` by default).
- **Table**: name, owner (`owner_type #owner_id`), disk, used bytes, quota (`∞` when unlimited),
  status, created-at. Default sort `created_at desc`.
- **Infolist** (view page): Drive / Owner / Usage sections, with human-formatted byte sizes.
- **Pages**: `index` (list) and `view` (`/{record}`). Classes: `ListDrives` and `ViewDrive`
  under `Vaulter\Filament\Resources\DriveResource\Pages`.

#### NodeResource

The heart of the panel: the unified `folder | file | document | shortcut` node tree. Mutations are
**never** flat-form edits — each row action calls a core Drive Action through the
[`DriveHandle`](/reference/facade):

| Row action | Core path | Gating ability |
|------------|-----------|----------------|
| Rename | `Vaulter::forStorage($node->storage)->rename(...)` | `Ability::Edit` |
| Move | `…->move(...)` (destination picked from the storage's folders; blank = root) | `Ability::Move` |
| Trash | `…->trash(...)` | `Ability::Trash` |
| Restore | `…->restore(...)` (visible only on a trashed node) | `Ability::Restore` |
| Delete permanently | `…->forceDelete(...)` (visible only on a trashed node) | `Ability::Delete` |

```php
// Inside NodeResource: the rename row action's handler.
Vaulter::forStorage($record->storage)->rename(
    node: $record,
    name: $name,
    actorId: PanelActor::id(),
);
```

- **Model**: `Config::nodeModel()` (`Vaulter\Models\Drive\Node`).
- **Table**: a kind icon (`folder` → folder, `file` → document, `document` → document-text,
  `shortcut` → arrow-top-right), name (root rows show `(root)`), kind badge, storage, parent, size,
  trashed-at, created-at.
- **Filters**: kind (`SelectFilter` over `NodeKind` cases), storage, and a `Trashed` ternary
  (`Live only` / `Trashed only`).
- **Query**: drops the `SoftDeletingScope` so soft-**trashed** rows (`trashed_at`) are visible to the
  Trashed filter, while hard-deleted (`deleted_at`) rows stay hidden.
- **Create**: disabled — folders/files are created through the Drive Actions, not a resource form.
- **Pages**: `index` only.

#### NodeGrantResource

List, create and revoke the per-node ACL grants the resolver folds into effective permissions. A
grant addresses a subject (`subject_type` + `subject_id`) on a node with a **level** + extra **CRUDS
bits**, an **allow|deny** effect, an **item|subtree** scope and an optional expiry.

Both mutations route through core Actions and require `Ability::Share` on the target node:

- **Create** (the list page's `Create grant` header action) →
  `GrantNodeAccessAction` (idempotent upsert on the grant key).
- **Revoke** (row action) → `RevokeNodeAccessAction` (drops every grant a subject holds).

```php
// NodeGrantResource::grantFromData — minting via the core Action.
app(GrantNodeAccessAction::class)->execute(
    node: $node,
    data: new GrantNodeAccessInput(
        subject: new Subject(type: $subjectType, id: $subjectId),
        level: GrantLevel::from($level),     // reader | commenter | editor | manager
        effect: Effect::from($effect),       // allow | deny
        scope: GrantScope::from($scope),     // item | subtree
        permissions: $extraBits,             // 0–31, OR-ed onto the level bits
        expiresAt: $expiresAt,
        grantedBy: PanelActor::id(),
    ),
);
```

- **Model**: `Config::grantModel()` (`Vaulter\Models\Access\NodeGrant`).
- **Table**: node, subject (`type #id`), level badge, effect badge (deny → danger), scope, raw bits
  (hidden by default), expires-at (`Never` when null), created-at. Filters: effect, level.
- **Form fields**: node, subject type (a registered morph alias such as `user` / `role` / `team`),
  subject id, level, effect, scope, extra CRUDS bits (0–31), expires-at.
- **Create**: via the header action only (`canCreate()` is `false`).
- **Pages**: `index` only.

::: warning Subject type is a morph alias
The grant form's `subject_type` expects a **registered morph alias** (`user`, `role`, `team`), not a
fully-qualified class. Register your aliases via `Relation::enforceMorphMap([...])`.
:::

#### NodeShareResource

List, create and revoke **bearer share-links** on a node. The raw token is **never stored and never
shown in the table** — only the non-secret `token_prefix` plus the live/expired/revoked/exhausted
status. The raw token is surfaced **exactly once**, at mint time, via a persistent notification.

- **Create** (the list page's `Create share link` header action) → `CreateShareLinkAction`
  (mints + hashes the token; the raw value is shown once).
- **Revoke** (row action) → `RevokeShareLinkAction` (stamps `revoked_at`; idempotent).

Both require `Ability::Share` on the node.

```php
$minted = app(CreateShareLinkAction::class)->execute(
    node: $node,
    data: new ShareLinkInput(
        permissions: $bits > 0 ? $bits : Permission::Read->value, // defaults to READ (1)
        level: GrantLevel::from($level),
        scope: GrantScope::from($scope),   // item | subtree
        password: $password,
        requireLogin: $requireLogin,
        allowDiscovery: $allowDiscovery,
        expiresAt: $expiresAt,
        maxUses: $maxUses,
        grantedBy: PanelActor::id(),
    ),
);

// Shown exactly once — never recoverable from the row afterward:
//   Config::shareUrlBase() . '/' . $minted->token
```

- **Model**: `Config::nodeShareModel()` (`Vaulter\Models\Sharing\NodeShare`).
- **Table**: node, `token_prefix…` badge, level, scope, a computed status badge
  (`Live` / `Revoked` / `Expired` / `Exhausted`), require-login icon, use count (`n / max` when
  capped), expires-at, created-at. Filter: a `Revoked` ternary.
- **Form fields**: node, level, scope, permissions (0–31, defaults to READ), optional password,
  require-login, allow-discovery, max-uses, expires-at.
- **Create**: via the header action only.
- **Pages**: `index` only.

#### ActivityResource

A **read-only** view of the append-only `v_activity` audit log — verb, actor, target and time. The
model is append-only by construction, so the resource is non-creatable, non-editable and
non-deletable (`canCreate`/`canEdit`/`canDelete` all return `false`).

- **Model**: `Config::activityModel()` (`Vaulter\Models\Activity\Activity`).
- **Table**: verb badge, actor (`type #id`), target (`type #id`), storage, when. Filter: verb
  (`SelectFilter` over `EventType` cases).
- **Infolist** (view page): Event / Actor / Target / Request sections (the Request section includes a
  `KeyValueEntry` for `context` plus ip / user-agent / request-id).
- **Pages**: `index` (list) and `view` (`/{record}`). Classes: `ListDrives` and `ViewDrive`
  under `Vaulter\Filament\Resources\DriveResource\Pages`.

### Legacy document-centric surface

These remain for hosts still on the document-centric tables. Each resolves its model through a
`Config::*Model()` helper so a swapped model is still governed.

| Resource | Default model | What it manages |
|----------|---------------|-----------------|
| `DocumentResource` | `Vaulter\Models\Documents\Document` | searchable/sortable documents (title, type, workspace), a trashed filter, an edit form and delete / restore / force-delete actions |
| `FolderResource` | `Vaulter\Models\Documents\DocumentFolder` | the workspace folder tree (list, create, edit, delete) |
| `ShareResource` | `Vaulter\Models\Documents\DocumentShare` | tokenized public document shares — list and **revoke** (read-only; links are minted via the API) |

Toggle them off with the `document`, `folder` and `legacy_share` config keys.

## Model swappability

Every resource resolves its model through a `Vaulter\Support\Config::*Model()` helper
(`storageModel()`, `nodeModel()`, `grantModel()`, `nodeShareModel()`, `activityModel()`, …). If your
host app swaps a Vaulter model for a subclass, the Filament resources keep governing it without any
change.

## Why a separate package

Filament is a heavy, optional dependency. Keeping the admin in its own package means apps that don't
use Filament never pull it in, and its CI runs in isolation against a Filament-compatible Laravel —
so it never constrains the core package's Laravel test matrix.

## See also

- [Vue package](/guide/vue) — the Drive UI for end users.
- [Authorization](/guide/authorization) — the `AccessResolver`, `Ability`, grants and share-links these
  resources respect.
- [Sharing](/guide/sharing) — the share-link channel `NodeShareResource` administers.
