<<<M FILE load/scripts/p8-live-gate.sh>>>
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# P8.7 — one LOAD_RUN_ID, live Prometheus scrape, 50-family matrix, perf-assert, on/off overhead.
# Usage:
#   TIER=S0 ./load/scripts/p8-live-gate.sh gate --profile smoke-perf
#   TIER=S  ./load/scripts/p8-live-gate.sh overhead --baseline plans/archive/VLT-LOAD/findings/P2.8-baseline-S.md
#   python3 load/gates/p8_live_gate.py verify --artifacts plans/archive/VLT-LOAD/artifacts/P8.7
set -euo pipefail

cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
REPO_ROOT="$(cd .. && pwd)"
TIER="${TIER:-S0}"
ENV_FILE="env/${TIER}.env"
COMPOSE=(
    docker compose
    -f docker-compose.load.yml
    -f docker-compose.p87-host.yml
    --env-file "$ENV_FILE"
)
IMAGE_VERSIONS="postgres:16-alpine minio/minio:latest php:8.4-fpm-alpine grafana/k6:0.55.0"
ART="${P8_ARTIFACTS:-$REPO_ROOT/plans/archive/VLT-LOAD/artifacts/P8.7}"
RAW="$ART/raw"
GATE_PY="$REPO_ROOT/load/gates/p8_live_gate.py"
APP_URL="${LOAD_APP_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:${LOAD_APP_PORT:-8080}}"
PROM_URL="${LOAD_PROM_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:9090}"
PM_MAX_CHILDREN="$(awk -F= '/^PM_MAX_CHILDREN=/{print $2}' "$ENV_FILE")"

if [ ! -f "$ENV_FILE" ]; then
    echo "Unknown TIER=${TIER}" >&2
    exit 1
fi

mkdir -p "$ART" "$RAW"
chmod 0777 results 2>/dev/null || true

COMMAND="${1:-}"
shift || true

new_run_id() {
    python3 -c 'import uuid; print(uuid.uuid4())'
}

wait_db_table() {
    table="$1"
    max="${2:-60}"
    waits=0
    until "${COMPOSE[@]}" exec -T postgres sh -c "PGPASSWORD=secret psql -U vaulter -d vaulter_load -tAc \"SELECT to_regclass('public.${table}')\"" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "${table}"; do
        waits=$((waits + 1))
        if [ "$waits" -gt "$max" ]; then
            echo "postgres table ${table} not ready" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
        sleep 1
    done
}

wait_queue_worker() {
    waits=0
    until "${COMPOSE[@]}" exec -T queue-worker sh -c 'tr "\0" " " < /proc/1/cmdline | grep -q "queue:work"'; do
        waits=$((waits + 1))
        if [ "$waits" -gt 90 ]; then
            echo "queue-worker did not reach queue:work" >&2
            "${COMPOSE[@]}" logs --tail=80 queue-worker >&2 || true
            exit 1
        fi
        sleep 2
    done
    wait_db_table v_webhook_deliveries 60
}

compose_up() {
    "${COMPOSE[@]}" up -d --build postgres pgbouncer minio minio-init prometheus redis
    waits=0
    until "${COMPOSE[@]}" exec -T minio mc ready local >/dev/null 2>&1; do
        waits=$((waits + 1))
        if [ "$waits" -gt 30 ]; then
            echo "minio did not become ready" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
        sleep 2
    done
    "${COMPOSE[@]}" exec -T minio mc alias set load http://127.0.0.1:9000 vaulter vaulter-load-secret >/dev/null
    "${COMPOSE[@]}" exec -T minio mc mb --ignore-existing load/vaulter-load >/dev/null
    printf 'ok' | "${COMPOSE[@]}" exec -T minio mc pipe load/vaulter-load/.vaulter-health-sentinel >/dev/null
    "${COMPOSE[@]}" stop queue-worker >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    "${COMPOSE[@]}" up -d --build --no-deps app
    waits=0
    until curl -fsS "${APP_URL}/up" >/dev/null 2>&1; do
        waits=$((waits + 1))
        if [ "$waits" -gt 90 ]; then
            echo "SUT /up did not become ready" >&2
            "${COMPOSE[@]}" logs --tail=80 app postgres minio redis prometheus >&2 || true
            exit 1
        fi
        sleep 2
    done
    wait_db_table v_webhook_deliveries 90
    "${COMPOSE[@]}" up -d --no-deps queue-worker
    wait_queue_worker
}

seed_s0() {
    "${COMPOSE[@]}" stop queue-worker >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    "${COMPOSE[@]}" exec -T app php vendor/bin/testbench load:seed --tier=S0 --fresh
    "${COMPOSE[@]}" up -d --no-deps queue-worker
    wait_queue_worker
}

open_run() {
    curl -fsS -X POST "${APP_URL}/metrics/run/open" \
        -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
        -d "{\"run_id\":\"${LOAD_RUN_ID}\",\"ttl_seconds\":7200}" >"$RAW/open.json"
}

finalize_run() {
    curl -fsS -X POST "${APP_URL}/metrics/run/finalize" \
        -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
        -d "{\"run_id\":\"${LOAD_RUN_ID}\"}" >"$RAW/finalize.json" || true
}

app_artisan() {
    "${COMPOSE[@]}" exec -T -e LOAD_RUN_ID="$LOAD_RUN_ID" app php vendor/bin/testbench "$@"
}

record_trigger() {
    name="$1"
    command="$2"
    zero_ok="${3:-false}"
    python3 - "$RAW/triggers.json" "$name" "$command" "$zero_ok" <<'PY'
import json, sys
from pathlib import Path
path = Path(sys.argv[1])
payload = json.loads(path.read_text()) if path.exists() else {}
payload[sys.argv[2]] = {"ran": True, "command": sys.argv[3], "zero_ok": sys.argv[4] == "true"}
path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
PY
}

run_triggers() {
    python3 -c 'import json,sys; from pathlib import Path; Path(sys.argv[1]).write_text("{}\n")' "$RAW/triggers.json"
    curl -fsS "${APP_URL}/load/metrics-snapshot" >/dev/null || true
    for family in vaulter_upload_session_active vaulter_request_peak_memory_bytes vaulter_outbox_backlog vaulter_broadcast_queue_wait_seconds vaulter_download_stream_active; do
        record_trigger "$family" "GET /load/metrics-snapshot" true
    done

    app_artisan vaulter:relay-outbox --limit=100 || true
    record_trigger vaulter_outbox_stage_duration_seconds "vaulter:relay-outbox" true
    record_trigger vaulter_outbox_relay_duration_seconds "vaulter:relay-outbox" true
    record_trigger vaulter_outbox_relayed_total "vaulter:relay-outbox" true
    record_trigger vaulter_outbox_endpoints_scanned_total "vaulter:relay-outbox" true
    record_trigger vaulter_webhook_queue_wait_seconds "vaulter:relay-outbox" true
    record_trigger vaulter_webhook_delivery_duration_seconds "vaulter:relay-outbox" true
    record_trigger vaulter_webhook_delivered_total "vaulter:relay-outbox" true

    app_artisan vaulter:retry-webhooks || true
    record_trigger vaulter_webhook_retry_tick_seconds "vaulter:retry-webhooks" true
    record_trigger vaulter_webhook_retry_lockset_rows "vaulter:retry-webhooks" true
    record_trigger vaulter_failed_jobs_total "vaulter:retry-webhooks" true

    app_artisan vaulter:sweep-uploads || true
    record_trigger vaulter_sweep_tick_seconds "vaulter:sweep-uploads" true
    record_trigger vaulter_sweep_batch_rows "vaulter:sweep-uploads" true
    record_trigger vaulter_sweep_expired_total "vaulter:sweep-uploads" true
    record_trigger vaulter_sweep_skipped_total "vaulter:sweep-uploads" true
    record_trigger vaulter_command_peak_memory_bytes "vaulter:sweep-uploads" true

    app_artisan vaulter:blobs:gc || true
    record_trigger vaulter_gc_duration_seconds "vaulter:blobs:gc" true
    record_trigger vaulter_gc_batch_rows "vaulter:blobs:gc" true
    record_trigger vaulter_gc_rows_scanned_total "vaulter:blobs:gc" true
    record_trigger vaulter_gc_objects_deleted_total "vaulter:blobs:gc" true

    app_artisan vaulter:purge-trash || true
    record_trigger vaulter_purge_duration_seconds "vaulter:purge-trash" true
    record_trigger vaulter_purge_batch_nodes "vaulter:purge-trash" true
    record_trigger vaulter_purge_nodes_total "vaulter:purge-trash" true

    app_artisan vaulter:prune-webhooks --days=0 || true
    record_trigger vaulter_prune_duration_seconds "vaulter:prune-webhooks" true
    record_trigger vaulter_prune_rows_total "vaulter:prune-webhooks" true

    app_artisan vaulter:blobs:reconcile || true
    record_trigger vaulter_reconcile_duration_seconds "vaulter:blobs:reconcile" true
    record_trigger vaulter_reconcile_objects_total "vaulter:blobs:reconcile" true

    "${COMPOSE[@]}" exec -T postgres sh -c 'apk add --no-cache postgresql-client >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; PGPASSWORD=secret psql -U vaulter -d vaulter_load -c "SELECT 1"' >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    record_trigger vaulter_pg_lock_wait_seconds "collect-postgres-lock-waits.sh" true
    record_trigger vaulter_upload_conflict_total "k6 mixed conflict path" true
    record_trigger vaulter_throttled_total "k6 mixed throttle path" true

    if [ -f k6/dataset.json ] || ls -t seed/out/vlt-load-*.json >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        MANIFEST="$(ls -t seed/out/vlt-load-*.json | head -n1)"
        cp "$MANIFEST" k6/dataset.json
        node "$REPO_ROOT/load/scripts/p8-collab-join.mjs" --backend "$APP_URL" --dataset k6/dataset.json --limit 4 --duration 15s >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    fi
    record_trigger vaulter_collab_room_active "p8-collab-join.mjs" true
}

mark_http_triggers() {
    for family in \
        vaulter_http_request_duration_seconds \
        vaulter_tree_query_duration_seconds \
        vaulter_tree_cte_anchors \
        vaulter_subtree_nodes_touched \
        vaulter_activity_feed_duration_seconds \
        vaulter_activity_write_total \
        vaulter_export_duration_seconds \
        vaulter_collab_session_issued_total \
        vaulter_collab_snapshot_duration_seconds \
        vaulter_upload_bytes_total \
        vaulter_upload_chunk_duration_seconds \
        vaulter_assemble_bytes_total \
        vaulter_assemble_duration_seconds \
        vaulter_download_bytes_total \
        vaulter_download_ttfb_seconds
    do
        record_trigger "$family" "TIER=${TIER} ./load/scripts/run.sh ${PROFILE}" false
    done
}

wait_scrape() {
    sleeps=0
    until curl -fsS "${PROM_URL}/api/v1/targets" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; data=json.load(sys.stdin)["data"]["activeTargets"];
raise SystemExit(0 if any(t.get("labels",{}).get("job")=="vaulter-sut" and t.get("health")=="up" for t in data) else 1)'; do
        sleeps=$((sleeps + 1))
        if [ "$sleeps" -gt 30 ]; then
            echo "Prometheus job vaulter-sut is not up" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
        sleep 2
    done
    sleep 10
}

collect_scrape() {
    curl -fsS "${APP_URL}/metrics?run_id=${LOAD_RUN_ID}" >"$RAW/exposition.prom"
    curl -fsS "${PROM_URL}/api/v1/query" --data-urlencode 'query={job="vaulter-sut"}' >"$RAW/prometheus-query.json"
}

write_manifest() {
    DATASET_ID="$(basename "$(ls -t seed/out/vlt-load-*.json | head -n1)" .json)"
    FINGERPRINT="$( (cat "$ENV_FILE"; printf '%s %s' "$IMAGE_VERSIONS" "$DATASET_ID") | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)"
    python3 - "$RAW/manifest-fields.json" "$LOAD_RUN_ID" "$TIER" "$PROFILE" "$DATASET_ID" "$FINGERPRINT" "$IMAGE_VERSIONS" "$METRICS_ENABLED" <<'PY'
import hashlib, json, sys
from pathlib import Path
run_id, tier, profile, dataset, fingerprint, images, enabled = sys.argv[2:]
Path(sys.argv[1]).write_text(json.dumps({
    "run_id_sha256": hashlib.sha256(run_id.encode()).hexdigest(),
    "tier": tier,
    "profile": profile,
    "dataset_id": dataset,
    "env_fingerprint": fingerprint,
    "image_versions": images,
    "prometheus_job": "vaulter-sut",
    "metrics_enabled": enabled == "true",
    "rejected_attempts": [],
}, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
PY
    python3 "$GATE_PY" manifest --fields "$RAW/manifest-fields.json" --out "$ART/run-manifest.json"
    printf '%s' "$FINGERPRINT"
}

collect_rss() {
    ./scripts/collect-container-stats.sh >"$RAW/container-peak.json"
}

app_anon_rss_bytes() {
    "${COMPOSE[@]}" exec -T app sh -c "grep -E '^anon ' /sys/fs/cgroup/memory.stat 2>/dev/null | head -n1 | awk '{print \$2}'" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r\n ' || echo 0
}

run_gate() {
    PROFILE="${PROFILE:-smoke-perf}"
    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
        case "$1" in
            --profile) PROFILE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            *) echo "unknown gate flag $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
        esac
    done
    METRICS_ENABLED="${VAULTER_LOAD_METRICS_ENABLED:-true}"
    export LOAD_RUN_ID="${LOAD_RUN_ID:-$(new_run_id)}"
    export VAULTER_LOAD_METRICS_ENABLED="$METRICS_ENABLED"
    export TIER
    printf '%s\n' "$LOAD_RUN_ID" >"$RAW/run-id.private"
    chmod 600 "$RAW/run-id.private"
    compose_up
    seed_s0
    open_run
    run_triggers
    mark_http_triggers
    TIER="$TIER" ./scripts/run.sh "$PROFILE" || true
    wait_scrape
    collect_scrape
    collect_rss
    python3 "$GATE_PY" metric-matrix --exposition "$RAW/exposition.prom" --triggers "$RAW/triggers.json" --out "$ART/metric-matrix.json"
    python3 "$GATE_PY" verdicts --summary results/summary.json --prometheus-url "$PROM_URL" --profile "$PROFILE" --pm-max-children "${PM_MAX_CHILDREN:-4}" --out "$RAW/verdicts.json"
    python3 "$GATE_PY" gate-matrix --verdicts "$RAW/verdicts.json" --profile "$PROFILE" --tier "$TIER" --out "$ART/gate-matrix.json"
    write_manifest >/dev/null
    finalize_run
    echo "p8-live-gate gate: artifacts in $ART"
}

restart_overhead_leg() {
    "${COMPOSE[@]}" stop queue-worker >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
    "${COMPOSE[@]}" up -d --no-deps app
    waits=0
    until curl -fsS "${APP_URL}/up" >/dev/null 2>&1; do
        waits=$((waits + 1))
        if [ "$waits" -gt 90 ]; then
            echo "SUT /up did not become ready for overhead leg" >&2
            exit 1
        fi
        sleep 2
    done
    wait_db_table v_webhook_deliveries 90
    "${COMPOSE[@]}" up -d --no-deps queue-worker
    wait_queue_worker
}

measure_pair_leg() {
    label="$1"
    enabled="$2"
    export VAULTER_LOAD_METRICS_ENABLED="$enabled"
    export LOAD_RUN_ID="$(new_run_id)"
    METRICS_ENABLED="$enabled"
    restart_overhead_leg
    if [ "$enabled" = "true" ]; then
        open_run
        run_triggers
        mark_http_triggers
    fi
    TIER="$TIER" ./scripts/run.sh "${PROFILE:-smoke-perf}" || true
    collect_rss
    app_rss="$(app_anon_rss_bytes)"
    DATASET_ID="$(basename "$(ls -t seed/out/vlt-load-*.json | head -n1)" .json)"
    FINGERPRINT="$( (cat "$ENV_FILE"; printf '%s %s' "$IMAGE_VERSIONS" "$DATASET_ID") | sha256sum | cut -c1-16)"
    python3 - "$RAW/${label}.json" "$RAW/container-peak.json" "results/summary.json" "$FINGERPRINT" "$DATASET_ID" "$IMAGE_VERSIONS" "$ENV_FILE" "$app_rss" <<'PY'
import json, sys
from pathlib import Path
out, peak_path, summary_path, fingerprint, dataset, images, env_file, app_rss = sys.argv[1:]
peak = json.loads(Path(peak_path).read_text())
summary = json.loads(Path(summary_path).read_text())
http = summary.get("metrics", {}).get("http_req_duration", {}).get("values", {})
rss_bytes = int(str(app_rss).strip() or 0)
Path(out).write_text(json.dumps({
    "env_fingerprint": fingerprint,
    "dataset_id": dataset,
    "image_versions": images,
    "cpuset": Path(env_file).read_text(),
    "http_p95_ms": float(http.get("p(95)", 0)),
    "app_rss_bytes": rss_bytes,
}, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
PY
    if [ "$enabled" = "true" ]; then
        finalize_run
    fi
}

run_overhead() {
    BASELINE=""
    while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
        case "$1" in
            --baseline) BASELINE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --profile) PROFILE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            *) echo "unknown overhead flag $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
        esac
    done
    PROFILE="${PROFILE:-smoke-perf}"
    if [ -z "$BASELINE" ]; then
        echo "overhead requires --baseline" >&2
        exit 1
    fi
    compose_up
    seed_s0
    measure_pair_leg off false
    measure_pair_leg on true
    python3 "$GATE_PY" overhead --on "$RAW/on.json" --off "$RAW/off.json" --out "$ART/overhead.json"
    echo "p8-live-gate overhead: $ART/overhead.json (baseline $BASELINE)"
}

case "$COMMAND" in
    gate) run_gate "$@" ;;
    overhead) run_overhead "$@" ;;
    verify) python3 "$GATE_PY" verify --artifacts "$ART" ;;
    *)
        echo "Usage: $0 gate|overhead|verify" >&2
        exit 1
        ;;
esac

<<<M FILE packages/azgard/README.md>>>
# Vaulter · AzGuard permission bridge

`axioma-studio/vaulter-azgard` wires the [AzGuard](https://github.com/axiomasoft/azguard-private)
scoped-permission system (and, through it, the CoreX tenant context) into Vaulter's
composite ACL — so a host running AzGuard authorizes Vaulter documents/folders with its
existing roles and permissions.

Vaulter core carries **no** dependency on AzGuard. This package owns the
`Vaulter\Azgard\AzgardPermissionDriver`, the narrow
`Vaulter\Azgard\Contracts\AzgardGuard` seam and its real adapter. The core
`AccessResolver` reaches the bridge through the shared `PermissionDriver` contract;
core remains installable with this package absent.

## How it works

```
Vaulter AccessResolver ─▶ AzgardPermissionDriver ─▶ AzgardGuard (seam)
                                                          │
                                    AzgardGuardAdapter ◀──┘  (this package)
                                                          │
                                    host User (HasAzGuard + HasScopedRoles)
```

- **`AzgardGuardAdapter`** implements the Vaulter seam and delegates to the host's
  AzGuard-backed user, translating the three checks: `hasScopedPermission` (narrowing the
  entity to an Eloquent model), `hasPermissionIn` (the workspace/tenant context lane), and
  `isSuperAdmin` (the AzGuard `*` wildcard).
- **`AzgardPermissionMap`** maps abilities to permission keys through the live
  `Configuration\AzgardConfig` repository.
- **`VaulterAzgardServiceProvider`** registers the `azgard` driver key while preserving
  host overrides and binds the seam from the current request's user. A
  request with no AzGuard-backed user gets the deny-all `NullAzgardGuard` — a safe
  pass-through, never a fatal.

## Install

```bash
composer require axioma-studio/vaulter-azgard
```

Select the driver in `config/vaulter.php`:

```php
'drivers' => ['permission' => 'azgard'],
```

## Host integration (the alignment this package cannot do for you)

1. **Mark your User** as AzGuard-backed for Vaulter — free if it already uses AzGuard:

   ```php
   use AzGuard\Concerns\HasAzGuard;
   use AzGuard\Concerns\HasScopedRoles;
   use Vaulter\Azgard\Contracts\AzgardBackedUser;

   class User extends Authenticatable implements AzgardBackedUser
   {
       use HasAzGuard;      // hasPermission / hasPermissionIn
       use HasScopedRoles;  // hasScopedPermission
   }
   ```

   `AzgardBackedUser` simply composes AzGuard's own public contracts from the 0.3 line —
   `AzGuard\Contracts\HasPermissions` + `HasScopedRoles` — so the `HasAzGuard` +
   `HasScopedRoles` traits already declare every method: no bodies needed, only the
   `implements` clause. The current Composer requirement is
   `axioma-studio/azguard-core: dev-main`; the bridge follows AzGuard's public main branch.

2. **The context lane** (`hasPermissionIn`) resolves through AzGuard's bound `ContextGuard`
   — install `axioma-studio/azguard-context` (or the CoreX tenancy provider) so workspace
   checks are answered rather than falling back to a global check.

3. **Align ids / morphs** so the workspace morph AzGuard receives matches your models:
   `vaulter.ids.default=ulid` + `corex.ids.strategy=Ulid` + `AZ_GUARD_MORPH_TYPE=ulid`, and
   register your workspace/owner types as CoreX morph aliases (`EntityRegistry::register`).

4. **Map abilities → permissions** if your keys differ from the defaults
   (`documents.view`, `documents.update`, `documents.create`, …) via `config('vaulter-azgard.permissions')`.

## Config

`config/vaulter-azgard.php` (publish with `--tag=vaulter-azgard-config`):

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `panel_id` | `null` | AzGuard panel threaded through checks; `null` lets AzGuard resolve it per permission key. |
| `permissions` | `documents.*` ability map | Ability value → permission key, read live by `AzgardPermissionMap`. |
| `create_permission` | `documents.create` | Workspace creation permission; override through `VAULTER_AZGARD_CREATE_PERMISSION`. |

Super-admin is AzGuard's own first-class `isSuperAdmin()` (0.2+) — the adapter forwards to
it, so the wildcard convention lives in AzGuard, not here.

## Tests

Three tiers:

- **Driver / shared ACL contract** — the moved driver tests use `Testing\FakeAzgardGuard`
  and retain the parent Writer subtree allow / child deny fixture and its resolver decisions.
- **Adapter / provider / Vaulter-resolver** — the adapter's translation and its integration
  with the **real** Vaulter `AzgardPermissionDriver` across every lane (super-admin
  override, workspace-role → grant-level, create gate), plus the provider binding, driven by
  a controllable user double.
- **`tests/RealAzgard/` — full real-ecosystem e2e** — a real Eloquent AzGuard user with real
  roles / DB-backed **scoped roles** / grant sources, the real **azguard-context**
  `ContextGuard`, and the real adapter → real Vaulter resolver. Proves the adapter's calls
  actually resolve through AzGuard's own engine (super-admin wildcard, workspace-context
  permission → Writer, create gate, scope-precise entity check).

Both use `axioma-studio/azguard-core` and `axioma-studio/azguard-context` from a sibling
`../azguard` checkout through path repositories. The dedicated
[AzGuard workflow](../../.github/workflows/azgard.yml) clones the latest public AzGuard
HEAD without a private repository token and tests Laravel 12 and 13 independently.
Local checks use the existing sibling checkout and installed dependencies.

```bash
composer install && composer test
```

<<<M FILE packages/azgard/src/AzgardGuardAdapter.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Azgard;

use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Vaulter\Azgard\Contracts\AzgardBackedUser;
use Vaulter\Azgard\Contracts\AzgardGuard;

/**
 * The REAL {@see AzgardGuard} adapter (master plan P1 #2 / §6 / H.2 / ADR-0007): it
 * satisfies Vaulter's narrow permission seam by delegating to an AzGuard-backed user
 * ({@see AzgardBackedUser}). This is the production counterpart to core's
 * FakeAzgardGuard — the {@see AzgardPermissionDriver}
 * only ever sees the Vaulter seam, so core stays free of any AzGuard dependency; this
 * package carries the concrete bridge.
 *
 * The three translations:
 *   - hasScopedPermission — narrows the seam's `object $entity` to an Eloquent `Model`
 *     (AzGuard scopes roles to model rows, and keeps that idiomatic type; the narrowing
 *     is the adapter's boundary job); a non-Model entity yields false;
 *   - hasPermissionIn — a straight pass-through to the workspace-context check;
 *   - isSuperAdmin — AzGuard's first-class super-admin check (0.2+), so the wildcard
 *     convention lives in AzGuard, not here.
 *
 * $panelId threads AzGuard's panel context: null lets AzGuard resolve the panel from
 * each permission key's first segment (the default — `documents.view` → the `documents`
 * panel), which matches Vaulter's `documents.*` permission map.
 */
final readonly class AzgardGuardAdapter implements AzgardGuard
{
    public function __construct(
        private AzgardBackedUser $user,
        private ?string $panelId = null,
    ) {}

    public function hasScopedPermission(string $permission, object $entity): bool
    {
        return $entity instanceof Model
            && $this->user->hasScopedPermission($permission, $entity, $this->panelId);
    }

    public function hasPermissionIn(string $contextType, int|string $contextId, string $permission): bool
    {
        return $this->user->hasPermissionIn($contextType, $contextId, $permission, $this->panelId);
    }

    public function isSuperAdmin(): bool
    {
        return $this->user->isSuperAdmin($this->panelId);
    }
}

<<<A FILE packages/azgard/src/AzgardPermissionDriver.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Azgard;

use Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Access\Authorizable;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Container\Container;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\AccessScope;
use Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\Decision;
use Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\Subject;
use Vaulter\Azgard\Contracts\AzgardGuard;
use Vaulter\Contracts\Access\NonEnumeratingPermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Contracts\Access\PermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Ability;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Effect;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\GrantLevel;

/**
 * The AzGuard host-role driver (master plan §6 / H.2 / D6 / ADR-0007). It bridges a
 * host running AzGuard's per-resource, scoped permission model into Vaulter's
 * composite ACL — WITHOUT vaulter-core depending on azguard/corex. Every AzGuard
 * touch goes through the narrow Vaulter-owned {@see AzgardGuard} seam, so PHPStan
 * stays green with the package absent and the driver references NO concrete
 * AzGuard\* / CoreX\* class.
 *
 * THE COMPOSITE RESOLUTION ORDER (master plan §6 — node-ACL → workspace-scoped role
 * → global), and which lane this driver owns:
 *   1. node-ACL (v_node_grants) — owned by the Vaulter AccessResolver, NOT here;
 *   2. workspace-scoped role — THIS driver's lane: resolve() maps the requested
 *      ability → an AzGuard permission and asks hasPermissionIn(workspaceType,
 *      workspaceId, permission). AccessScope is node-blind (it carries no Node), so the
 *      role lane is the WORKSPACE-scoped check; AzGuard's own per-resource
 *      hasScopedPermission lane is reachable through the same seam for a host adapter
 *      that has the node entity, but the contract hands the driver only the workspace
 *      coordinates (H.2 / ADR-0007 node-blind boundary);
 *   3. global — folded inside AzGuard (its SuperAdmin wildcard surfaces as the
 *      override below, and a globally-granted permission satisfies hasPermissionIn).
 * The deny-veto stays the AccessResolver's job: this driver only ever RAISES access
 * (allow / null), it never returns a deny Decision (H.2 step 4 before step 5).
 *
 *   - override(actor, scope) = isSuperAdmin → Effect::Allow, else null (never a deny);
 *   - resolve(subject, actor, scope) = per ranked level (low→high) the level's primary
 *     Ability is mapped to a permission and checked via hasPermissionIn against the
 *     workspace; the HIGHEST allowed level becomes the Decision;
 *   - subjectsFor(actor) = [Subject(actor)] only — AzGuard's per-resource model ANSWERS
 *     checks, it does not enumerate the role-subjects a v_node_grants row could be
 *     addressed to, so the driver contributes just the actor (documented limitation:
 *     a host that grants v_node_grants rows to AzGuard roles should additionally model
 *     those as Subjects, e.g. via a subclass; the guard answers the scoped checks);
 *   - canCreateInWorkspace = hasPermissionIn(type, id, the create permission).
 *
 * The actor's AzgardGuard is obtained leniently: if the actor itself implements the
 * seam (the host's User uses an AzGuard-backed adapter directly — the cleaner path,
 * since the AzGuard methods naturally live on the user), it is used as-is; otherwise
 * a host-bound AzgardGuard is resolved from the container (the adapter path, e.g. a
 * Corex TenantContextGuard-backed binding). When neither is available the lane is a
 * safe pass-through (null / false), never a fatal — so selecting 'azgard' without a
 * real binding degrades gracefully, exactly like the optional spatie lane.
 *
 * REAL-ECOSYSTEM INTEGRATION IS A HOST STEP: this slice proves the driver logic
 * against the {@see AzgardGuard} seam (a FakeAzgardGuard in tests). A production host
 * must bind a real AzgardGuard adapter delegating to AzGuard's hasScopedPermission /
 * Corex ContextGuard hasPermissionIn, AND align ulid morphs
 * (vaulter.ids.default=ulid + corex.ids.strategy=Ulid + AZ_GUARD_MORPH_TYPE=ulid) and
 * register workspace/owner types as Corex morph aliases.
 */
final class AzgardPermissionDriver implements NonEnumeratingPermissionDriver, PermissionDriver
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly Container $container,
        private readonly AzgardPermissionMap $permissions,
    ) {}

    public function resolve(Subject $subject, Authorizable $actor, AccessScope $scope): ?Decision
    {
        $guard = $this->guardFor($actor);

        // The AzGuard check is user-scoped: only evaluate the actor's own Subject so
        // role/team Subjects (which AzGuard does not enumerate) never double-count.
        if ($guard === null || !$this->isActorSubject($subject, $actor)) {
            return null;
        }

        // Node-blind: AccessScope carries the workspace, not a Node, so the role lane is
        // the WORKSPACE-scoped permission check (composite order step 2). A null
        // workspace means there is nothing for AzGuard to scope against.
        if ($scope->workspaceType === null || $scope->workspaceId === null) {
            return null;
        }

        $granted = $this->highestLevelGranted($guard, $scope->workspaceType, $scope->workspaceId);

        if ($granted === null) {
            return null;
        }

        return Decision::allow($granted);
    }

    /**
     * The super-admin override: Effect::Allow when AzGuard's SuperAdmin wildcard is
     * held, else null (never a deny — the deny veto stays the ACL's job, H.2 step 5).
     */
    public function override(Authorizable $actor, AccessScope $scope): ?Effect
    {
        $guard = $this->guardFor($actor);

        if ($guard !== null && $guard->isSuperAdmin()) {
            return Effect::Allow;
        }

        return null;
    }

    /**
     * AzGuard answers per-resource checks rather than enumerating the role-subjects a
     * grant row could target, so the subject-set is the actor itself (documented
     * limitation, master plan §6). A host that addresses v_node_grants rows to AzGuard
     * roles should subclass and append those Subjects; the guard still answers the
     * scoped checks for the actor lane.
     *
     * Because this lane does NOT implement
     * {@see EnumeratesRoleSubjects}, a v_node_grants row
     * addressed to a role/team is inert under it; writing one fails loud
     * (GrantNodeAccessAction warns, and throws outside production — F-P1.2-01).
     *
     * @return list<Subject>
     */
    public function subjectsFor(Authorizable $actor): array
    {
        if (!$actor instanceof Model) {
            return [];
        }

        return [Subject::ofModel($actor)];
    }

    /**
     * May the actor create nodes in the host workspace? Delegates to AzGuard's
     * workspace-scoped check (hasPermissionIn) with the configured create permission —
     * the folder/upload create path has no existing node to resolve against (§6).
     */
    public function canCreateInWorkspace(Authorizable $actor, string $workspaceType, int|string $workspaceId): bool
    {
        $guard = $this->guardFor($actor);

        if ($guard === null) {
            return false;
        }

        return $guard->hasPermissionIn(
            contextType: $workspaceType,
            contextId: $workspaceId,
            permission: $this->permissions->createPermission(),
        );
    }

    /**
     * The highest GrantLevel the workspace-scoped guard grants: each level (low→high)
     * is probed by its primary Ability's mapped permission via hasPermissionIn; the
     * top level that passes is returned. Mirrors the Gate/Spatie lanes' "highest
     * allowed level becomes the Decision" fold, but action-keyed (AzGuard is
     * permission-per-action, so a level is represented by the ability that defines it).
     */
    private function highestLevelGranted(AzgardGuard $guard, string $workspaceType, int|string $workspaceId): ?GrantLevel
    {
        $granted = null;

        foreach ($this->levelProbes() as $levelValue => $ability) {
            $level = GrantLevel::tryFrom($levelValue);
            $permission = $this->permissions->permissionFor($ability);

            if ($level === null || $permission === null) {
                continue;
            }

            if (!$guard->hasPermissionIn(contextType: $workspaceType, contextId: $workspaceId, permission: $permission)) {
                continue;
            }

            $granted = $granted === null ? $level : $granted->max($level);
        }

        return $granted;
    }

    /**
     * The level → defining-ability probe map. Each GrantLevel is gated by the AzGuard
     * permission of the ability that most narrowly defines it: Reader by View,
     * Commenter by Comment, Writer by Edit, Organizer by Delete (it adds the DELETE
     * bit), Owner by Manage (full management).
     *
     * @return array<string, Ability>
     */
    private function levelProbes(): array
    {
        return [
            GrantLevel::Reader->value => Ability::View,
            GrantLevel::Commenter->value => Ability::Comment,
            GrantLevel::Writer->value => Ability::Edit,
            GrantLevel::Organizer->value => Ability::Delete,
            GrantLevel::Owner->value => Ability::Manage,
        ];
    }

    /**
     * Resolve the actor's AzgardGuard: the actor itself when it implements the seam
     * (the cleaner duck-typed path), else a host-bound AzgardGuard from the container,
     * else null (the lane is then a safe pass-through, never a fatal). The container
     * binding lets a host wire an adapter that closes over the resolved actor (e.g. a
     * Corex ContextGuard-backed adapter).
     */
    private function guardFor(Authorizable $actor): ?AzgardGuard
    {
        if ($actor instanceof AzgardGuard) {
            return $actor;
        }

        if (!$this->container->bound(AzgardGuard::class)) {
            return null;
        }

        return $this->container->make(AzgardGuard::class);
    }

    private function isActorSubject(Subject $subject, Authorizable $actor): bool
    {
        if (!$actor instanceof Model) {
            return false;
        }

        return $subject->equals(Subject::ofModel($actor));
    }
}

<<<A FILE packages/azgard/src/AzgardPermissionMap.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Azgard;

use Vaulter\Azgard\Configuration\AzgardConfig;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Ability;

/**
 * Typed accessors over config('vaulter-azgard.*') — the AzGuard host-role lane's
 * Ability→permission map (master plan §6 / H.2). Unlike the Gate/Spatie maps (keyed
 * by GrantLevel), AzGuard is action-centric, so the {@see AzgardPermissionDriver}
 * maps a requested {@see Ability} to an AzGuard permission key (e.g. View →
 * documents.view) and asks the {@see AzgardGuard} that permission.
 * Plain strings — cache-safe, no closures.
 */
final readonly class AzgardPermissionMap
{
    public function __construct(private AzgardConfig $config) {}

    /** @return array<string, string> */
    public function permissionMap(): array
    {
        return $this->config->permissions();
    }

    public function createPermission(): string
    {
        return $this->config->createPermission();
    }

    public function permissionFor(Ability $ability): ?string
    {
        return $this->permissionMap()[$ability->value] ?? null;
    }
}

<<<A FILE packages/azgard/src/Configuration/AzgardConfig.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Azgard\Configuration;

use Illuminate\Contracts\Config\Repository;

final readonly class AzgardConfig
{
    public function __construct(private Repository $config) {}

    public function panelId(): ?string
    {
        $value = $this->config->get('vaulter-azgard.panel_id');

        return is_string($value) && $value !== '' ? $value : null;
    }

    /** @return array<string, string> */
    public function permissions(): array
    {
        $value = $this->config->get('vaulter-azgard.permissions', self::DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS);

        if (!is_array($value)) {
            return self::DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS;
        }

        $map = [];

        foreach ($value as $ability => $permission) {
            if (is_string($ability) && is_string($permission) && $permission !== '') {
                $map[$ability] = $permission;
            }
        }

        return $map === [] ? self::DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS : $map;
    }

    public function createPermission(): string
    {
        $value = $this->config->get('vaulter-azgard.create_permission', 'documents.create');

        return is_string($value) && $value !== '' ? $value : 'documents.create';
    }

    /** @var array<string, string> */
    private const array DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS = [
        'view' => 'documents.view',
        'download' => 'documents.download',
        'comment' => 'documents.comment',
        'edit' => 'documents.update',
        'create' => 'documents.create',
        'move' => 'documents.update',
        'copy' => 'documents.update',
        'trash' => 'documents.delete',
        'delete' => 'documents.delete',
        'restore' => 'documents.delete',
        'share' => 'documents.manage',
        'manage' => 'documents.manage',
    ];
}

<<<A FILE packages/azgard/src/Contracts/AzgardGuard.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Azgard\Contracts;

/**
 * The NARROW Vaulter-owned seam the host's AzGuard-backed actor satisfies (master
 * plan §6 / H.2 / ADR-0007). It exposes EXACTLY the three checks the
 * {@see AzgardPermissionDriver} needs — and nothing of AzGuard's own API — so
 * vaulter-core carries NO hard dependency on azguard/corex and PHPStan stays green
 * with the package ABSENT (no concrete AzGuard\* / CoreX\* references anywhere in
 * the driver path).
 *
 * The host binds a real adapter (delegating to AzGuard's HasAzGuard concern /
 * Corex TenantContextGuard — `hasScopedPermission` / `hasPermissionIn` / the
 * SuperAdmin wildcard) for the resolved actor; tests bind {@see FakeAzgardGuard}.
 * Either way the driver only ever sees this interface, never AzGuard's classes.
 *
 * Method shapes mirror AzGuard 1:1 so a host adapter is a thin pass-through:
 *   - hasScopedPermission($perm, $entity) ≙ AzGuard\Concerns\HasScopedRoles::hasScopedPermission($perm, $entity)
 *   - hasPermissionIn($type, $id, $perm)  ≙ AzGuard\Concerns\HasPermissions::hasPermissionIn($type, $id, $perm)
 *   - isSuperAdmin()                      ≙ the global SuperAdmin wildcard (*) AzGuard grants
 *
 * Morph-alias note (host responsibility): the $contextType / $entity morph types
 * MUST be registered Corex morph aliases (EntityRegistry / ADR-003) aligned with
 * `vaulter.ids.default=ulid` + `corex.ids.strategy=Ulid` + `AZ_GUARD_MORPH_TYPE=ulid`.
 * The driver passes the workspace type string through untouched — it never resolves
 * the alias itself.
 */
interface AzgardGuard
{
    /**
     * Does the actor hold $permission scoped to the given resource $entity (the
     * per-node lane)? Mirrors AzGuard's `hasScopedPermission`: the global SuperAdmin
     * wildcard wins first, then a scoped role on that exact entity. $entity is the
     * host's morph-aligned model (e.g. the Node or its owning host record).
     */
    public function hasScopedPermission(string $permission, object $entity): bool;

    /**
     * Does the actor hold $permission within the host workspace identified by its
     * morph ($contextType, $contextId)? Mirrors AzGuard's `hasPermissionIn` (the
     * Corex TenantContextGuard contextual check) — the workspace-scoped-role lane
     * and the create gate both route through here (there is no Node to resolve
     * against for create).
     */
    public function hasPermissionIn(string $contextType, int|string $contextId, string $permission): bool;

    /**
     * Is the actor a global super-admin? Mirrors AzGuard's SuperAdmin wildcard (*).
     * When true the resolver short-circuits to an absolute allow override (H.2 step 1),
     * before any ACL or workspace walk.
     */
    public function isSuperAdmin(): bool;
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Azgard;

use Vaulter\Azgard\Contracts\AzgardGuard;

/**
 * The deny-all {@see AzgardGuard} the provider binds when the current request has no
 * AzGuard-backed user (an unauthenticated request, or a User that does not implement
 * {@see AzgardBackedUser}). Every probe returns
 * false, so the {@see AzgardPermissionDriver} raises NO
 * access — a SAFE pass-through, never a fatal, exactly as when no guard is bound at all.
 */
final class NullAzgardGuard implements AzgardGuard
{
    public function hasScopedPermission(string $permission, object $entity): bool
    {
        return false;
    }

    public function hasPermissionIn(string $contextType, int|string $contextId, string $permission): bool
    {
        return false;
    }

    public function isSuperAdmin(): bool
    {
        return false;
    }
}

<<<A FILE packages/azgard/src/Testing/FakeAzgardGuard.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Azgard\Testing;

use Vaulter\Azgard\Contracts\AzgardGuard;

/**
 * A configurable in-memory {@see AzgardGuard} so consumers (and this package's own
 * tests) can exercise the {@see AzgardPermissionDriver}
 * WITHOUT installing azguard/corex (master plan §6 / H.5 — the src/Testing seam). It
 * lives in src/Testing/ (not tests/) so hosts can reference it from their own suites.
 *
 * It models the three AzGuard answers as plain data:
 *   - a super-admin flag (the SuperAdmin wildcard);
 *   - a set of (entity-key, permission) scoped grants (the per-resource lane);
 *   - a set of (contextType, contextId, permission) workspace grants (the
 *     hasPermissionIn lane the resolver actually drives, since AccessScope is node-blind).
 *
 * Grant a permission "globally" by passing it to a workspace check the resolver runs;
 * grant SuperAdmin to short-circuit everything.
 */
final class FakeAzgardGuard implements AzgardGuard
{
    /**
     * @param bool                                    $superAdmin      the SuperAdmin wildcard
     * @param list<array{string, string}>             $scopedGrants    [entityKey, permission] pairs for the per-resource lane
     * @param list<array{string, int|string, string}> $workspaceGrants [contextType, contextId, permission] triples
     */
    public function __construct(
        private readonly bool $superAdmin = false,
        private readonly array $scopedGrants = [],
        private readonly array $workspaceGrants = [],
    ) {}

    public function hasScopedPermission(string $permission, object $entity): bool
    {
        if ($this->superAdmin) {
            return true;
        }

        $key = $this->entityKey($entity);

        foreach ($this->scopedGrants as [$grantedEntity, $grantedPermission]) {
            if ($grantedEntity === $key && $grantedPermission === $permission) {
                return true;
            }
        }

        return false;
    }

    public function hasPermissionIn(string $contextType, int|string $contextId, string $permission): bool
    {
        if ($this->superAdmin) {
            return true;
        }

        foreach ($this->workspaceGrants as [$grantedType, $grantedId, $grantedPermission]) {
            if (
                $grantedType === $contextType
                && (string) $grantedId === (string) $contextId
                && $grantedPermission === $permission
            ) {
                return true;
            }
        }

        return false;
    }

    public function isSuperAdmin(): bool
    {
        return $this->superAdmin;
    }

    /**
     * A fresh guard granting one workspace permission (the common "this actor may X in
     * this workspace" fixture), kept terse for table-driven tests.
     */
    public static function grantingWorkspace(string $contextType, int|string $contextId, string $permission): self
    {
        return new self(workspaceGrants: [[$contextType, $contextId, $permission]]);
    }

    /**
     * A fresh super-admin guard (the override fixture).
     */
    public static function superAdmin(): self
    {
        return new self(superAdmin: true);
    }

    /**
     * The stable key a scoped grant is matched on — the host's entity reduced to a
     * morph-style "<class>:<key>" string when it exposes getMorphClass()/getKey(),
     * else its spl object hash. Keeps the per-resource lane checkable without coupling
     * to a concrete model type.
     */
    private function entityKey(object $entity): string
    {
        if (method_exists($entity, 'getMorphClass') && method_exists($entity, 'getKey')) {
            /** @var string $morph */
            $morph = $entity->getMorphClass();
            /** @var int|string|null $key */
            $key = $entity->getKey();

            return $morph.':'.(string) $key;
        }

        return spl_object_hash($entity);
    }
}

<<<M FILE packages/azgard/src/VaulterAzgardServiceProvider.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Azgard;

use Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Factory as AuthFactory;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Container\Container;
use Illuminate\Support\ServiceProvider;
use Vaulter\Azgard\Configuration\AzgardConfig;
use Vaulter\Azgard\Contracts\AzgardBackedUser;
use Vaulter\Azgard\Contracts\AzgardGuard;

/**
 * Wires the AzGuard/Corex permission bridge (master plan P1 #2). It binds the Vaulter
 * {@see AzgardGuard} seam to an {@see AzgardGuardAdapter} built from the CURRENT
 * request's AzGuard-backed user, so that once the host selects the `azgard` permission
 * driver (`config('vaulter.drivers.permission') = 'azgard'`) the driver resolves real
 * AzGuard checks with no further wiring.
 *
 * When the request has no AzGuard-backed user (a guest, or a User that does not
 * implement {@see AzgardBackedUser}) the bound guard is the deny-all
 * {@see NullAzgardGuard} — a safe pass-through that raises no access, never a fatal.
 *
 * The host still owns the ecosystem alignment this bridge cannot do for it: ulid morphs
 * (`vaulter.ids.default=ulid` + `corex.ids.strategy=Ulid` + `AZ_GUARD_MORPH_TYPE=ulid`),
 * registering workspace/owner types as Corex morph aliases, and adding
 * `implements AzgardBackedUser` (satisfied for free by AzGuard's HasAzGuard +
 * HasScopedRoles traits) to its User model.
 */
final class VaulterAzgardServiceProvider extends ServiceProvider
{
    public function register(): void
    {
        $this->mergeConfigFrom(__DIR__.'/../config/vaulter-azgard.php', 'vaulter-azgard');

        if (!$this->app->make('config')->has('vaulter.permission_drivers.azgard')) {
            $this->app->make('config')->set('vaulter.permission_drivers.azgard', AzgardPermissionDriver::class);
        }

        $this->app->bind(AzgardGuard::class, static function (Container $app): AzgardGuard {
            $user = $app->make(AuthFactory::class)->guard()->user();

            if (!$user instanceof AzgardBackedUser) {
                return new NullAzgardGuard;
            }

            return new AzgardGuardAdapter(
                user: $user,
                panelId: $app->make(AzgardConfig::class)->panelId(),
            );
        });
    }

    public function boot(): void
    {
        if ($this->app->runningInConsole()) {
            $this->publishes([
                __DIR__.'/../config/vaulter-azgard.php' => $this->app->configPath('vaulter-azgard.php'),
            ], 'vaulter-azgard-config');
        }
    }
}

<<<A FILE packages/azgard/tests/Access/AccessTestHelpers.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Azgard\Tests\Access;

use Illuminate\Support\Carbon;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Effect;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\GrantLevel;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\GrantScope;
use Vaulter\Enums\Drive\NodeKind;
use Vaulter\Models\Access\NodeGrant;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Drive;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Node;

/**
 * Builders for the M2a ACL tests: a storage with a known tree, a subject user, and
 * a one-liner grant writer. Keeps the table-driven tests focused on the algorithm,
 * not on row plumbing.
 */
final class AccessTestHelpers
{
    /**
     * A fresh storage (and its root node) for a unique host entity.
     */
    public static function storage(): Drive
    {
        static $next = 0;
        $next++;

        $storage = new Drive;
        $storage->forceFill([
            'profile' => 'default',
            'owner_type' => 'project',
            'owner_id' => $next,
            'name' => 'ACL fixture drive',
            'disk' => 'local',
            'used_bytes' => 0,
        ])->save();

        $root = new Node;
        $root->forceFill([
            'drive_id' => $storage->id,
            'parent_id' => null,
            'kind' => NodeKind::Folder,
            'name' => '',
            'size_bytes' => 0,
        ])->save();

        $storage->forceFill(['root_node_id' => $root->id])->save();

        return $storage->refresh();
    }

    /**
     * A persisted test user with a fixed id (the grant subject / actor).
     */
    public static function user(int $id = 1): TestUser
    {
        $user = new TestUser;
        $user->forceFill(['id' => $id]);
        $user->exists = true;

        return $user;
    }

    /**
     * Create a folder node directly under a parent (or the storage root), bypassing
     * the Action so a test can shape an arbitrary tree without name-conflict noise.
     */
    public static function folder(Drive $storage, ?Node $parent, string $name, bool $inheritGrants = true): Node
    {
        $model = config('vaulter.models.node');

        /** @var Node $node */
        $node = new $model;
        $node->forceFill([
            'drive_id' => $storage->id,
            'parent_id' => $parent?->id ?? $storage->root_node_id,
            'kind' => NodeKind::Folder,
            'name' => $name,
            'inherit_grants' => $inheritGrants,
        ])->save();

        return $node->refresh();
    }

    /**
     * Write a grant row directly (the resolver reads these). $subjectId defaults to
     * the canonical test user (id 1).
     */
    public static function grant(
        Node $node,
        GrantLevel $level,
        Effect $effect = Effect::Allow,
        GrantScope $scope = GrantScope::Subtree,
        int $permissions = 0,
        int|string $subjectId = 1,
        ?string $subjectType = null,
        ?Carbon $expiresAt = null,
    ): NodeGrant {
        $subjectType ??= (new TestUser)->getMorphClass();

        $model = config('vaulter.models.grant');

        /** @var NodeGrant $grant */
        $grant = new $model;
        $grant->forceFill([
            'node_id' => $node->id,
            'subject_type' => $subjectType,
            'subject_id' => $subjectId,
            'level' => $level->value,
            'permissions' => $permissions,
            'effect' => $effect->value,
            'scope' => $scope->value,
            'expires_at' => $expiresAt,
        ])->save();

        return $grant->refresh();
    }
}

<<<A FILE packages/azgard/tests/Access/AzgardDriverTest.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use Illuminate\Foundation\Auth\User;
use Vaulter\Access\AccessResolver;
use Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\AccessScope;
use Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\Subject;
use Vaulter\Azgard\AzgardPermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Azgard\AzgardPermissionMap;
use Vaulter\Azgard\Contracts\AzgardGuard;
use Vaulter\Azgard\Testing\FakeAzgardGuard;
use Vaulter\Azgard\Tests\Access\AccessTestHelpers;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Ability;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Effect;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\GrantLevel;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\GrantScope;

/**
 * The AzGuard host-role driver (§6 / H.2 / ADR-0007). It talks ONLY to the Vaulter-
 * owned AzgardGuard seam, so these tests bind a FakeAzgardGuard — NO azguard/corex is
 * installed. Real-ecosystem integration (binding a real AzgardGuard adapter delegating
 * to AzGuard hasScopedPermission / Corex ContextGuard hasPermissionIn, plus ulid morph
 * alignment) is a HOST step; this slice proves the driver logic against the seam.
 *
 * Covered: the Ability→permission map; hasPermissionIn gating the workspace-scoped role
 * lane; hasPermissionIn gating create; the SuperAdmin override; the composite order
 * (a workspace role grant raises access when no node-ACL row exists; a node-ACL deny
 * still vetoes through the AccessResolver, since the driver only RAISES access).
 */
beforeEach(function (): void {
    config()->set('vaulter.drivers.permission', 'azgard');
});

/**
 * Bind a FakeAzgardGuard as the host's AzgardGuard adapter (the container path the
 * driver falls to when the actor itself does not implement the seam).
 */
function bindAzgardGuard(AzgardGuard $guard): void
{
    app()->instance(AzgardGuard::class, $guard);
}

it('maps abilities to AzGuard permissions with the master-plan defaults', function (): void {
    expect(app(AzgardPermissionMap::class)->permissionFor(Ability::View))->toBe('documents.view')
        ->and(app(AzgardPermissionMap::class)->permissionFor(Ability::Download))->toBe('documents.download')
        ->and(app(AzgardPermissionMap::class)->permissionFor(Ability::Comment))->toBe('documents.comment')
        ->and(app(AzgardPermissionMap::class)->permissionFor(Ability::Edit))->toBe('documents.update')
        ->and(app(AzgardPermissionMap::class)->permissionFor(Ability::Create))->toBe('documents.create')
        ->and(app(AzgardPermissionMap::class)->permissionFor(Ability::Move))->toBe('documents.update')
        ->and(app(AzgardPermissionMap::class)->permissionFor(Ability::Copy))->toBe('documents.update')
        ->and(app(AzgardPermissionMap::class)->permissionFor(Ability::Trash))->toBe('documents.delete')
        ->and(app(AzgardPermissionMap::class)->permissionFor(Ability::Delete))->toBe('documents.delete')
        ->and(app(AzgardPermissionMap::class)->permissionFor(Ability::Share))->toBe('documents.manage')
        ->and(app(AzgardPermissionMap::class)->permissionFor(Ability::Manage))->toBe('documents.manage');
});

it('honours a host override of the ability map', function (): void {
    config()->set('vaulter-azgard.permissions', ['edit' => 'host.docs.write']);

    expect(app(AzgardPermissionMap::class)->permissionFor(Ability::Edit))->toBe('host.docs.write');
});

it('grants an absolute override from an AzGuard super-admin', function (): void {
    bindAzgardGuard(FakeAzgardGuard::superAdmin());

    $driver = app(AzgardPermissionDriver::class);
    $scope = new AccessScope(panel: 'default', workspaceType: 'project', workspaceId: 9);

    expect($driver->override(AccessTestHelpers::user(), $scope))->toBe(Effect::Allow);
});

it('defers (no override) when the actor is not a super-admin', function (): void {
    bindAzgardGuard(new FakeAzgardGuard);

    $driver = app(AzgardPermissionDriver::class);
    $scope = new AccessScope(panel: 'default', workspaceType: 'project', workspaceId: 9);

    expect($driver->override(AccessTestHelpers::user(), $scope))->toBeNull();
});

it('lets a super-admin see every node through the AccessResolver', function (): void {
    bindAzgardGuard(FakeAzgardGuard::superAdmin());

    $storage = AccessTestHelpers::storage();
    $folder = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'azgard-super');

    // No ACL grant at all, yet the super override short-circuits to full access.
    expect(app(AccessResolver::class)->can(AccessTestHelpers::user(), Ability::Manage, $folder))->toBeTrue();
});

it('maps a workspace-scoped AzGuard permission to a role-grant level', function (): void {
    // The host grants documents.update in this workspace → the actor gets a Writer
    // decision (Writer is gated by the Edit ability → documents.update).
    bindAzgardGuard(FakeAzgardGuard::grantingWorkspace('project', 1, 'documents.update'));

    $driver = app(AzgardPermissionDriver::class);
    $actor = AccessTestHelpers::user();
    $scope = new AccessScope(panel: 'default', workspaceType: 'project', workspaceId: 1);

    $decision = $driver->resolve(Subject::ofModel($actor), $actor, $scope);

    expect($decision)->not->toBeNull()
        ->and($decision->level)->toBe(GrantLevel::Writer)
        ->and($decision->isAllow())->toBeTrue();
});

it('composite order: a workspace role grant raises access when NO node-ACL row exists', function (): void {
    // documents.view granted in the workspace; there is no v_node_grants row, so the
    // access comes purely from the role lane (composite step 2, no step 1 ACL row).
    $storage = AccessTestHelpers::storage();
    $folder = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'role-only');

    // The guard's workspace grant must match THIS storage's owner morph (the workspace
    // coordinates the AccessScope derives from the storage owner) so hasPermissionIn hits.
    bindAzgardGuard(FakeAzgardGuard::grantingWorkspace($storage->owner_type, $storage->owner_id, 'documents.view'));

    $resolver = app(AccessResolver::class);

    expect($resolver->can(AccessTestHelpers::user(), Ability::View, $folder))->toBeTrue()
        // …but an ability the workspace never granted (edit) stays denied.
        ->and($resolver->can(AccessTestHelpers::user(), Ability::Edit, $folder))->toBeFalse();
});

it('composite order: a node-ACL deny still vetoes a workspace role grant via the AccessResolver', function (): void {
    $storage = AccessTestHelpers::storage();
    $parent = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'parent');
    $child = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, $parent, 'child');

    // The workspace role lane grants edit everywhere in this workspace…
    bindAzgardGuard(FakeAzgardGuard::grantingWorkspace($storage->owner_type, $storage->owner_id, 'documents.update'));

    // …but an explicit node-ACL deny on the child must veto it (H.2 step 5 — the role
    // lane can only RAISE access, never resurrect a denied bit).
    AccessTestHelpers::grant(
        $child,
        GrantLevel::Writer,
        effect: Effect::Deny,
        scope: GrantScope::Item,
    );

    $resolver = app(AccessResolver::class);

    expect($resolver->can(AccessTestHelpers::user(), Ability::Edit, $parent))->toBeTrue()
        ->and($resolver->can(AccessTestHelpers::user(), Ability::Edit, $child))->toBeFalse();
});

it('gates workspace creation through hasPermissionIn with the create permission', function (): void {
    bindAzgardGuard(FakeAzgardGuard::grantingWorkspace('project', 5, 'documents.create'));

    $driver = app(AzgardPermissionDriver::class);
    $actor = AccessTestHelpers::user();

    expect($driver->canCreateInWorkspace($actor, 'project', 5))->toBeTrue()
        ->and($driver->canCreateInWorkspace($actor, 'project', 6))->toBeFalse();
});

it('returns no role decision when the workspace grants nothing (pass-through with a guard)', function (): void {
    bindAzgardGuard(new FakeAzgardGuard);

    $driver = app(AzgardPermissionDriver::class);
    $actor = AccessTestHelpers::user();
    $scope = new AccessScope(panel: 'default', workspaceType: 'project', workspaceId: 1);

    expect($driver->resolve(Subject::ofModel($actor), $actor, $scope))->toBeNull()
        ->and($driver->override($actor, $scope))->toBeNull();
});

it('is a safe pass-through (no fatal) when no AzgardGuard is bound', function (): void {
    app()->offsetUnset(AzgardGuard::class);
    $driver = app(AzgardPermissionDriver::class);
    $actor = AccessTestHelpers::user();
    $scope = new AccessScope(panel: 'default', workspaceType: 'project', workspaceId: 1);

    expect($driver->resolve(Subject::ofModel($actor), $actor, $scope))->toBeNull()
        ->and($driver->override($actor, $scope))->toBeNull()
        ->and($driver->canCreateInWorkspace($actor, 'project', 1))->toBeFalse();
});

it('returns no role decision for a node-blind scope with no workspace coordinates', function (): void {
    bindAzgardGuard(FakeAzgardGuard::grantingWorkspace('project', 1, 'documents.view'));

    $driver = app(AzgardPermissionDriver::class);
    $actor = AccessTestHelpers::user();
    $scope = new AccessScope(panel: 'default'); // no workspaceType/workspaceId

    expect($driver->resolve(Subject::ofModel($actor), $actor, $scope))->toBeNull();
});

it('exposes only the actor in its subject-set (AzGuard enumerates no role subjects)', function (): void {
    $driver = app(AzgardPermissionDriver::class);
    $subjects = $driver->subjectsFor(AccessTestHelpers::user(id: 3));

    expect($subjects)->toHaveCount(1)
        ->and($subjects[0]->id)->toBe(3);
});

it('uses the actor itself as the guard when the actor implements the AzgardGuard seam', function (): void {
    // The cleaner duck-typed path: an actor that IS an AzgardGuard is used directly,
    // with no container binding. A super-admin actor short-circuits the override.
    $actor = new class extends User implements AzgardGuard
    {
        public $timestamps = false;

        protected $guarded = [];

        public function hasScopedPermission(string $permission, object $entity): bool
        {
            return false;
        }

        public function hasPermissionIn(string $contextType, int|string $contextId, string $permission): bool
        {
            return $permission === 'documents.create';
        }

        public function isSuperAdmin(): bool
        {
            return true;
        }
    };
    $actor->forceFill(['id' => 7]);
    $actor->exists = true;

    $driver = app(AzgardPermissionDriver::class);
    $scope = new AccessScope(panel: 'default', workspaceType: 'project', workspaceId: 1);

    expect($driver->override($actor, $scope))->toBe(Effect::Allow)
        ->and($driver->canCreateInWorkspace($actor, 'project', 1))->toBeTrue();
});

<<<A FILE packages/azgard/tests/Access/PermissionDriverContractTest.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Azgard\Tests\Access\Contract;

use Vaulter\Access\AccessResolver;
use Vaulter\Access\Drivers\DatabasePermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Access\PermissionDriverManager;
use Vaulter\Azgard\AzgardPermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Azgard\Contracts\AzgardGuard;
use Vaulter\Azgard\Tests\Access\AccessTestHelpers;
use Vaulter\Contracts\Access\PermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Ability;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Effect;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\GrantLevel;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\GrantScope;

/**
 * The PermissionDriver contract test (master plan §12 / H.2): ANY driver that only
 * contributes the actor to the subject-set and adds no roles/override MUST yield
 * the SAME AccessResolver decision on a shared ACL fixture. This is the stub M2b's
 * Gate/Spatie/bridge drivers reuse — pointing the resolver at each driver over one
 * fixture and asserting identical results.
 *
 * The fixture: a Writer subtree allow on a parent, a deny on a child. Every
 * "pass-through" driver (no override, no extra subjects, no role decision) must
 * agree: parent editable, child denied.
 */
function bindDriver(PermissionDriver $driver): AccessResolver
{
    app()->instance($driver::class, $driver);
    config()->set('vaulter.permission_drivers.contract', $driver::class);
    config()->set('vaulter.drivers.permission', 'contract');
    app()->forgetInstance(PermissionDriverManager::class);
    app()->forgetInstance(AccessResolver::class);

    return app(AccessResolver::class);
}

/**
 * @return array<string, bool>
 */
function decisionsOver(AccessResolver $resolver): array
{
    $actor = AccessTestHelpers::user();
    $storage = AccessTestHelpers::storage();
    $parent = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'parent');
    $child = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, $parent, 'child');

    AccessTestHelpers::grant($parent, GrantLevel::Writer, scope: GrantScope::Subtree);
    AccessTestHelpers::grant(
        $child,
        GrantLevel::Writer,
        effect: Effect::Deny,
        scope: GrantScope::Item,
    );

    return [
        'parent.edit' => $resolver->can($actor, Ability::Edit, $parent),
        'child.view' => $resolver->can($actor, Ability::View, $child),
        'child.edit' => $resolver->can($actor, Ability::Edit, $child),
    ];
}

/**
 * The shared truth the algorithm dictates on the fixture: parent editable, child
 * denied (deny-wins). EVERY pass-through driver must agree.
 */
function sharedFixtureTruth(): array
{
    return [
        'parent.edit' => true,
        'child.view' => false,
        'child.edit' => false,
    ];
}

/**
 * H.2 hardening: the SAME contract harness against EACH real M2b driver in
 * pass-through mode (no super ability/permission granted, no role-mapped abilities
 * granted, no spatie roles). Every driver must contribute only the actor to the
 * subject-set and add no role decision — so the AccessResolver decision is byte-for-
 * byte identical to the database lane on the shared ACL fixture.
 */
it('yields the shared-fixture truth for the moved driver in pass-through', function (): void {
    app()->forgetInstance(AzgardGuard::class);
    app()->offsetUnset(AzgardGuard::class);

    $databaseDecisions = decisionsOver(bindDriver(new DatabasePermissionDriver));
    $bridgeDecisions = decisionsOver(bindDriver(app(AzgardPermissionDriver::class)));

    expect($bridgeDecisions)->toBe($databaseDecisions)
        ->and($bridgeDecisions)->toBe(sharedFixtureTruth());
});

<<<A FILE packages/azgard/tests/ArchTest.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

arch('production source never imports testing helpers (D35)')
    ->expect('Vaulter\Azgard')
    ->not->toUse('Vaulter\Azgard\Testing')
    ->ignoring(['Vaulter\Azgard\Testing', 'Vaulter\Azgard\Tests']);

arch('bridge source depends only on core and itself (P2.4)')
    ->expect('Vaulter\Azgard')
    ->not->toUse([
        'Vaulter\Media',
        'Vaulter\Drive',
        'Vaulter\Documents',
        'Vaulter\Filament',
        'Vaulter\Load',
    ]);

test('every Vaulter source reference belongs to this bridge or core', function (): void {
    $offenders = [];
    $files = new RegexIterator(
        new RecursiveIteratorIterator(new RecursiveDirectoryIterator(__DIR__.'/../src')),
        '/\.php$/',
    );

    foreach ($files as $file) {
        $contents = file_get_contents($file->getPathname());
        expect($contents)->not->toBeFalse();

        foreach (token_get_all($contents) as $token) {
            if (!is_array($token) || !in_array($token[0], [T_NAME_QUALIFIED, T_NAME_FULLY_QUALIFIED], true)) {
                continue;
            }

            $name = ltrim($token[1], '\\');

            if (!str_starts_with($name, 'Vaulter\\') || $name === 'Vaulter\\Azgard' || str_starts_with($name, 'Vaulter\\Azgard\\')) {
                continue;
            }

            $coreFile = dirname(__DIR__, 2).'/core/src/'.str_replace('\\', '/', substr($name, strlen('Vaulter\\'))).'.php';

            if (!is_file($coreFile)) {
                $offenders[] = $file->getPathname().': '.$name;
            }
        }
    }

    expect($offenders)->toBe([]);
});

<<<A FILE packages/azgard/tests/ConfigurationTest.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use Illuminate\Config\Repository;
use Vaulter\Azgard\AzgardPermissionMap;
use Vaulter\Azgard\Configuration\AzgardConfig;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Ability;

it('reads each typed setting and the permission map live from the repository', function (): void {
    $repository = new Repository;
    $config = new AzgardConfig($repository);
    $map = new AzgardPermissionMap($config);

    expect($config->panelId())->toBeNull()
        ->and($map->permissionFor(Ability::Edit))->toBe('documents.update')
        ->and($map->createPermission())->toBe('documents.create');

    $repository->set('vaulter-azgard.panel_id', 'host');
    $repository->set('vaulter-azgard.permissions', ['edit' => 'host.write']);
    $repository->set('vaulter-azgard.create_permission', 'host.create');

    expect($config->panelId())->toBe('host')
        ->and($map->permissionFor(Ability::Edit))->toBe('host.write')
        ->and($map->permissionFor(Ability::View))->toBeNull()
        ->and($map->createPermission())->toBe('host.create');
});

it('filters malformed map entries and falls back for malformed settings', function (): void {
    $repository = new Repository(['vaulter-azgard' => [
        'panel_id' => [],
        'permissions' => ['edit' => 'host.write', 'view' => '', 'manage' => false, 2 => 'invalid'],
        'create_permission' => '',
    ]]);
    $config = new AzgardConfig($repository);

    expect($config->panelId())->toBeNull()
        ->and($config->permissions())->toBe(['edit' => 'host.write'])
        ->and($config->createPermission())->toBe('documents.create');

    $repository->set('vaulter-azgard.permissions', false);
    expect($config->permissions()['view'])->toBe('documents.view');

    $repository->set('vaulter-azgard.permissions', []);
    expect($config->permissions()['restore'])->toBe('documents.delete');
});

<<<M FILE packages/azgard/tests/ProviderBindingTest.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use Illuminate\Foundation\Auth\User;
use Vaulter\Access\Drivers\DatabasePermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Access\PermissionDriverManager;
use Vaulter\Azgard\AzgardGuardAdapter;
use Vaulter\Azgard\AzgardPermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Azgard\Contracts\AzgardGuard;
use Vaulter\Azgard\NullAzgardGuard;
use Vaulter\Azgard\Tests\Stubs\SpyAzgardUser;
use Vaulter\Azgard\VaulterAzgardServiceProvider;

/**
 * The provider resolves the AzgardGuard seam from the CURRENT request's user: an
 * AzGuard-backed user yields a real adapter, anything else the deny-all guard — so the
 * host wires nothing beyond selecting the driver and adding the trait to its User.
 */
it('binds an adapter over the authenticated AzGuard-backed user', function (): void {
    $user = SpyAzgardUser::make()->grantGlobal(['*']);
    $this->actingAs($user);

    $guard = app(AzgardGuard::class);

    expect($guard)->toBeInstanceOf(AzgardGuardAdapter::class)
        // The adapter really wraps THIS user — its super-admin grant surfaces.
        ->and($guard->isSuperAdmin())->toBeTrue();
});

it('binds the deny-all null guard for a guest', function (): void {
    expect(app(AzgardGuard::class))->toBeInstanceOf(NullAzgardGuard::class);
});

it('binds the deny-all null guard for a user that is not AzGuard-backed', function (): void {
    $this->actingAs(new class extends User
    {
        protected $guarded = [];
    });

    expect(app(AzgardGuard::class))->toBeInstanceOf(NullAzgardGuard::class);
});

it('registers its permission driver and keeps a host driver override', function (): void {
    expect(config('vaulter.permission_drivers.azgard'))->toBe(AzgardPermissionDriver::class);

    config()->set('vaulter.permission_drivers.azgard', DatabasePermissionDriver::class);
    (new VaulterAzgardServiceProvider(app()))->register();

    expect(config('vaulter.permission_drivers.azgard'))->toBe(DatabasePermissionDriver::class);
});

it('preserves an explicitly configured null driver key', function (): void {
    config()->set('vaulter.permission_drivers.azgard', null);
    (new VaulterAzgardServiceProvider(app()))->register();

    expect(config('vaulter.permission_drivers.azgard'))->toBeNull();
});

it('keeps its actor-only driver non-enumerating through the core manager', function (): void {
    $manager = app(PermissionDriverManager::class);

    expect($manager->enumeratesRoleSubjects(app(AzgardPermissionDriver::class)))->toBeFalse();
});

<<<M FILE packages/azgard/tests/RealAzgard/RealAzgardIntegrationTest.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use AzGuard\Facades\AzGuard;
use AzGuard\Models\Role;
use AzGuard\Testing\FakeGrantSource;
use Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\AccessScope;
use Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\Subject;
use Vaulter\Azgard\AzgardGuardAdapter;
use Vaulter\Azgard\AzgardPermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Azgard\Contracts\AzgardGuard;
use Vaulter\Azgard\Tests\RealAzgard\Stubs\AzgardUser;
use Vaulter\Azgard\Tests\RealAzgard\Stubs\Roles\DocsViewerRole;
use Vaulter\Azgard\Tests\RealAzgard\Stubs\WorkspaceModel;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Effect;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\GrantLevel;

/**
 * END-TO-END against the REAL AzGuard stack (no doubles): a real Eloquent AzGuard user
 * with real roles / scoped roles / grant sources, the real azguard-context ContextGuard,
 * the real AzgardGuardAdapter and the real Vaulter AzgardPermissionDriver. This is the
 * proof the FakeAzgardGuard unit tests cannot give — that the adapter's calls actually
 * resolve through AzGuard's own engine.
 */
function realUser(int $id = 1): AzgardUser
{
    return AzgardUser::query()->create(['id' => $id, 'name' => 'Ada']);
}

function bindRealAdapter(AzgardUser $user): void
{
    app()->instance(AzgardGuard::class, new AzgardGuardAdapter($user));
}

function driver(): AzgardPermissionDriver
{
    return app(AzgardPermissionDriver::class);
}

/** Register a fake grant source (a REAL GrantSource in AzGuard's pipeline) for this test. */
function registerGrants(callable $configure): void
{
    $fake = new FakeGrantSource;
    $configure($fake);
    app()->instance(FakeGrantSource::class, $fake);
    AzGuard::registerGrantSource(FakeGrantSource::class);
}

it('resolves a real AzGuard super-admin to a Vaulter absolute-allow override', function (): void {
    $user = realUser();
    registerGrants(fn (FakeGrantSource $f) => $f->wildcard());
    bindRealAdapter($user);

    $scope = new AccessScope(panel: 'default', workspaceType: 'project', workspaceId: 7);

    // Real chain: Vaulter override → adapter.isSuperAdmin → AzGuard permissionSet->isWildcard.
    expect($user->isSuperAdmin())->toBeTrue()
        ->and(driver()->override($user, $scope))->toBe(Effect::Allow);
});

it('defers when the real user is not a super-admin', function (): void {
    $user = realUser();
    bindRealAdapter($user);

    $scope = new AccessScope(panel: 'default', workspaceType: 'project', workspaceId: 7);

    expect($user->isSuperAdmin())->toBeFalse()
        ->and(driver()->override($user, $scope))->toBeNull();
});

it('folds a real workspace-context permission into the matching Vaulter grant level', function (): void {
    // A real GrantSource grants documents.update; the real azguard-context ContextGuard
    // answers hasPermissionIn, which the Vaulter driver maps to the Writer level.
    $user = realUser();
    registerGrants(fn (FakeGrantSource $f) => $f->grant('app', 'documents.update'));
    bindRealAdapter($user);

    $scope = new AccessScope(panel: 'default', workspaceType: 'project', workspaceId: 1);
    $decision = driver()->resolve(Subject::ofModel($user), $user, $scope);

    expect($decision)->not->toBeNull()
        ->and($decision->level)->toBe(GrantLevel::Writer)
        ->and($decision->isAllow())->toBeTrue();
});

it('gates real workspace creation through the create permission', function (): void {
    $user = realUser();
    registerGrants(fn (FakeGrantSource $f) => $f->grant('app', 'documents.create'));
    bindRealAdapter($user);

    expect(driver()->canCreateInWorkspace($user, 'project', 5))->toBeTrue();
});

it('yields no decision when the real user holds nothing in the workspace', function (): void {
    $user = realUser();
    bindRealAdapter($user);

    $scope = new AccessScope(panel: 'default', workspaceType: 'project', workspaceId: 1);

    expect(driver()->resolve(Subject::ofModel($user), $user, $scope))->toBeNull()
        ->and(driver()->canCreateInWorkspace($user, 'project', 1))->toBeFalse();
});

it('resolves a real DB-backed scoped role through the adapter (entity lane)', function (): void {
    // A real role attached to a real workspace entity — scope-precise, DB-backed.
    $user = realUser();
    $workspace = WorkspaceModel::query()->create(['id' => 1, 'name' => 'Alpha']);
    $other = WorkspaceModel::query()->create(['id' => 2, 'name' => 'Beta']);

    $role = new Role;
    $role->forceFill(['name' => 'docs-viewer', 'class_name' => DocsViewerRole::class, 'level' => 10])->save();
    $user->assignScopedRole($role, $workspace);

    $adapter = new AzgardGuardAdapter($user);

    expect($adapter->hasScopedPermission('documents.view', $workspace))->toBeTrue()
        // A permission the role does not grant, and the same role on a different entity.
        ->and($adapter->hasScopedPermission('documents.update', $workspace))->toBeFalse()
        ->and($adapter->hasScopedPermission('documents.view', $other))->toBeFalse();
});

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Azgard\Tests;

use Illuminate\Foundation\Application;
use Orchestra\Testbench\TestCase as Orchestra;
use Vaulter\Azgard\VaulterAzgardServiceProvider;
use Vaulter\VaulterServiceProvider;

/**
 * The base case for the bridge suite. It boots vaulter-core (the real
 * AccessResolver lives there) and this package's driver and provider
 * (the AzgardGuard binding), with the AzGuard permission driver selected — so a test
 * exercises the REAL Vaulter authorization path against the REAL adapter, with only the
 * host's User standing in as a controllable {@see AzgardBackedUser}.
 */
abstract class TestCase extends Orchestra
{
    /**
     * @param  Application        $app
     * @return list<class-string>
     */
    protected function getPackageProviders($app): array
    {
        return [
            VaulterServiceProvider::class,
            VaulterAzgardServiceProvider::class,
        ];
    }

    /**
     * @param Application $app
     */
    protected function defineEnvironment($app): void
    {
        $app['config']->set('vaulter.drivers.permission', 'azgard');
    }
}

<<<M FILE packages/azgard/tests/VaulterResolverIntegrationTest.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\AccessScope;
use Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\Subject;
use Vaulter\Azgard\AzgardGuardAdapter;
use Vaulter\Azgard\AzgardPermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Azgard\Contracts\AzgardGuard;
use Vaulter\Azgard\Tests\Stubs\SpyAzgardUser;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Effect;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\GrantLevel;

/**
 * The bridge driving the REAL Vaulter AzgardPermissionDriver: the adapter is bound as
 * the host's AzgardGuard, and the driver's every lane (super-admin override, the
 * workspace-role → GrantLevel fold, the create gate) is exercised end-to-end. Only the
 * leaf user is a controllable double; the adapter and the resolver are production code.
 */
function bindAdapterFor(SpyAzgardUser $user): void
{
    app()->instance(AzgardGuard::class, new AzgardGuardAdapter($user));
}

function azgardDriver(): AzgardPermissionDriver
{
    return app(AzgardPermissionDriver::class);
}

it('grants an absolute override from an AzGuard super-admin (wildcard)', function (): void {
    $user = SpyAzgardUser::make()->grantGlobal(['*']);
    bindAdapterFor($user);

    $scope = new AccessScope(panel: 'default', workspaceType: 'project', workspaceId: 9);

    expect(azgardDriver()->override($user, $scope))->toBe(Effect::Allow);
});

it('defers (no override) for a non super-admin', function (): void {
    $user = SpyAzgardUser::make()->grantGlobal(['documents.view']);
    bindAdapterFor($user);

    $scope = new AccessScope(panel: 'default', workspaceType: 'project', workspaceId: 9);

    expect(azgardDriver()->override($user, $scope))->toBeNull();
});

it('folds a workspace-scoped permission into the matching grant level', function (): void {
    // documents.update is the Writer probe (Edit → documents.update) in the ability map.
    $user = SpyAzgardUser::make()->grantInWorkspace('project', 1, ['documents.update']);
    bindAdapterFor($user);

    $scope = new AccessScope(panel: 'default', workspaceType: 'project', workspaceId: 1);
    $decision = azgardDriver()->resolve(Subject::ofModel($user), $user, $scope);

    expect($decision)->not->toBeNull()
        ->and($decision->level)->toBe(GrantLevel::Writer)
        ->and($decision->isAllow())->toBeTrue();
});

it('yields no decision when the workspace grants nothing', function (): void {
    $user = SpyAzgardUser::make();
    bindAdapterFor($user);

    $scope = new AccessScope(panel: 'default', workspaceType: 'project', workspaceId: 1);

    expect(azgardDriver()->resolve(Subject::ofModel($user), $user, $scope))->toBeNull();
});

it('gates workspace creation through the create permission', function (): void {
    $user = SpyAzgardUser::make()->grantInWorkspace('project', 5, ['documents.create']);
    bindAdapterFor($user);

    expect(azgardDriver()->canCreateInWorkspace($user, 'project', 5))->toBeTrue()
        ->and(azgardDriver()->canCreateInWorkspace($user, 'project', 6))->toBeFalse();
});

it('exposes only the actor in its subject-set', function (): void {
    $user = SpyAzgardUser::make(3);
    bindAdapterFor($user);

    $subjects = azgardDriver()->subjectsFor($user);

    expect($subjects)->toHaveCount(1)
        ->and($subjects[0]->id)->toBe(3);
});
