    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Global feature toggles. A panel may override any of these per-panel; these
    | are the install-wide defaults read by Config::featureEnabled(). Only cheap
    | sync-path flags belong here — infrastructure features are driver bindings.
    */
    'features' => [

        'versions' => true,
        'grants' => true,
        'activity' => true,
        'uploads' => true,
        'share_links' => false,

        // ADR-0014 шаг 1 — gates the v_node_comments schema + the node-comment

        'comments' => false,

        // Documents (M4a). 'document_versions' gates the v_node_document_versions
        // schema + the document-node Actions/HTTP (default off → opt-in).
        // 'spreadsheets' gates the feature-flagged UniverHandler (xlsx editing).

        'spreadsheets' => false,

        // Realtime collaboration (VLT-REMED P3.1 / F-P1.6-01, D13/D20). A SEPARATE
        // opt-in from 'document_versions': 'document_versions' alone gates the

        // already relies on realtime collab MUST flip this to true after upgrading
        // (breaking change, see UPGRADE.md).
        'collaboration' => false,

        'public_listing' => false,
        'reliability' => true,
    ],

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Document handlers — the format-extensibility registry (§4.5 / §7 / H.5)
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | The FileHandlerRegistry resolves the best \Vaulter\Contracts\Handlers\FileHandler
    | for a file by mime → extension → capability → priority, falling back to the
    | DownloadOnlyHandler null-object. List FQCNs here (cache-safe — FQCN only, no
    | closures); a host adds a NEW format with ONE class + an entry here (or a tagged
    | 'vaulter.handlers' binding, or Vaulter::handlers()->register() at runtime) — NO
    | migration, NO core change, NOT gated by any sealed enum (H.5).
    |
    | Preview/DownloadOnly are the core-owned BASELINE (VLT-CANON P0.4/D10, superseding
    | H.5/T5): a drive-only host with no other package installed still resolves a real
    | preview/download descriptor for every leaf node. axioma-studio/vaulter-documents
    | (P2 #5 / ADR-0015, T9) ADDS TipTapHandler (+ UniverHandler when the 'spreadsheets'
    | feature is on) via its own config/vaulter-documents.php merge — it never owns the
    | baseline.
    */
    'handlers' => [
        PreviewHandler::class,
        DownloadOnlyHandler::class,
    ],

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | TipTap content schema — the store-time allow-list seam (D27 / D28)
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Vaulter validates rich-text content against a CLOSED allow-list of node types,
    | mark types and per-type attributes before it is stored (F-P1.11-01/-02): an
    | unknown node, an unlisted attribute or a non-http(s)/mailto URL rejects the whole
    | document. The canon shipped in ValueObjects\Documents\TipTapContent covers exactly
    | what this package offers the editor through #[TiptapExtensions] (StarterKit, Image,
    | Table, Link, CodeBlock).
    |
    | If you mount your OWN Tiptap extensions in the editor, declare their nodes/marks/
    | attributes here — otherwise the content they produce cannot be saved.
    |
    | The seam is ADDITIVE (D28): these keys only ADD to the canon, they never replace
    | it — dropping 'doc'/'text' from the list would silently break every save, and
    | "overriding" the attribute allow-list is a classic way to hand yourself an XSS.
    |
    | Widening the allow-list does NOT switch the XSS barrier off (R-11): EVERY URL-bearing
    | attribute is scheme-checked (http/https/mailto) at save AND when the content is read
    | back into the editor — the ones you add here included, not just 'link.href' and
    | 'image.src'. An attribute is URL-bearing when its name says so ('src', 'href', 'url',
    | 'poster', 'action', 'cite', …) or when you declare it in 'url_attributes' (for a URL
    | living under a name we cannot recognise, e.g. 'location').
    |
    | And whatever the name: an attribute VALUE carrying an executable scheme ('javascript:',
    | 'data:', 'vbscript:') is REJECTED at save and stripped on read (P5.2). Declaring an
    | attribute in 'url_attributes' buys you the full allow-list check (a relative or
    | 'file:' URL is rejected too) — it is not what stands between your editor and an XSS.
    |
    | Example:
    |   'extra_nodes' => ['mention', 'taskList', 'taskItem'],
    |   'extra_marks' => ['highlight'],
    |   'extra_attributes' => ['mention' => ['id', 'label'], 'taskItem' => ['checked']],
    |   'url_attributes' => ['embed' => ['location']],
    */
    'tiptap' => [
        'extra_nodes' => [],
        'extra_marks' => [],
        'extra_attributes' => [],
        'url_attributes' => [],
    ],

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Tenancy
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | When enabled the migrations add a tenant column. Vaulter does not scope
    | by it — supply a tenant-aware model (via 'models') that applies your scope.
    */
    'tenant' => [
        'enabled' => env('VAULTER_TENANT_ENABLED', false),
        'column' => 'tenant_id',
    ],

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Table prefix
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Prefix for every Vaulter table (published migrations and models read it),
    | so the package coexists with host tables and naming conventions.
    */

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Content-addressed blob store (CAS, M1b / H.3)
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | The swappable CAS engine (content_store / storage_driver / blob_store) is
    | OWNED by the axioma-studio/vaulter-media package (P2 #5, D2/D3): its provider
    | merges the concrete-class defaults under this same `vaulter.cas.*` key, so a
    | host keeps reading/overriding config('vaulter.cas.content_store') etc. with
    | no path change. The dedup/gc/storage knobs below stay in core because the
    | v_blobs SCHEMA (core-owned) reads dedup.scope regardless of that package.
    */

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Deduplication scope (D18 / H.3)
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | The boundary the content address (sha256) is unique within:
    |  'global'  — one physical object per sha256 across the whole install.
    |  'tenant'  — unique per (tenant_id, sha256); no cross-tenant existence leak.
    |  'storage' — unique per (storage_id, sha256).
    | This drives BOTH the dedup-UNIQUE index (SchemaBuilder::defineBlobs)
    | and the scope-qualified storage_key "<scope>/ab/cd/<sha256>" (H.3 — a
    | scope-free path would let one scope's GC delete another scope's bytes).
    | dedup_scope ⊆ encryption scope: plaintext-sha256 dedup never crosses an
    | encryption boundary (note for the future envelope-encryption slice).
    */
    'dedup' => [
        'scope' => env('VAULTER_DEDUP_SCOPE', 'tenant'), // global|tenant|storage
    ],

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Blob garbage collection (H.3)
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Two-phase GC grace window. A blob whose ref-count cache reaches zero is
    | tombstoned with delete_after_at = now + grace; only after the grace passes
    | are its bytes swept. The grace must be ≥ the worst-case multipart-commit
    | latency so an in-flight upload can resurrect the blob first. Floored at 1h.
    |
    | orphan_grace_hours is the separate, generally MORE generous window the
    | `vaulter:blobs:reconcile --orphans` disk-walk applies before it treats an
    | object that has NO blob row as a deletable orphan. A commit promotes its bytes
    | BEFORE its row is durable, and a resumable upload may promote then commit much
    | later, so a fresh row-less object is likely a commit-in-progress, NOT garbage.
    | Defaults to the GC grace; floored at 1h.
    */
    'gc' => [
        'grace_hours' => env('VAULTER_GC_GRACE_HOURS', 24),
        'orphan_grace_hours' => env('VAULTER_ORPHAN_GRACE_HOURS', env('VAULTER_GC_GRACE_HOURS', 24)),
    ],

    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------

    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | The default Flysystem disk for the canonical CAS objects when a blob's
    | storage (v_storages.disk) does not pin its own. The CAS bucket must be
    | UNVERSIONED: never use S3 lifecycle/versioning as a blob-deletion mechanism.
    */
    'storage' => [

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Share-link token generator
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | FQCN of a \Vaulter\Contracts\Sharing\ShareTokenGenerator. Swap to mint short,
    | hashed or prefixed tokens (must be unique and fit the token column).
    */
    'share_token_generator' => RandomShareTokenGenerator::class,

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Bearer share links (M2c / §2.7)
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | The SEPARATE public sharing channel — a bearer token granting exactly its
    | own bitmask on its own node-set, evaluated in its own pass intersected with
    | item-safety (tenant/trash/quarantine), NEVER unioned with the identity ACL.
    |
    |  - token_generator: the \Vaulter\Contracts\Sharing\ShareTokenGenerator used to mint
    |    the raw bearer token. Only the sha256 HASH of that token is ever stored
    |    (token_hash), with a short token_prefix kept for owner-side UX lookup.
    |  - url_base: the public base a share URL is built from in NodeShareResource
    |    (the raw token is appended). The token itself is returned to the creator
    |    exactly once; the resource never re-exposes it.
    |  - prefix_length: how many leading characters of the raw token are stored as
    |    the (non-secret) token_prefix.
    |  - default_ttl_hours (P1.2 / F-P1.3-03, S4.1): the expiry a link gets when the
    |    creator supplies none. A share is never minted with a null expires_at
    |    (bearer links must not be immortal by omission); default 72h.
    |  - max_ttl_hours (P1.2 / F-P1.3-03): the ceiling `expires_at` may not exceed,
    |    enforced by StoreShareLinkRequest validation on an EXPLICIT expiry too —
    |    the default only covers the omitted case. Default 720h (30 days).
    */
    'share' => [
        'token_generator' => RandomShareTokenGenerator::class,
        'url_base' => env('VAULTER_SHARE_URL_BASE', '/share'),
        'prefix_length' => 8,
        'default_ttl_hours' => env('VAULTER_SHARE_DEFAULT_TTL_HOURS', 72),
        'max_ttl_hours' => env('VAULTER_SHARE_MAX_TTL_HOURS', 720),
    ],

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Download headers (P1.1 / F-P1.3-04, F-P1.11-03)
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff is always set on a download response.
    | `Content-Type` mirrors the file's declared mime_type ONLY when it is on this
    | closed allow-list; anything else — including active-content types such as
    | text/html or image/svg+xml — is served as application/octet-stream instead,
    | so a stored file can never render inline as HTML/JS on the app's own origin.
    */
    'downloads' => [
        'inline_mime_whitelist' => [
            'image/png',
            'image/jpeg',
            'image/gif',
            'image/webp',
            'application/pdf',
            'text/plain',
        ],
    ],

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Trash purge (D17 / §2.10)
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | The retention window before a trashed node's subtree is permanently
    | force-deleted by `php artisan vaulter:purge-trash` (schedulable). A node
    | whose trashed_at is older than now() - retention_days is purged; its blob
    | edges detach so the bytes become GC-eligible.
    */
    'trash' => [
        'retention_days' => env('VAULTER_TRASH_RETENTION_DAYS', 30),
    ],

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Resumable uploads (D16 / §2.8 / M3a)
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Large files upload resumably (tus.io on ANY disk; S3-multipart on object
    | stores), then the assembled staged bytes go through the SAME race-free
    | BlobStore.commit (H.3 — server recomputes sha256 from the assembled staged
    | file; the client sha256 / S3 ETag is NEVER trusted as the content address).
    |
    |  - max_bytes: the hard ceiling on a session's declared total size (0 = ∞).
    |  - chunk_size: the advertised default chunk size (a HINT; the server accepts any
    |    PATCH/part size up to max_chunk_bytes — the separate hard cap below).
    |  - max_chunk_bytes: the hard ceiling on a SINGLE PATCH/part body — a memory/IO
    |    DoS lever kept distinct from the chunk_size hint. It SHIPS ENABLED (64 MiB =
    |    8x the advertised hint): a request whose Content-Length exceeds it is refused
    |    413 before its body is read, and a body with no declared length is cut off at
    |    the ceiling before a byte is staged. 0 disables the cap — an unbounded single
    |    PATCH is then a memory/IO DoS vector, so only lift it deliberately.
    |  - session_ttl_hours: a session not committed in this window is swept by
    |    `php artisan vaulter:sweep-uploads` (staged temp + S3 multipart reclaimed,
    |    status → expired). PAIR this with an S3 bucket lifecycle rule
    |    `AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload` so an abandoned multipart never lingers as
    |    storage cost — the sweeper aborts in-flight multiparts it KNOWS about; the
    |    lifecycle rule is the backstop for any it does not.
    |  - tus.enabled: gate the tus resumable endpoints (independent of the 'uploads'
    |    schema feature flag).
    |  - max_active_sessions (P1.3 / F-P1.4-09): the cap on how many OPEN
    |    (initiated|uploading) sessions a single actor may hold at once — `initiate()`
    |    refuses a new session past this cap BEFORE staging a byte. 0 disables the
    |    cap (unbounded).
    |
    | The 'uploads' feature flag (features below) gates BOTH the v_upload_sessions /
    | v_upload_parts schema AND the resumable route group.
    */
    'uploads' => [
        'max_bytes' => env('VAULTER_UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES', 5_368_709_120), // 5 GiB
        'chunk_size' => env('VAULTER_UPLOAD_CHUNK_SIZE', 8_388_608), // 8 MiB
        'max_chunk_bytes' => env('VAULTER_UPLOAD_MAX_CHUNK_BYTES', 67_108_864), // 64 MiB (0 = no per-chunk cap)
        'session_ttl_hours' => env('VAULTER_UPLOAD_SESSION_TTL_HOURS', 24),
        'max_active_sessions' => env('VAULTER_UPLOAD_MAX_ACTIVE_SESSIONS', 20),
        'tus' => [
            'enabled' => env('VAULTER_UPLOAD_TUS_ENABLED', true),
        ],

        // F-P1.4-08: the closed allow-list of tus Upload-Metadata / JSON `metadata`
        // keys the server stores; anything outside it is silently dropped (not
        // rejected — one unknown vendor key must not fail the whole upload), and any
        // accepted value is truncated to max_value_length. Unbounded keys/lengths
        // otherwise grow v_upload_sessions.metadata without limit (U4.3/U4.4).
        'metadata' => [
            'allowed_keys' => ['filename', 'filetype', 'name', 'mime_type'],
            'max_value_length' => 512,
        ],
    ],

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Reliability — transactional outbox + webhooks (D14 / §2.11 / M3b)
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Ported from chatom 1:1. A domain event is staged in v_outbox in the same
    | request as the mutation (after-commit subscriber — see OutboxRecorder), then
    | the relay (vaulter:relay-outbox) fans each pending row out into one signed
    | v_webhook_deliveries row per subscribed active endpoint and queues the HTTP
    | POST. At-least-once with exponential backoff + DLQ; consumers DEDUPE on the
    | event_id carried in the payload (the outbox is idempotent by event_id, the
    | delivery may be re-queued).
    |
    |  - timeout: HTTP request timeout (seconds) for a single delivery POST.
    |  - max_attempts: total attempts before a delivery is parked dead (DLQ).
    |  - backoff: per-attempt retry delay (seconds); the tail entry caps further
    |    retries.
    |  - disable_after_failures: consecutive dead deliveries that flip an endpoint's
    |    is_active off (circuit breaker against a permanently broken receiver).
    |  - signature_header / event_header: the HMAC-SHA256 signature + event-name
    |    headers the delivery POST carries; the signature is over the exact JSON
    |    body and a timestamp (timestamp_header) to make it replay-resistant.
    |  - retention_days: the age past which dispatched outbox rows and terminal
    |    deliveries become eligible for pruning.
    |
    | The 'reliability' feature flag (features above) gates BOTH the v_outbox /
    | v_webhook_* schema AND the outbox subscriber + endpoint routes.
    */
    'webhooks' => [
        'timeout' => 5,
        'max_attempts' => 5,
        'backoff' => [10, 30, 60, 300, 1800],
        'disable_after_failures' => 10,
        'signature_header' => 'X-Vaulter-Signature',
        'timestamp_header' => 'X-Vaulter-Timestamp',
        'event_header' => 'X-Vaulter-Event',
        'retention_days' => 30,

        // The visibility-timeout (seconds) a due retry's next_retry_at is bumped
        // forward when a sweep claims it (F-P1.7-05): a concurrent/next sweep won't
        // re-dispatch the same delivery, and a lost job becomes due again after it.
        'retry_claim_seconds' => 60,

        // The Gate ability that gates the webhook-endpoint management surface
        // (register/update/deactivate/delete). The host defines this ability; until
        // it does, an authenticated user is allowed (the route still requires auth) —
        // a host MUST tighten this in production. Set to null to allow any
        // authenticated user explicitly.
        'manage_ability' => env('VAULTER_WEBHOOKS_MANAGE_ABILITY', 'vaulter.webhooks.manage'),

        // Outbound delivery SSRF hardening (D5 / N2 / F-P1.7-01). The endpoint URL is
        // a user-controlled primitive, so the relay resolves it (A + AAAA), refuses any
        // address in a private/loopback/link-local/reserved range, PINS the vetted IP
        // onto the connection (no DNS-rebind window), disables redirects and locks the
        // transport to http(s). A host may swap the guard or re-open a trusted internal
        // range — the default is closed.
        'delivery' => [
            // Swap for a host implementation of Vaulter\Contracts\Webhooks\OutboundUrlGuard.
            'url_guard' => DefaultOutboundUrlGuard::class,

            // Schemes an outbound delivery may dial. Anything else is refused.
            'allowed_schemes' => ['http', 'https'],

            // Ranges a delivery must NOT resolve into. null → the closed default set
            // (loopback, RFC-1918, link-local incl. 169.254.169.254, CGNAT, IPv6
            // ULA/link-local). Set an explicit list to override wholesale.
            'blocked_ip_ranges' => null,

            // Ranges a host EXPLICITLY re-opens for a trusted internal receiver. Empty
            // by default — the guard stays closed until a host opts in.
            'allowed_ip_ranges' => [],

            // NB: there is deliberately no 'follow_redirects' key (VLT-REMED D30 / R-05).
            // Redirects are NEVER followed: the IP pin above covers the original host only,
            // so a receiver answering `302 Location: http://169.254.169.254/…` would send the
            // delivery to the metadata service through a fresh, unguarded DNS resolve. A
            // config flag that turns a security barrier off is a mine, not flexibility.

            // TCP connect timeout (seconds) — a fast fail on an unreachable host.
            'connect_timeout' => 2,

            // Hard ceiling (bytes) on the receiver's response body; delivery needs only
            // the status. 0 disables the check.
            'max_response_bytes' => 65536,
        ],
    ],

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | API routes
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    */
    'route_prefix' => env('VAULTER_ROUTE_PREFIX', 'api/vaulter'),
    // Keep actor authentication separate from bearer shares and signed hub calls.

    'routes' => [

    'enabled_document_types' => ['richtext', 'table', 'markdown', 'template'],
    'max_document_size_kb' => 5120,

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Drive uploads (binary files)
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | The upload policy for the BINARY Drive path (v_files / v_blobs), kept apart
    | from the TipTap document limit above so a file disk and a document editor

    |
    |  - max_upload_kb: hard size ceiling (kilobytes) for an uploaded file,

    |  - allowed_mime: an OPTIONAL mime allowlist. EMPTY = permissive (any mime
    |    accepted, the default). Listing one or more mimes (e.g. 'application/pdf',

    |    no_separators_pattern is the raw (no `regex:` prefix) negated-match pattern
    |    that rejects a name carrying a path separator — the tree is adjacency-based,
    |    a name is a single segment, never a path. Defaults reproduce the pre-P4.5
    |    hardcoded values (255 / `/^[^\/\\]+$/`) — out-of-the-box behaviour does not
    |    change until a host overrides one of these keys (VLT-REMED P4.5, F-P3.1-01).
    */
    'drive' => [

        'allowed_mime' => [],
        'name_rules' => [

    /*

    | (P2 #5 / ADR-0015, T9): core ships no default here — the documents provider
    | merges them via config/vaulter-documents.php. Support\Config::exporters() falls
    | back to [] (no documents installed = no exporters registered).
    */
    'exporters' => [],

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Real-time collaboration (M4 / §7 / ADR-0001)
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Yjs is the SOURCE OF TRUTH (the binary CRDT state stored on a document
    | node's version); TipTap JSON is the derived projection. The transport is
    | swappable behind the driver:
    |
    |   The default collaborative-editing transport uses an external Node hub —
    |                  the Yjs collaboration backend TipTap documents and maintains.
    |                  The client connects to the hub URL with a signed room JWT;
    |                  the hub's onAuthenticate/onStoreDocument call BACK into the
    |                  collab/authenticate + collab/store webhooks below. This is the
    |                  only path with awareness sync + server-debounced persistence
    |                  and a real read-only guarantee on the socket.
    |
    | channel_prefix is the room namespace; a room is ALWAYS prefix.nodeId so a
    | token is bound to exactly one node (no cross-node access).
    |
    | webhook_secret is the shared secret the Node hub presents on the server-to-
    | server webhook endpoints. The driver-level signing secret is both the
    | room-JWT signing key AND the key the webhooks verify a JWT against — a
    | SEPARATE key from webhook_secret by design (C1.2: never reuse a JWT-signing
    | key as a body-integrity key).
    |
    | HARDENING (VLT-REMED P3.2 / F-P1.6-02, N2): every collab/authenticate + collab/
    | store call — whether it identified itself with the secret header OR a JWT —
    | must ALSO carry a valid HMAC-SHA256 signature of "{timestamp}.{rawBody}" keyed
    | by webhook_secret (X-Vaulter-Collab-Timestamp + X-Vaulter-Collab-Signature),
    | the same canonical string {@see \Vaulter\Webhooks\WebhookSigner} already uses
    | for OUTBOUND deliveries. This is an ADDITIONAL barrier on top of the identity
    | check, never a replacement for it — an unsigned call, a stale timestamp
    | (outside webhook_timestamp_tolerance) or a replayed signature is refused even
    | with a perfectly valid secret/JWT. BREAKING: webhook_secret is now REQUIRED for
    | ANY collab webhook call to succeed (JWT-only, no webhook_secret configured, no
    | longer works) — see UPGRADE.md.
    */
    'collaboration' => [
        'driver' => env('VAULTER_COLLAB_DRIVER', 'hocuspocus'),
        'channel_prefix' => 'vaulter.documents',
        'webhook_secret' => env('VAULTER_COLLAB_WEBHOOK_SECRET'),

        // The ± tolerance (seconds) an incoming webhook's X-Vaulter-Collab-Timestamp
        // may drift from now before the call is refused as stale/replayed; also the
        // TTL a seen signature (nonce) is remembered for replay detection.
        'webhook_timestamp_tolerance' => 300,

        'drivers' => [
            'hocuspocus' => [
                'url' => env('VAULTER_COLLAB_URL', 'ws://localhost:1234'),
                'app_id' => env('VAULTER_COLLAB_APP_ID'),
                'secret' => env('VAULTER_COLLAB_SECRET'),
                'token_ttl' => 3600,
            ],
        ],
    ],

    /*
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | Observability (VLT-LOAD P8 / D35)
    |--------------------------------------------------------------------------
    | MetricsRecorder seam: disabled by default (Null). When enabled, `recorder`
    | must be an FQCN implementing Vaulter\Contracts\Observability\MetricsRecorder
    | (typically a host/load adapter). Invalid or missing class falls back to Null.
    */
    'observability' => [
        'enabled' => env('VAULTER_OBSERVABILITY_ENABLED', false),
        'recorder' => env('VAULTER_OBSERVABILITY_RECORDER'),
        'tracing' => [
            'enabled' => env('VAULTER_TRACING_ENABLED', false),
            'recorder' => env('VAULTER_TRACING_RECORDER'),

<<<D FILE packages/core/src/Access/Drivers/AzgardPermissionDriver.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Access\Drivers;

use Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Access\Authorizable;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Container\Container;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\AccessScope;
use Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\Decision;
use Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\Subject;
use Vaulter\Contracts\Access\AzgardGuard;
use Vaulter\Contracts\Access\PermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Ability;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Effect;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\GrantLevel;
use Vaulter\Support\AzgardConfig;

/**
 * The AzGuard host-role driver (master plan §6 / H.2 / D6 / ADR-0007). It bridges a
 * host running AzGuard's per-resource, scoped permission model into Vaulter's
 * composite ACL — WITHOUT vaulter-core depending on azguard/corex. Every AzGuard
 * touch goes through the narrow Vaulter-owned {@see AzgardGuard} seam, so PHPStan
 * stays green with the package absent and the driver references NO concrete
 * AzGuard\* / CoreX\* class.
 *
 * THE COMPOSITE RESOLUTION ORDER (master plan §6 — node-ACL → workspace-scoped role
 * → global), and which lane this driver owns:
 *   1. node-ACL (v_node_grants) — owned by the Vaulter AccessResolver, NOT here;
 *   2. workspace-scoped role — THIS driver's lane: resolve() maps the requested
 *      ability → an AzGuard permission and asks hasPermissionIn(workspaceType,
 *      workspaceId, permission). AccessScope is node-blind (it carries no Node), so the
 *      role lane is the WORKSPACE-scoped check; AzGuard's own per-resource
 *      hasScopedPermission lane is reachable through the same seam for a host adapter
 *      that has the node entity, but the contract hands the driver only the workspace
 *      coordinates (H.2 / ADR-0007 node-blind boundary);
 *   3. global — folded inside AzGuard (its SuperAdmin wildcard surfaces as the
 *      override below, and a globally-granted permission satisfies hasPermissionIn).
 * The deny-veto stays the AccessResolver's job: this driver only ever RAISES access
 * (allow / null), it never returns a deny Decision (H.2 step 4 before step 5).
 *
 *   - override(actor, scope) = isSuperAdmin → Effect::Allow, else null (never a deny);
 *   - resolve(subject, actor, scope) = per ranked level (low→high) the level's primary
 *     Ability is mapped to a permission and checked via hasPermissionIn against the
 *     workspace; the HIGHEST allowed level becomes the Decision;
 *   - subjectsFor(actor) = [Subject(actor)] only — AzGuard's per-resource model ANSWERS
 *     checks, it does not enumerate the role-subjects a v_node_grants row could be
 *     addressed to, so the driver contributes just the actor (documented limitation:
 *     a host that grants v_node_grants rows to AzGuard roles should additionally model
 *     those as Subjects, e.g. via a subclass; the guard answers the scoped checks);
 *   - canCreateInWorkspace = hasPermissionIn(type, id, the create permission).
 *
 * The actor's AzgardGuard is obtained leniently: if the actor itself implements the
 * seam (the host's User uses an AzGuard-backed adapter directly — the cleaner path,
 * since the AzGuard methods naturally live on the user), it is used as-is; otherwise
 * a host-bound AzgardGuard is resolved from the container (the adapter path, e.g. a
 * Corex TenantContextGuard-backed binding). When neither is available the lane is a
 * safe pass-through (null / false), never a fatal — so selecting 'azgard' without a
 * real binding degrades gracefully, exactly like the optional spatie lane.
 *
 * REAL-ECOSYSTEM INTEGRATION IS A HOST STEP: this slice proves the driver logic
 * against the {@see AzgardGuard} seam (a FakeAzgardGuard in tests). A production host
 * must bind a real AzgardGuard adapter delegating to AzGuard's hasScopedPermission /
 * Corex ContextGuard hasPermissionIn, AND align ulid morphs
 * (vaulter.ids.default=ulid + corex.ids.strategy=Ulid + AZ_GUARD_MORPH_TYPE=ulid) and
 * register workspace/owner types as Corex morph aliases.
 */
final class AzgardPermissionDriver implements PermissionDriver
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly Container $container,
    ) {}

    public function resolve(Subject $subject, Authorizable $actor, AccessScope $scope): ?Decision
    {
        $guard = $this->guardFor($actor);

        // The AzGuard check is user-scoped: only evaluate the actor's own Subject so
        // role/team Subjects (which AzGuard does not enumerate) never double-count.
        if ($guard === null || !$this->isActorSubject($subject, $actor)) {
            return null;
        }

        // Node-blind: AccessScope carries the workspace, not a Node, so the role lane is
        // the WORKSPACE-scoped permission check (composite order step 2). A null
        // workspace means there is nothing for AzGuard to scope against.
        if ($scope->workspaceType === null || $scope->workspaceId === null) {
            return null;
        }

        $granted = $this->highestLevelGranted($guard, $scope->workspaceType, $scope->workspaceId);

        if ($granted === null) {
            return null;
        }

        return Decision::allow($granted);
    }

    /**
     * The super-admin override: Effect::Allow when AzGuard's SuperAdmin wildcard is
     * held, else null (never a deny — the deny veto stays the ACL's job, H.2 step 5).
     */
    public function override(Authorizable $actor, AccessScope $scope): ?Effect
    {
        $guard = $this->guardFor($actor);

        if ($guard !== null && $guard->isSuperAdmin()) {
            return Effect::Allow;
        }

        return null;
    }

    /**
     * AzGuard answers per-resource checks rather than enumerating the role-subjects a
     * grant row could target, so the subject-set is the actor itself (documented
     * limitation, master plan §6). A host that addresses v_node_grants rows to AzGuard
     * roles should subclass and append those Subjects; the guard still answers the
     * scoped checks for the actor lane.
     *
     * Because this lane does NOT implement
     * {@see EnumeratesRoleSubjects}, a v_node_grants row
     * addressed to a role/team is inert under it; writing one fails loud
     * (GrantNodeAccessAction warns, and throws outside production — F-P1.2-01).
     *
     * @return list<Subject>
     */
    public function subjectsFor(Authorizable $actor): array
    {
        if (!$actor instanceof Model) {
            return [];
        }

        return [Subject::ofModel($actor)];
    }

    /**
     * May the actor create nodes in the host workspace? Delegates to AzGuard's
     * workspace-scoped check (hasPermissionIn) with the configured create permission —
     * the folder/upload create path has no existing node to resolve against (§6).
     */
    public function canCreateInWorkspace(Authorizable $actor, string $workspaceType, int|string $workspaceId): bool
    {
        $guard = $this->guardFor($actor);

        if ($guard === null) {
            return false;
        }

        return $guard->hasPermissionIn(
            contextType: $workspaceType,
            contextId: $workspaceId,
            permission: AzgardConfig::createPermission(),
        );
    }

    /**
     * The highest GrantLevel the workspace-scoped guard grants: each level (low→high)
     * is probed by its primary Ability's mapped permission via hasPermissionIn; the
     * top level that passes is returned. Mirrors the Gate/Spatie lanes' "highest
     * allowed level becomes the Decision" fold, but action-keyed (AzGuard is
     * permission-per-action, so a level is represented by the ability that defines it).
     */
    private function highestLevelGranted(AzgardGuard $guard, string $workspaceType, int|string $workspaceId): ?GrantLevel
    {
        $granted = null;

        foreach ($this->levelProbes() as $levelValue => $ability) {
            $level = GrantLevel::tryFrom($levelValue);
            $permission = AzgardConfig::permissionFor($ability);

            if ($level === null || $permission === null) {
                continue;
            }

            if (!$guard->hasPermissionIn(contextType: $workspaceType, contextId: $workspaceId, permission: $permission)) {
                continue;
            }

            $granted = $granted === null ? $level : $granted->max($level);
        }

        return $granted;
    }

    /**
     * The level → defining-ability probe map. Each GrantLevel is gated by the AzGuard
     * permission of the ability that most narrowly defines it: Reader by View,
     * Commenter by Comment, Writer by Edit, Organizer by Delete (it adds the DELETE
     * bit), Owner by Manage (full management).
     *
     * @return array<string, Ability>
     */
    private function levelProbes(): array
    {
        return [
            GrantLevel::Reader->value => Ability::View,
            GrantLevel::Commenter->value => Ability::Comment,
            GrantLevel::Writer->value => Ability::Edit,
            GrantLevel::Organizer->value => Ability::Delete,
            GrantLevel::Owner->value => Ability::Manage,
        ];
    }

    /**
     * Resolve the actor's AzgardGuard: the actor itself when it implements the seam
     * (the cleaner duck-typed path), else a host-bound AzgardGuard from the container,
     * else null (the lane is then a safe pass-through, never a fatal). The container
     * binding lets a host wire an adapter that closes over the resolved actor (e.g. a
     * Corex ContextGuard-backed adapter).
     */
    private function guardFor(Authorizable $actor): ?AzgardGuard
    {
        if ($actor instanceof AzgardGuard) {
            return $actor;
        }

        if (!$this->container->bound(AzgardGuard::class)) {
            return null;
        }

        return $this->container->make(AzgardGuard::class);
    }

    private function isActorSubject(Subject $subject, Authorizable $actor): bool
    {
        if (!$actor instanceof Model) {
            return false;
        }

        return $subject->equals(Subject::ofModel($actor));
    }
}

<<<M FILE packages/core/src/Access/Drivers/GatePermissionDriver.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Access\Drivers;

use Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Access\Authorizable;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Gate;
use Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\AccessScope;
use Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\Decision;
use Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\Subject;
use Vaulter\Contracts\Access\PermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Effect;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\GrantLevel;
use Vaulter\Support\GateConfig;

/**
 * The Laravel-Gate host-role driver (master plan §6 / H.2) — a zero-extra-dependency
 * lane, because the Gate ships with the framework. It bridges a host that already
 * authorises through Gate abilities / policies into Vaulter WITHOUT teaching Vaulter
 * the host's abilities: every coupling lives in a configurable ability map.
 *
 *   - subjectsFor(actor) = [Subject(actor)] — the Gate exposes no role/team subjects
 *     (abilities are evaluated against the user, not enumerated), so only the actor's
 *     own identity joins the subject-set; v_node_grants addressed to a role/team are
 *     simply not matched by this lane (use the Spatie/host authorization lane for that).
 *   - override(actor, scope) = a configurable super-admin ability (default
 *     'vaulter.super'); when the Gate allows it the actor short-circuits to full
 *     access, else this lane defers (null) — never a hard deny.
 *   - resolve(subject, actor, scope) = per requested level, the Gate is asked the
 *     mapped ability ('vaulter.view'/'vaulter.edit'/…); the HIGHEST allowed level
 *     becomes the Decision. The Gate check is Node-BLIND: it receives the AccessScope's
 *     panel + workspace coordinates, never a Node, so the contract stays swappable.
 *   - canCreateInWorkspace = the configured create ability, passed [type, id].
 *
 * Every Gate check goes through Gate::forUser($actor) so the driver is stateless and
 * never depends on the currently-authenticated user.
 */
final class GatePermissionDriver implements PermissionDriver
{
    /**
     * Per requested level (low → high) the Gate is asked the mapped ability; the
     * highest one it allows becomes the role Decision the AccessResolver folds in.
     * The AccessResolver itself iterates the subject-set, but the Gate is per-user
     * (not per-subject), so we evaluate the actor's own abilities here and the
     * resolve loop converges on the same Decision for the actor Subject.
     */
    public function resolve(Subject $subject, Authorizable $actor, AccessScope $scope): ?Decision
    {
        // The Gate is user-scoped, not subject-scoped: only evaluate against the
        // actor's own Subject so role/team Subjects (which the Gate cannot answer
        // for) do not double-count. A non-actor subject contributes nothing.
        if (!$this->isActorSubject($subject, $actor)) {
            return null;
        }

        $granted = null;

        foreach (GateConfig::abilityMap() as $levelValue => $ability) {
            $level = GrantLevel::tryFrom($levelValue);

            if ($level === null) {
                continue;
            }

            if (!$this->gateAllows($actor, $ability, [$this->contextFor($scope)])) {
                continue;
            }

            $granted = $granted === null ? $level : $granted->max($level);
        }

        if ($granted === null) {
            return null;
        }

        return Decision::allow($granted);
    }

    /**
     * The super-admin override: an Effect::Allow when the host's super ability is
     * granted, else null (never a deny — the Gate lane only widens access here, the
     * deny veto stays the ACL's job).
     */
    public function override(Authorizable $actor, AccessScope $scope): ?Effect
    {
        if ($this->gateAllows($actor, GateConfig::superAbility(), [$this->contextFor($scope)])) {
            return Effect::Allow;
        }

        return null;
    }

    /**
     * The Gate exposes no enumerable role/team subjects — abilities are evaluated
     * against the user, not listed — so the subject-set is the actor itself. A host
     * whose grants target Gate-derived roles should use the Spatie lane.
     *
     * Because this lane does NOT implement
     * {@see EnumeratesRoleSubjects}, a v_node_grants row
     * addressed to a role/team is inert under it; writing one fails loud
     * (GrantNodeAccessAction warns, and throws outside production — F-P1.2-01).
     *
     * @return list<Subject>
     */
    public function subjectsFor(Authorizable $actor): array
    {
        if (!$actor instanceof Model) {
            return [];
        }

        return [Subject::ofModel($actor)];
    }

    /**
     * May the actor create nodes in the host workspace? Delegates to the configured
     * create ability, passing the workspace [type, id] as the ability arguments so
     * the host's gate/policy can decide per workspace.
     */
    public function canCreateInWorkspace(Authorizable $actor, string $workspaceType, int|string $workspaceId): bool
    {
        return $this->gateAllows($actor, GateConfig::createAbility(), [$workspaceType, $workspaceId]);
    }

    /**
     * Run a Gate ability for the actor, node-blind (F-P1.2-02: this is a plain
     * delegation, there is no try/catch here — `Gate::allows()` itself already
     * returns false, never throws, for an ability the host has not defined, which
     * is what keeps an unconfigured host gate fail-closed).
     *
     * @param list<mixed> $arguments
     */
    private function gateAllows(Authorizable $actor, string $ability, array $arguments): bool
    {
        return Gate::forUser($actor)->allows($ability, $arguments);
    }

    /**
     * The Node-BLIND context handed to a Gate ability: the panel + workspace
     * coordinates from the AccessScope, never a Node. A host gate receives exactly the
     * workspace it authorises within (the contract's identity-agnostic boundary).
     *
     * @return array{panel: string, workspace_type: ?string, workspace_id: int|string|null}
     */
    private function contextFor(AccessScope $scope): array
    {
        return [
            'panel' => $scope->panel,
            'workspace_type' => $scope->workspaceType,
            'workspace_id' => $scope->workspaceId,
        ];
    }

    private function isActorSubject(Subject $subject, Authorizable $actor): bool
    {
        if (!$actor instanceof Model) {
            return false;
        }

        return $subject->equals(Subject::ofModel($actor));
    }
}

<<<M FILE packages/core/src/Access/PermissionDriverManager.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Access;

use Illuminate\Contracts\Container\Container;
use ReflectionMethod;
use Vaulter\Access\Drivers\DatabasePermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Access\Drivers\GatePermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Contracts\Access\EnumeratesRoleSubjects;
use Vaulter\Contracts\Access\NonEnumeratingPermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Contracts\Access\NonProductionPermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Contracts\Access\PermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Exceptions\Access\MissingPermissionDriverException;
use Vaulter\Support\Config;

/**
 * Resolves the active {@see PermissionDriver} from config (H.2), keyed by the driver
 * key so a per-panel resolved-state never leaks across panels (H.1). It is the
 * single seam the AccessResolver obtains its role lane through, and the place the
 * null-driver fail-loud guard (D6″) lives: the open NullPermissionDriver is rejected in
 * production, so a missing/null driver can never silently open a prod install.
 *
 * The default key is 'database' — the standalone {@see DatabasePermissionDriver}.
 */
final class PermissionDriverManager
{
    /**
     * The built-in lanes whose subjectsFor() provably contributes ONLY the actor's own
     * identity — no role/team fan-out. A driver that inherits subjectsFor() UNCHANGED
     * from one of these cannot match a v_node_grants row addressed to a role/team.
     *
     * @var list<class-string<PermissionDriver>>
     */
    private const array NON_ENUMERATING_BASE_LANES = [
        DatabasePermissionDriver::class,
        GatePermissionDriver::class,
    ];

    /**
     * @var array<string, PermissionDriver>
     */
    private array $resolved = [];

    public function __construct(
        private readonly Container $container,
        private readonly bool $isProduction,
    ) {}

    /**
     * The driver for the given key (default: the configured driver). Memoised per
     * key (H.1). Throws in production when the key resolves to the open null
     * driver, or when an unknown key has no FQCN.
     */
    public function driver(?string $key = null): PermissionDriver
    {
        $key ??= Config::permissionDriver();

        if (isset($this->resolved[$key])) {
            return $this->resolved[$key];
        }

        $class = $this->classFor($key);

        if (is_a($class, NonProductionPermissionDriver::class, allow_string: true) && $this->isProduction) {
            throw MissingPermissionDriverException::nullDriverInProduction($key);
        }

        /** @var PermissionDriver $driver */
        $driver = $this->container->make($class);

        return $this->resolved[$key] = $driver;
    }

    /**
     * Does the driver expand an actor into role/group/team {@see Subject}s — so a
     * v_node_grants row addressed to a role/team actually enters the AccessResolver
     * subject-set (F-P1.2-01)? Two signals, in order:
     *
     *   1. it implements the explicit {@see EnumeratesRoleSubjects} marker (the spatie
     *      lane, or any host driver that opts in); OR
     *   2. it has OVERRIDDEN subjectsFor() away from a built-in base lane whose
     *      implementation provably contributes only the actor.
     *
     * The second signal keeps the DOCUMENTED extension path honest (H.2 / ADR-0007):
     * {@see DatabasePermissionDriver}'s own docblock promotes "subclass and append
     * Subject(type:'role', …) in subjectsFor()" as the way to add a role lane on the
     * default base. A host that follows it — its role grants genuinely take effect — is
     * recognised WITHOUT also having to add the marker. We therefore fail a role/team
     * grant loud ONLY when the active driver PROVABLY cannot enumerate them (subjectsFor
     * is inherited unchanged from a base lane that returns just [actor]), never for a
     * working-but-unmarked override.
     */
    public function enumeratesRoleSubjects(PermissionDriver $driver): bool
    {
        if ($driver instanceof EnumeratesRoleSubjects) {
            return true;
        }

        $declaration = (new ReflectionMethod($driver, 'subjectsFor'))->getDeclaringClass();

        if (in_array($declaration->getName(), self::NON_ENUMERATING_BASE_LANES, true)) {
            return false;
        }

        // Only the marked base implementation is actor-only. A subclass that
        // overrides subjectsFor() inherits its interfaces but may add role subjects.
        $parent = $declaration->getParentClass();

        return !$declaration->implementsInterface(NonEnumeratingPermissionDriver::class)
            || ($parent !== false && $parent->implementsInterface(NonEnumeratingPermissionDriver::class));
    }

    /**
     * @return class-string<PermissionDriver>
     */
    private function classFor(string $key): string
    {
        $drivers = Config::permissionDrivers();

        if (isset($drivers[$key])) {
            return $drivers[$key];
        }

        throw MissingPermissionDriverException::unknownDriver($key, array_keys($drivers));
    }
}

<<<M FILE packages/core/src/Actions/Access/GrantNodeAccessAction.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Actions\Access;

use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Log;
use Vaulter\Access\PermissionDriverManager;
use Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\Subject;
use Vaulter\Data\Access\GrantNodeAccessInput;
use Vaulter\Database\VaulterDatabase;
use Vaulter\Events\Access\NodeGrantCreated;
use Vaulter\Exceptions\Access\UnenumerableGrantSubjectException;
use Vaulter\Models\Access\NodeGrant;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Node;
use Vaulter\Repositories\Access\GrantStoreRepository;
use Vaulter\Support\SpatieConfig;

/**
 * Grant (or deny) a subject access to a node (§2.6 / H.2). Idempotent on the
 * grant-unique key: re-granting the same subject the same scope/effect updates the
 * level/bits/expiry. The write runs in a transaction and emits NodeGrantCreated.
 *
 * Authorization (the actor may Share/Manage the node) is enforced by the caller
 * (controller/policy) before reaching the Action — the Action persists, it does
 * not re-authorize.
 */
final readonly class GrantNodeAccessAction
{
    public function __construct(
        private GrantStoreRepository $grants,
        private PermissionDriverManager $drivers,
        private VaulterDatabase $database,
    ) {}

    public function execute(Node $node, GrantNodeAccessInput $data): NodeGrant
    {
        // Fail-loud (F-P1.2-01) BEFORE persisting: a grant to a role/team subject under
        // a driver that cannot enumerate role subjects would be silently inert.
        $this->guardEnumerableSubject($data);

        // The event fires INSIDE the transaction (F-P1.7-03): the outbox/activity rows
        // stage in the SAME commit as the grant — no crash window between commit and
        // staging. The subscribers swallow their own failures, so staging still never
        // rolls the grant back.
        return $this->database->transaction(function () use ($node, $data): NodeGrant {
            $grant = $this->grants->grant(node: $node, data: $data);

            event(new NodeGrantCreated(grant: $grant, actorId: $data->grantedBy));

            return $grant;
        });
    }

    /**
     * Make the silent no-op loud (F-P1.2-01): a grant addressed to a role/group/team
     * subject only ever matches when the active {@see PermissionDriver} expands the actor
     * into those Subjects. Whether it does is decided by
     * {@see PermissionDriverManager::enumeratesRoleSubjects()} — the explicit
     * {@see EnumeratesRoleSubjects} marker OR an overridden `subjectsFor()` (the
     * documented subclass-and-append extension path counts, marker or not). We fail loud
     * ONLY when the driver PROVABLY cannot enumerate role subjects — the standalone
     * `database` base, `gate`, `bridge`, or the `null` lane with `subjectsFor()`
     * inherited unchanged. We always warn, and outside production we throw so a developer
     * notices immediately. The direction is safe (an inert grant grants nothing), so
     * production degrades to a log line rather than a broken write path.
     */
    private function guardEnumerableSubject(GrantNodeAccessInput $data): void
    {
        if (!$this->isRoleLikeSubject($data->subject)) {
            return;
        }

        $driver = $this->drivers->driver();

        if ($this->drivers->enumeratesRoleSubjects($driver)) {
            return;
        }

        Log::warning(
            '[Vaulter] Grant addressed to a role/team subject under a host-role driver '
            .'that does not enumerate role subjects — it will never take effect.',
            [
                'subject_type' => $data->subject->type,
                'subject_id' => $data->subject->id,
                'driver' => $driver::class,
            ],
        );

        if (!app()->environment('production')) {
            throw UnenumerableGrantSubjectException::for($data->subject, $driver::class);
        }
    }

    /**
     * Is the subject a role/group/team subject (as opposed to a user identity)? The
     * canonical role/team subject-type aliases are the ones grant rows are addressed to
     * (config vaulter.spatie.role_subject_type / team_subject_type).
     */
    private function isRoleLikeSubject(Subject $subject): bool
    {
        return in_array(
            $subject->type,
            [SpatieConfig::roleSubjectType(), SpatieConfig::teamSubjectType()],
            strict: true,
        );
    }
}

<<<D FILE packages/core/src/Contracts/Access/AzgardGuard.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Contracts\Access;

/**
 * The NARROW Vaulter-owned seam the host's AzGuard-backed actor satisfies (master
 * plan §6 / H.2 / ADR-0007). It exposes EXACTLY the three checks the
 * {@see AzgardPermissionDriver} needs — and nothing of AzGuard's own API — so
 * vaulter-core carries NO hard dependency on azguard/corex and PHPStan stays green
 * with the package ABSENT (no concrete AzGuard\* / CoreX\* references anywhere in
 * the driver path).
 *
 * The host binds a real adapter (delegating to AzGuard's HasAzGuard concern /
 * Corex TenantContextGuard — `hasScopedPermission` / `hasPermissionIn` / the
 * SuperAdmin wildcard) for the resolved actor; tests bind {@see FakeAzgardGuard}.
 * Either way the driver only ever sees this interface, never AzGuard's classes.
 *
 * Method shapes mirror AzGuard 1:1 so a host adapter is a thin pass-through:
 *   - hasScopedPermission($perm, $entity) ≙ AzGuard\Concerns\HasScopedRoles::hasScopedPermission($perm, $entity)
 *   - hasPermissionIn($type, $id, $perm)  ≙ AzGuard\Concerns\HasPermissions::hasPermissionIn($type, $id, $perm)
 *   - isSuperAdmin()                      ≙ the global SuperAdmin wildcard (*) AzGuard grants
 *
 * Morph-alias note (host responsibility): the $contextType / $entity morph types
 * MUST be registered Corex morph aliases (EntityRegistry / ADR-003) aligned with
 * `vaulter.ids.default=ulid` + `corex.ids.strategy=Ulid` + `AZ_GUARD_MORPH_TYPE=ulid`.
 * The driver passes the workspace type string through untouched — it never resolves
 * the alias itself.
 */
interface AzgardGuard
{
    /**
     * Does the actor hold $permission scoped to the given resource $entity (the
     * per-node lane)? Mirrors AzGuard's `hasScopedPermission`: the global SuperAdmin
     * wildcard wins first, then a scoped role on that exact entity. $entity is the
     * host's morph-aligned model (e.g. the Node or its owning host record).
     */
    public function hasScopedPermission(string $permission, object $entity): bool;

    /**
     * Does the actor hold $permission within the host workspace identified by its
     * morph ($contextType, $contextId)? Mirrors AzGuard's `hasPermissionIn` (the
     * Corex TenantContextGuard contextual check) — the workspace-scoped-role lane
     * and the create gate both route through here (there is no Node to resolve
     * against for create).
     */
    public function hasPermissionIn(string $contextType, int|string $contextId, string $permission): bool;

    /**
     * Is the actor a global super-admin? Mirrors AzGuard's SuperAdmin wildcard (*).
     * When true the resolver short-circuits to an absolute allow override (H.2 step 1),
     * before any ACL or workspace walk.
     */
    public function isSuperAdmin(): bool;
}

<<<M FILE packages/core/src/Contracts/Access/EnumeratesRoleSubjects.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Contracts\Access;

/**
 * A capability marker (F-P1.2-01): the {@see PermissionDriver} implementing it declares
 * that its `subjectsFor()` DOES expand an actor into role/group/team {@see Subject}s,
 * not just the actor's own identity — so a `v_node_grants` row addressed to a role or
 * team actually enters the AccessResolver's subject-set and takes effect.
 *
 * This marker is the EXPLICIT capability signal, but not the only one: the built-in
 * base lanes that inherit `subjectsFor()` unchanged (the standalone `database` base,
 * `gate`, `bridge`, the `null` lane) contribute only the actor itself, so a grant
 * addressed to a role/team under them is silently inert. Vaulter makes that silence
 * LOUD — {@see GrantNodeAccessAction} warns (and, outside production, throws) — but ONLY
 * when the driver PROVABLY cannot enumerate: neither this marker NOR an overridden
 * `subjectsFor()` (see {@see PermissionDriverManager::enumeratesRoleSubjects()}).
 * A host that follows the documented extension path — subclass a base lane and override
 * `subjectsFor()` to append role/team Subjects — is recognised WITHOUT this marker.
 *
 * It is a pure marker — no methods — because the fan-out lives in `subjectsFor()`; this
 * interface only ADVERTISES that the driver honours the full ADR-0007 contract
 * (actor → users + roles + teams), sparing the reflection probe. Implementing it is the
 * cleanest way for a host role driver to declare the capability, but overriding
 * `subjectsFor()` alone already suffices for role grants to be accepted.
 */
interface EnumeratesRoleSubjects {}

<<<M FILE packages/core/src/Contracts/Access/GrantAuthoritativeDriver.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Contracts\Access;

/**
 * A capability a {@see PermissionDriver} implements to declare that v_node_grants is the
 * SOLE authority for read-visibility (master plan P1 #3 / H.4). When {@see
 * isGrantAuthoritative()} is true, the grant-anchor narrowing in {@see
 * NodeReadRepository::constrainToAccessible()} is a COMPLETE superset of everything the
 * actor can reach, so narrowing a listing to that set never wrongly hides a row.
 *
 * Only the standalone {@see DatabasePermissionDriver} declares it true out of the box.
 * For the gate/spatie/bridge drivers the host's roles govern (an actor can see nodes with
 * NO grant anchor), so they do NOT implement this interface at all ⇒ the listing stays
 * OPEN (the safe default, never wrongly hiding).
 *
 * This is deliberately a SEPARATE capability, not a method on the SemVer-frozen
 * {@see PermissionDriver} (adding to that contract would break every external driver). A
 * driver opts IN by implementing this; its absence is the conservative, BC-safe default.
 *
 * It is a METHOD, not a bare marker, on purpose: PHP interfaces are INHERITED, so a host
 * that SUBCLASSES {@see DatabasePermissionDriver} to add a role lane (resolve()) or a
 * super-admin override() still carries the interface — declaring or not declaring it on
 * the subclass changes nothing. Such a subclass MUST override {@see isGrantAuthoritative()}
 * to return false (it can now reach un-anchored nodes, so narrowing would hide them). A
 * pure subject-broadening subclass that introduces no new authority keeps returning true.
 */
interface GrantAuthoritativeDriver
{
    /**
     * Whether v_node_grants is THIS driver instance's sole read-visibility authority, so a
     * listing may safely narrow to the actor's grant-reachable candidate set. Return false
     * the moment the driver confers access by ANY non-grant means (host roles/teams, a
     * workspace-create gate, a super-admin override()).
     */
    public function isGrantAuthoritative(): bool;
}

<<<M FILE packages/core/src/Contracts/Access/PermissionDriver.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Contracts\Access;

use Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Access\Authorizable;
use Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\AccessScope;
use Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\Decision;
use Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\Subject;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Effect;

/**
 * The host's pluggable, per-panel role lane (master plan H.2 / D6). It bridges the
 * host application's identity + role system into Vaulter WITHOUT leaking Vaulter's
 * own domain: it never receives a Node and never deals in magic-string actions —
 * only an Authorizable actor and an {@see AccessScope} (panel + workspace coordinates
 * + node owner). The Vaulter-owned, NON-swappable {@see AccessResolver}
 * combines this driver's answers with the v_node_grants ACL.
 *
 * Swap it via config('vaulter.drivers.permission' + permission_drivers map); the
 * default is the standalone {@see DatabasePermissionDriver}.
 *
 * Implementations are a SemVer-frozen public API from M2a — M2b's Gate/Spatie/
 * host authorization drivers implement exactly this surface, and a contract test asserts every
 * driver yields identical AccessResolver decisions on a shared fixture.
 */
interface PermissionDriver
{
    /**
     * The host's role decision for an actor within a scope, or null when the host
     * role system has nothing to say (decisions then come purely from the ACL). A
     * returned Decision is folded as roleAllow into `granted = max(aclAllow,
     * roleAllow)` (H.2 step 4) — it can RAISE access but can never override a deny
     * (the final veto, H.2 step 5, still applies).
     */
    public function resolve(Subject $subject, Authorizable $actor, AccessScope $scope): ?Decision;

    /**
     * An absolute host override (super-admin / Gate::before), or null when none
     * applies (H.2 step 1). Effect::Allow short-circuits to full access; Effect::Deny
     * short-circuits to no access — both in BOTH directions, before any ACL walk.
     */
    public function override(Authorizable $actor, AccessScope $scope): ?Effect;

    /**
     * Expand an actor into the set of Subjects whose grants apply to them (H.2): the
     * user itself plus any host roles/teams it belongs to. Vaulter builds
     * `WHERE (subject_type, subject_id) IN (...)` from this list, so the driver
     * controls the identity fan-out without Vaulter knowing the host's role schema.
     *
     * @return list<Subject>
     */
    public function subjectsFor(Authorizable $actor): array;

    /**
     * May the actor create nodes in the given host workspace? Used by the folder/
     * upload create path, where there is no existing node to resolve against
     * (`canCreate`). The workspace is identified by its host morph type + id.
     */
    public function canCreateInWorkspace(Authorizable $actor, string $workspaceType, int|string $workspaceId): bool;
}

<<<M FILE packages/core/src/Contracts/IdStrategy.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Contracts;

use Illuminate\Database\Schema\Blueprint;

/**
 * Primary-key strategy. Drives column types in the published (and later
 * generated) migrations plus the matching model concern, so "ulid vs uuid7 vs
 * bigint" is decided from config('vaulter.ids.default') rather than hard-coded.
 *
 * Vaulter defaults to ulid (D9) so morph keys line up with the Corex/host authorization
 * ecosystem; uuid7 maps onto native Postgres uuid columns and bigint is the
 * legacy auto-increment path. Implementations live in the Schema namespace.
 */
interface IdStrategy
{
    /**
     * Define the primary-key column on the table.
     */
    public function key(Blueprint $table, string $column = 'id'): void;

    /**
     * Define a foreign reference to another Vaulter entity (same key type).
     * The explicit ->foreign()->cascadeOnDelete() is added by the migration.
     */
    public function reference(Blueprint $table, string $column, bool $nullable = false): void;

    /**
     * Define a reference to an actor (host user id) — no DB-level FK, because
     * the consuming application owns the users table.
     */
    public function actor(Blueprint $table, string $column, bool $nullable = false): void;

    /**
     * Eloquent cast for the key type.
     */
    public function cast(): string;

    /**
     * Model concern (trait FQCN) applying this key type, or null for bigint.
     *
     * @return class-string|null
     */
    public function modelConcern(): ?string;

    /**
     * Mint a fresh key for the creating event, or null for auto-increment keys
     * (where the database assigns the value).
     */
    public function newId(): string|int|null;
}

<<<M FILE packages/core/src/Exceptions/Access/MissingPermissionDriverException.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Exceptions\Access;

use Vaulter\Exceptions\VaulterException;

/**
 * The host-role driver is missing, unknown, or the open null-driver was selected
 * in production (master plan H.2 / D6″ — fail-loud, never silently open).
 */
final class MissingPermissionDriverException extends VaulterException
{
    public static function nullDriverInProduction(string $key): self
    {
        return new self(
            sprintf('[Vaulter] The open null host-role driver [%s] is forbidden in production. ', $key)
            .'Why: it grants every actor full access; running it in prod would expose every node. '
            .'Fix: set config(vaulter.drivers.permission) to a real driver (database|gate|spatie or an installed bridge) '
            .'or bind your own \Vaulter\Contracts\Access\PermissionDriver. '
            .'Docs: '.self::docs('missing-host-role-driver'),
        );
    }

    /**
     * @param list<string> $known
     */
    public static function unknownDriver(string $key, array $known): self
    {
        return new self(
            sprintf('[Vaulter] Unknown host-role driver [%s]. ', $key)
            .sprintf('Known drivers: [%s]. ', implode(', ', $known))
            .'Fix: register it under config(vaulter.permission_drivers) with an FQCN implementing '
            .'\Vaulter\Contracts\Access\PermissionDriver, or pick a known key in config(vaulter.drivers.permission). '
            .'Docs: '.self::docs('missing-host-role-driver'),
        );
    }
}
