<<<M FILE packages/core/src/Repositories/Drive/NodeReadRepository.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Repositories\Drive;

use Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Access\Authorizable;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Database\Query\Builder as QueryBuilder;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Builder;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Collection;
use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Model;
use Illuminate\Support\Carbon;
use Vaulter\Access\AccessResolver;
use Vaulter\Access\PermissionDriverManager;
use Vaulter\Contracts\Access\GrantAuthoritativeDriver;
use Vaulter\Contracts\Observability\MetricsRecorder;
use Vaulter\Database\VaulterDatabase;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\GrantScope;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Drive;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Node;
use Vaulter\Repositories\Access\GrantReadRepository;
use Vaulter\Support\Config;
use Vaulter\Support\Identity;
use Vaulter\Support\LoadTier;

/**
 * Read-side queries over the v_nodes adjacency tree (§2.2 / H.4). Tree reads use
 * the staudenmeir recursive relationships (descendants/ancestors), always bounded
 * by treeOf(storage) and — for bulk descents — withMaxDepth, never the BANNED
 * whereHas('descendants') / withCount('descendants') which break on MariaDB and
 * degrade on Postgres (H.4 arch-ban).
 *
 * queryForUser()/constrainToAccessible() narrow grant-authoritative drivers to
 * candidate IDs. Candidates require exact AccessResolver evaluation before display;
 * the REST listings and admin table apply that after fetching each page.
 */
final class NodeReadRepository
{
    /**
     * The maximum recursion depth for bulk subtree descents — file managers live
     * at depth ≤ ~20 (§1.5), so this caps a pathological tree without an explicit
     * caller bound.
     */
    public const int DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH = 64;

    /**
     * Keep small sets bound, with room for storage, parent and cursor bindings even
     * on SQLite builds limited to 999 variables. Larger sets use escaped SQL literals
     * and add no bindings, regardless of the number of grant-reachable nodes.
     */
    private const int WHERE_IN_BIND_LIMIT = 900;

    public function __construct(
        private readonly AccessResolver $access,
        private readonly PermissionDriverManager $drivers,
        private readonly GrantReadRepository $grants,
        private readonly MetricsRecorder $metrics,
    ) {}

    public function find(int|string $id): ?Node
    {
        return $this->query()->find($id);
    }

    /**
     * Every live (non-trashed, non-deleted) node in a storage's tree.
     *
     * @return Builder<Node>
     */
    public function forStorage(Drive $storage): Builder
    {
        return $this->query()
            ->treeOf($storage->id)
            ->whereNull('trashed_at');
    }

    /**
     * Direct children of a folder (or the storage root when $parent is null),
     * ordered by the manual sibling position then name.
     *
     * @return Builder<Node>
     */
    public function children(Drive $storage, ?Node $parent): Builder
    {
        return $this->metrics->timing(
            name: 'vaulter_tree_query_duration_seconds',
            operation: fn (): Builder => $this->query()
                ->treeOf($storage->id)
                ->whereNull('trashed_at')
                ->where('parent_id', $parent?->id)
                ->orderBy('position')
                ->orderBy('name')
                ->orderBy('id'),
            labels: [
                'query_kind' => 'children',
                'tier' => LoadTier::label(),
            ],
        );
    }

    /**
     * Whether the node is its drive's root — the one node without a parent, which
     * tree operations never take as an operand.
     */
    public function isRoot(Node $node): bool
    {
        $rootId = $node->storage->root_node_id;

        return $rootId !== null && Identity::stringify($node->getKey()) === Identity::stringify($rootId);
    }

    /**
     * The whole subtree below a node via the recursive CTE, bounded by
     * withMaxDepth so the descent never runs unbounded (H.4). The node itself is
     * NOT part of descendants() — callers add it when needed.
     *
     * @return Collection<int, Node>
     */
    public function descendants(Node $node, ?int $maxDepth = null): Collection
    {
        $model = Config::nodeModel();

        /** @var Collection<int, Node> $result */
        $result = $model::withMaxDepth(
            $maxDepth ?? self::DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH,
            static fn (): Collection => $node->descendants()->get(),
        );

        return $result;
    }

    /**
     * The node plus its whole subtree (the node first), bounded by withMaxDepth.
     * This is the unit a trash/restore/force-delete touches atomically.
     *
     * @return Collection<int, Node>
     */
    public function subtree(Node $node, ?int $maxDepth = null): Collection
    {
        return $this->metrics->timing(
            name: 'vaulter_tree_query_duration_seconds',
            operation: function () use ($node, $maxDepth): Collection {
                $model = Config::nodeModel();

                /** @var Collection<int, Node> $result */
                $result = $model::withMaxDepth(
                    $maxDepth ?? self::DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH,
                    static fn (): Collection => $node->descendantsAndSelf()->get(),
                );

                return $result;
            },
            labels: [
                'query_kind' => 'subtree',
                'tier' => LoadTier::label(),
            ],
        );
    }

    /**
     * @param  list<int|string>               $parentIds
     * @return array<string, list<\stdClass>>
     */
    public function ancestorChains(array $parentIds): array
    {
        if ($parentIds === []) {
            return [];
        }
        /** @var \Staudenmeir\LaravelAdjacencyList\Eloquent\Builder<Node> $query */
        $query = $this->query();
        $connection = app(VaulterDatabase::class)->connection();
        $grammar = $query->getExpressionGrammar();
        $table = $connection->getQueryGrammar()->wrapTable($query->getModel()->getTable());
        $separator = $query->getModel()->getPathSeparator();
        $initialPath = $grammar->compileInitialPath('id', '__acl_path');
        $seed = $this->whereKeyInBounded($query, $parentIds)
            ->select(['id', 'parent_id', 'drive_id', 'inherit_grants'])->selectRaw('id as origin, 0 as depth');
        // Match ancestors()'s ascend semantics, including its database-specific
        // cycle guard. withMaxDepth(+64) does not limit negative ancestor depths.
        $path = $grammar->compileRecursivePath('n.id', 'c.__acl_path');
        $cycle = $grammar->compileCycleDetection('n.id', 'c.__acl_path');
        $sql = 'WITH RECURSIVE chain AS (SELECT seed.*, '.$initialPath.' FROM ('.$seed->toSql().') seed
            UNION ALL SELECT n.id, n.parent_id, n.drive_id, n.inherit_grants, c.origin, c.depth + 1, '.$path.'
            FROM '.$table.' n JOIN chain c ON n.id = c.parent_id AND n.drive_id = c.drive_id
            WHERE c.inherit_grants = ? AND NOT ('.$cycle.') AND n.deleted_at IS NULL)
            SELECT * FROM chain ORDER BY origin, depth';
        $rows = $connection->select($sql, [
            ...$seed->getBindings(),
            ...$grammar->getRecursivePathBindings($separator),
            true,
            ...$grammar->getCycleDetectionBindings($separator),
        ]);
        $chains = [];
        foreach ($rows as $row) {
            if (!$row instanceof \stdClass || (!is_string($row->origin) && !is_int($row->origin))) {
                throw new \LogicException('Invalid ancestor chain row.');
            }
            $chains[Identity::stringify($row->origin)][] = $row;
        }

        return $chains;
    }

    /**
     * The ancestor chain from the node up to the storage root (nearest first),
     * bounded by withMaxDepth (F-P4.2-01, VLT-REMED P4.3) — the same cap
     * descendants()/subtree() already apply on the other traversal direction
     * (ADR-0005 requires the symmetry; this was the missing ascend-side half).
     *
     * @return Collection<int, Node>
     */
    public function ancestors(Node $node): Collection
    {
        $model = Config::nodeModel();

        /** @var Collection<int, Node> $result */
        $result = $model::withMaxDepth(
            self::DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH,
            static fn (): Collection => $node->ancestors()->get(),
        );

        return $result;
    }

    /**
     * Breadcrumb from the storage root down to the node (root first), the node
     * included as the last crumb. Bounded by withMaxDepth (F-P4.2-01) — same
     * reasoning as ancestors() above.
     *
     * @return Collection<int, Node>
     */
    public function breadcrumb(Node $node): Collection
    {
        return $this->metrics->timing(
            name: 'vaulter_tree_query_duration_seconds',
            operation: function () use ($node): Collection {
                $model = Config::nodeModel();

                /** @var Collection<int, Node> $crumbs */
                $crumbs = $model::withMaxDepth(
                    self::DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH,
                    static fn (): Collection => $node->ancestorsAndSelf()->get(),
                );

                /** @var Collection<int, Node> $ordered */
                $ordered = $crumbs->reverse()->values();

                return $ordered;
            },
            labels: [
                'query_kind' => 'breadcrumb',
                'tier' => LoadTier::label(),
            ],
        );
    }

    /**
     * Name search within a storage tree (live nodes only). Matches a case-folded
     * substring of the node name — the §2.2 search index backs this.
     *
     * The caller-supplied term is untrusted (F-P1.8-03): `LIKE` metacharacters
     * (`%`, `_`, `\`) are escaped BEFORE the substring wildcards are wrapped
     * around it, with an explicit `ESCAPE '\'` clause — a raw `%`/`_` in the
     * term is matched LITERALLY, never as a wildcard, on both SQLite and
     * PostgreSQL. Case-folding happens first so escaping never touches
     * multibyte case-mapping. `orderBy('id')` is a stable tie-breaker
     * (F-P4.2-05, VLT-REMED P4.3): `name` is unique only per-parent (ADR-0005)
     * and this method searches across the WHOLE tree, so cursorPaginate()'s
     * keyset would otherwise skip/duplicate rows across a page boundary that
     * lands on two nodes sharing a name in different folders.
     *
     * @return Builder<Node>
     */
    public function search(Drive $storage, string $term): Builder
    {
        return $this->metrics->timing(
            name: 'vaulter_tree_query_duration_seconds',
            operation: function () use ($storage, $term): Builder {
                $escaped = addcslashes(mb_strtolower($term), '%_\\');

                return $this->query()
                    ->treeOf($storage->id)
                    ->whereNull('trashed_at')
                    ->whereRaw("lower(name) like ? escape '\\'", ['%'.$escaped.'%'])
                    ->orderBy('name')
                    ->orderBy('id');
            },
            labels: [
                'query_kind' => 'search',
                'tier' => LoadTier::label(),
            ],
        );
    }

    /**
     * The trash view: trashed (but not yet permanently deleted) nodes in a
     * storage, newest first. `orderByDesc('id')` is a stable tie-breaker
     * (F-P4.2-05, VLT-REMED P4.3): several nodes trashed by the same
     * operation/request share an identical trashed_at timestamp, so
     * cursorPaginate()'s keyset would otherwise skip/duplicate rows on that
     * page boundary.
     *
     * @return Builder<Node>
     */
    public function trashed(Drive $storage): Builder
    {
        return $this->query()
            ->treeOf($storage->id)
            ->whereNotNull('trashed_at')
            ->orderByDesc('trashed_at')
            ->orderByDesc('id');
    }

    /**
     * The trashed nodes whose trashed_at is at or before $threshold — the
     * purge-trash candidates past their retention window (§2.10). Only ROOTS of a
     * trash operation are returned: a node whose own parent is itself trashed is
     * skipped, because force-deleting an ancestor's subtree already reclaims it (so
     * a child is never purged twice). Returns a Builder so the command chunks it.
     *
     * @return Builder<Node>
     */
    public function trashedBefore(Carbon $threshold): Builder
    {
        $model = Config::nodeModel();
        $table = (new $model)->getTable();

        return $this->query()
            ->whereNotNull('trashed_at')
            ->where('trashed_at', '<=', $threshold)
            // Skip descendants whose own parent is also trashed — the trashed
            // ancestor is the purge root and its subtree force-delete covers them.
            ->whereNotExists(static function (QueryBuilder $sub) use ($table): void {
                $sub->selectRaw('1')
                    ->from($table.' as parent_node')
                    ->whereColumn('parent_node.id', $table.'.parent_id')
                    ->whereNotNull('parent_node.trashed_at');
            })
            ->orderBy('trashed_at');
    }

    /**
     * Whether a live sibling already owns $name under $parentId in this storage
     * (case-insensitive) — the §2.2 sibling-unique predicate the Actions check
     * before create/move/rename. $ignoreId excludes the node being renamed in
     * place. Uses a direct EXISTS, NOT a recursive descendant aggregate (H.4).
     */
    public function siblingNameExists(
        Drive $storage,
        int|string|null $parentId,
        string $name,
        int|string|null $ignoreId = null,
    ): bool {
        $query = $this->query()
            ->treeOf($storage->id)
            ->where('parent_id', $parentId)
            ->whereNull('trashed_at')
            ->whereRaw('lower(name) = ?', [mb_strtolower($name)]);

        if ($ignoreId !== null) {
            $query->whereKeyNot($ignoreId);
        }

        return $query->exists();
    }

    /**
     * The STANDALONE public seam (master plan P1 #3): the live (non-trashed) nodes an
     * actor may reach, as a Builder for pagination / admin. It is the named entry
     * for "give me this actor's nodes" = the live-nodes base + constrainToAccessible.
     * A caller that needs its own trashed-state control (the children cursor below, or
     * the admin table whose Trashed filter flips trashed_at) composes
     * {@see constrainToAccessible()} on its own base instead.
     *
     * When grant-filtering applies (see {@see grantFilteringApplies()}) the base is
     * constrained to the actor's CANDIDATE accessible node ids; otherwise the base is
     * returned UNCHANGED (open listing — the host's roles govern).
     *
     * The candidate set is the grant ANCHORS for the actor's subject-set UNION the
     * descendants of every SUBTREE-scoped anchor (an item-scoped anchor contributes
     * only its own node). It is a deliberate SUPERSET: it does NOT apply the deny-veto
     * or the inherit_grants cut-off in SQL, so a node a nearer deny revokes can still
     * be in the set. The candidate-set listing semantic is documented on
     * {@see constrainToAccessible()}; per-ACTION authorization stays EXACT via the
     * {@see AccessResolver} on every mutation/show.
     *
     * @return Builder<Node>
     */
    public function queryForUser(Authorizable $actor): Builder
    {
        $base = $this->query()->whereNull('trashed_at');

        return $this->constrainToAccessible($base, $actor);
    }

    /**
     * Constrain an ALREADY-BUILT node query to the actor's grant-reachable candidate
     * set (P1 #3), WITHOUT imposing the live/trashed filter — so a caller that owns
     * its own trashed-state handling (the children cursor; the admin table, whose
     * Trashed filter flips trashed_at) composes the access narrowing on top of its own
     * query. A no-op when grant-filtering does not apply (open drivers); forces an
     * empty result when it applies and the actor reaches no candidate.
     *
     * This SQL prefilter deliberately admits denied candidates. Apply exact batch
     * AccessResolver evaluation before display.
     *
     * Generic over the concrete model so a Node-typed base (the core listing paths) and
     * a admin resource's `Builder<Model>` both compose without a variance clash — the
     * narrowing is key-based, never model-specific.
     *
     * @template TModel of Model
     *
     * @param  Builder<TModel> $query
     * @return Builder<TModel>
     */
    public function constrainToAccessible(Builder $query, Authorizable $actor): Builder
    {
        if (!$this->grantFilteringApplies()) {
            return $query;
        }

        $candidateIds = $this->candidateNodeIds($actor);

        if ($candidateIds === []) {
            return $query->whereRaw('1 = 0');
        }

        return $this->whereKeyInBounded($query, $candidateIds);
    }

    /**
     * Narrow an already-loaded set of nodes to the ones the actor may actually View,
     * delegating to the AccessResolver (the EXACT deny-veto / inherit-cutoff gate,
     * H.2). This is the correctness companion to the SUPERSET candidate query: a
     * caller lists candidates cheaply, then runs the page through here.
     *
     * @param  iterable<Node> $nodes
     * @return list<Node>
     */
    public function filterViewable(Authorizable $actor, iterable $nodes): array
    {
        return $this->access->filterSharedWith($actor, $nodes);
    }

    /**
     * The "shared with me" top-level view (§2.6 / H.2): the nodes the actor holds a
     * live allow-grant on, RE-RESOLVED through the full algorithm so a nearer deny
     * that revokes a row excludes it (the EXACT gate, over a bounded candidate set —
     * unlike the candidate-SQL listings). Cross-storage by nature: the subject index
     * is not storage-bound.
     *
     * Eager-loads the storage relation so the per-candidate re-resolution does NOT
     * fire one storage query per node: the {@see AccessResolver} prefers an
     * already-loaded `storage` relation over a per-node lookup, so this `with('storage')`
     * spares the gate's per-node storage query (and the NodeResource reads the same
     * relation). Without it the eager-load would be dead weight.
     *
     * @return Collection<int, Node>
     */
    public function sharedWith(Authorizable $actor): Collection
    {
        $candidateIds = $this->access->sharedNodeIds($actor);

        if ($candidateIds === []) {
            /** @var Collection<int, Node> $empty */
            $empty = new Collection;

            return $empty;
        }

        $base = $this->query()
            ->whereNull('trashed_at')
            ->with('storage');

        /** @var Collection<int, Node> $candidates */
        $candidates = $this->whereKeyInBounded($base, $candidateIds)->get();

        /** @var Collection<int, Node> $visible */
        $visible = new Collection($this->filterViewable($actor, $candidates));

        return $visible;
    }

    /**
     * Whether the access-aware grant narrowing applies to a listing. It does ONLY
     * when the 'grants' feature is on AND the active permission driver is
     * {@see GrantAuthoritativeDriver} with {@see GrantAuthoritativeDriver::isGrantAuthoritative()}
     * true — i.e. treats v_node_grants as the SOLE authority for read-visibility (the
     * standalone {@see DatabasePermissionDriver}).
     *
     * The gate keys on the CAPABILITY, NOT on the driver KEY string: a host that
     * SUBCLASSES DatabasePermissionDriver under the same 'database' key to add a
     * role/team lane or a super-admin override() confers access on nodes with NO grant
     * anchor — so it overrides isGrantAuthoritative() to return false (the interface is
     * inherited and cannot be un-declared), and the listing stays OPEN. For the
     * gate/spatie/bridge/null drivers the host's roles govern and v_node_grants is not
     * the source of truth, so a grant-id constraint would WRONGLY hide nodes the host
     * role lane allows; they don't implement the capability either ⇒ listing stays OPEN
     * (the safe default that never wrongly hides).
     *
     * Public so a caller listing a page through a NON-queryForUser path (the children
     * cursor, the admin table) can decide whether to narrow the query to the
     * candidate set up front.
     */
    public function grantFilteringApplies(): bool
    {
        $driver = $this->drivers->driver();

        return Config::featureEnabled('grants')
            && $driver instanceof GrantAuthoritativeDriver
            && $driver->isGrantAuthoritative();
    }

    /**
     * The actor's candidate accessible node ids: the grant anchors UNION the
     * descendants of every SUBTREE-scoped anchor. Item-scoped anchors contribute
     * only their own node. A SUPERSET — see {@see queryForUser()}.
     *
     * PUBLIC (F-P1.10-01): {@see constrainToAccessible()} narrows a query by the
     * NODE model's own primary key, which only fits a Node-shaped listing. The
     * admin panel's non-Node resources (grant/share/activity/storage) key off a
     * DIFFERENT column (node_id / target_id / root_node_id), so they call this
     * directly to build their own `whereIn` — same candidate set, same
     * grantFilteringApplies() gate, no duplicated grant-resolution logic.
     *
     * @return list<int|string>
     */
    public function candidateNodeIds(Authorizable $actor): array
    {
        $subjects = $this->drivers->driver()->subjectsFor($actor);
        $anchors = $this->grants->allowAnchorsFor(subjects: $subjects, now: Carbon::now());

        if ($anchors->isEmpty()) {
            return [];
        }

        /** @var array<string, int|string> $ids */
        $ids = [];
        /** @var array<string, int|string> $subtreeAnchorIds */
        $subtreeAnchorIds = [];

        foreach ($anchors as $anchor) {
            $ids[Identity::stringify($anchor->node_id)] = $anchor->node_id;

            if ($anchor->scope === GrantScope::Subtree) {
                // Dedup by stringified key: the same subtree anchor can appear under
                // several subjects, but it seeds the descent exactly once.
                $subtreeAnchorIds[Identity::stringify($anchor->node_id)] = $anchor->node_id;
            }
        }

        foreach ($this->descendantIdsOf(array_values($subtreeAnchorIds)) as $descendantId) {
            $ids[Identity::stringify($descendantId)] = $descendantId;
        }

        return array_values($ids);
    }

    /**
     * The descendant node ids BELOW the given subtree anchors, via the staudenmeir
     * recursive CTE, bounded by withMaxDepth — H.4, never whereHas('descendants') /
     * withCount('descendants'). KEY-ONLY: the only full models hydrated are the anchors
     * themselves (bounded by the actor's grant count, NOT the subtree size); each
     * anchor's descendant subtree is pulled with ->pluck(key) — node KEYS, never
     * hydrated Node models — so a wide subtree never inflates memory.
     *
     * One recursive descent per anchor: the Node model REPURPOSES the staudenmeir
     * treeOf scope as a storage filter (scopeTreeOf(storageId)), so the multi-root
     * single-seed descent is not available here; the per-anchor loop stays, but the
     * anchor set is already deduped by the caller and only keys are read.
     *
     * @param  list<int|string> $anchorIds
     * @return list<int|string>
     */
    private function descendantIdsOf(array $anchorIds): array
    {
        if ($anchorIds === []) {
            return [];
        }

        $model = Config::nodeModel();
        $keyName = (new $model)->getKeyName();

        /** @var Collection<int, Node> $anchors */
        $anchors = $this->whereKeyInBounded($model::query(), $anchorIds)->get();

        /** @var list<int|string> $ids */
        $ids = [];

        foreach ($anchors as $anchor) {
            $this->metrics->histogram(
                name: 'vaulter_tree_cte_anchors',
                value: 1,
                labels: ['tier' => LoadTier::label()],
            );

            /** @var list<int|string> $descendantKeys */
            $descendantKeys = $model::withMaxDepth(
                self::DEFAULT_MAX_DEPTH,
                static fn (): array => $anchor->descendants()->pluck($keyName)->all(),
            );

            foreach ($descendantKeys as $descendantKey) {
                $ids[] = $descendantKey;
            }
        }

        return $ids;
    }

    /**
     * Bound the ID list's contribution to the statement-wide parameter count.
     * OR-ing whereIn chunks still binds every ID in one statement. Above the small
     * set budget, Laravel's connection escape() safely quotes each value through
     * the read PDO driver. No integer casts: ULIDs and bigint strings retain their
     * exact values. The predicate remains one AND-ed IN condition, so existing
     * storage/scopes, ordering and SQL cursor pagination keep their semantics.
     *
     * @template TModel of Model
     *
     * @param  Builder<TModel>  $query
     * @param  list<int|string> $ids
     * @return Builder<TModel>
     */
    private function whereKeyInBounded(Builder $query, array $ids): Builder
    {
        $keyName = $query->getModel()->getKeyName();

        if (count($ids) <= self::WHERE_IN_BIND_LIMIT) {
            return $query->whereIn($keyName, $ids);
        }

        return $query->whereRaw(new EscapedKeySet($keyName, $ids));
    }

    /**
     * @return Builder<Node>
     */
    private function query(): Builder
    {
        $model = Config::nodeModel();

        return $model::query();
    }
}

<<<M FILE packages/core/src/Schema/UlidIds.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Schema;

use Illuminate\Database\Eloquent\Concerns\HasUlids;
use Illuminate\Database\Schema\Blueprint;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;
use Vaulter\Contracts\IdStrategy;

/**
 * Lexicographically sortable ULID keys (26-char Crockford base32). The default
 * strategy (D9) — its morph keys line up with the Corex/host authorization ecosystem.
 */
final class UlidIds implements IdStrategy
{
    public function key(Blueprint $table, string $column = 'id'): void
    {
        // Declare the PRIMARY KEY as an explicit command at key() time rather than a
        // fluent ->primary() modifier. Laravel appends fluent indexes LAST (after the
        // table's foreign-key commands), so on PostgreSQL a SELF-referencing FK added in
        // the same create (v_nodes.parent_id → v_nodes.id) would be compiled BEFORE the
        // PK and rejected with "no unique constraint matching given keys". An explicit
        // command keeps the PK ahead of the foreign keys. (bigIncrements is immune — its
        // PK is inlined into CREATE TABLE.)
        $table->char(column: $column, length: 26);
        $table->primary($column);
    }

    public function reference(Blueprint $table, string $column, bool $nullable = false): void
    {
        $table->char(column: $column, length: 26)->nullable(value: $nullable)->index();
    }

    public function actor(Blueprint $table, string $column, bool $nullable = false): void
    {
        $table->char(column: $column, length: 26)->nullable(value: $nullable);
    }

    public function cast(): string
    {
        return 'string';
    }

    /**
     * @return class-string
     */
    public function modelConcern(): string
    {
        return HasUlids::class;
    }

    public function newId(): string
    {
        return (string) Str::ulid();
    }
}

<<<D FILE packages/core/src/Support/AzgardConfig.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Support;

use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Ability;

/**
 * Typed accessors over config('vaulter.azgard.*') — the AzGuard host-role lane's
 * Ability→permission map (master plan §6 / H.2). Unlike the Gate/Spatie maps (keyed
 * by GrantLevel), AzGuard is action-centric, so the {@see AzgardPermissionDriver}
 * maps a requested {@see Ability} to an AzGuard permission key (e.g. View →
 * documents.view) and asks the {@see AzgardGuard} that permission.
 * Plain strings — cache-safe, no closures.
 */
final class AzgardConfig
{
    /**
     * The Ability-value → AzGuard-permission-key map. The resolver maps the requested
     * ability through this before asking the guard; an ability with no mapping
     * contributes no decision.
     *
     * @return array<string, string>
     */
    public static function permissionMap(): array
    {
        $value = config('vaulter.azgard.permissions', self::defaults());

        if (!is_array($value)) {
            return self::defaults();
        }

        $map = [];

        foreach ($value as $ability => $permission) {
            if (is_string($ability) && is_string($permission) && $permission !== '') {
                $map[$ability] = $permission;
            }
        }

        return $map === [] ? self::defaults() : $map;
    }

    /**
     * The AzGuard permission gating node creation (the canCreateInWorkspace lane),
     * checked via hasPermissionIn against the workspace morph. Defaults to
     * 'documents.create'.
     */
    public static function createPermission(): string
    {
        $value = config('vaulter.azgard.create_permission', 'documents.create');

        return is_string($value) && $value !== '' ? $value : 'documents.create';
    }

    /**
     * The AzGuard permission key for a single ability, or null when the ability is
     * unmapped. The lookup the resolver runs per requested ability.
     */
    public static function permissionFor(Ability $ability): ?string
    {
        return self::permissionMap()[$ability->value] ?? null;
    }

    /**
     * The built-in Ability → AzGuard-permission defaults (master plan §6). View/
     * Download/Comment/Edit/Create map to their own verbs; Move/Copy fold into
     * documents.update (re-parent = an update), Trash/Delete into documents.delete,
     * and Share/Manage into documents.manage.
     *
     * @return array<string, string>
     */
    private static function defaults(): array
    {
        return [
            Ability::View->value => 'documents.view',
            Ability::Download->value => 'documents.download',
            Ability::Comment->value => 'documents.comment',
            Ability::Edit->value => 'documents.update',
            Ability::Create->value => 'documents.create',
            Ability::Move->value => 'documents.update',
            Ability::Copy->value => 'documents.update',
            Ability::Trash->value => 'documents.delete',
            Ability::Delete->value => 'documents.delete',
            Ability::Restore->value => 'documents.delete',
            Ability::Share->value => 'documents.manage',
            Ability::Manage->value => 'documents.manage',
        ];
    }
}

        $class = config('vaulter.models.webhook_delivery', WebhookDelivery::class);

        return $class;
    }

    /**
     * The HTTP request timeout (seconds) for a single webhook delivery POST
     * (§2.11). Floored at 1.
     */
    public static function webhookTimeout(): int
    {
        $value = config('vaulter.webhooks.timeout', 5);

        $seconds = is_numeric($value) ? (int) $value : 5;

        return max($seconds, 1);
    }

    /**
     * The total number of delivery attempts before a webhook delivery is parked
     * dead (DLQ, §2.11). Floored at 1.
     */
    public static function webhookMaxAttempts(): int
    {
        $value = config('vaulter.webhooks.max_attempts', 5);

        $attempts = is_numeric($value) ? (int) $value : 5;

        return max($attempts, 1);
    }

    /**
     * The backoff delay (seconds) before retrying after the given 1-based attempt
     * number failed (§2.11). Past the configured tail the last entry caps further
     * retries; an empty schedule means retry immediately (0).
     */
    public static function webhookBackoff(int $attempt): int
    {
        $schedule = config('vaulter.webhooks.backoff', [10, 30, 60, 300, 1800]);

        if (!is_array($schedule) || $schedule === []) {
            return 0;
        }

        $values = array_values(array_map(static fn (mixed $seconds): int => is_numeric($seconds) ? (int) $seconds : 0, $schedule));

        $index = max(0, $attempt - 1);

        return $values[$index] ?? $values[array_key_last($values)];
    }

    /**
     * The number of consecutive endpoint failures that flips an endpoint's
     * is_active off (the §2.11 circuit breaker). Floored at 1.
     */
    public static function webhookDisableAfterFailures(): int
    {
        $value = config('vaulter.webhooks.disable_after_failures', 10);

        $failures = is_numeric($value) ? (int) $value : 10;

        return max($failures, 1);
    }

    /**
     * The HMAC-SHA256 signature header name the delivery POST carries (§2.11).
     */
    public static function webhookSignatureHeader(): string
    {
        $value = config('vaulter.webhooks.signature_header', 'X-Vaulter-Signature');

        return is_string($value) && $value !== '' ? $value : 'X-Vaulter-Signature';

    /**

    /**

    /**
     * The SWAPPABLE outbound SSRF guard (§2.11 / D5 / F-P1.7-01). A host may point
     * config('vaulter.webhooks.delivery.url_guard') at its own implementation (e.g. one
     * that defers to an egress proxy). Only a valid OutboundUrlGuard FQCN is returned.
     *
     * @return class-string<OutboundUrlGuard>
     */
    public static function webhookUrlGuardClass(): string
    {
        $class = config('vaulter.webhooks.delivery.url_guard', DefaultOutboundUrlGuard::class);

        if (is_string($class) && is_a($class, OutboundUrlGuard::class, allow_string: true)) {
            /** @var class-string<OutboundUrlGuard> $class */
            return $class;
        }

        return DefaultOutboundUrlGuard::class;
    }

    /**
     * The URL schemes an outbound webhook may dial (§2.11 / N2). Lower-cased; defaults
     * to http + https. Anything else (file/gopher/ftp/…) is refused by the guard.
     *
     * @return list<string>
     */
    public static function webhookAllowedSchemes(): array
    {
        $value = config('vaulter.webhooks.delivery.allowed_schemes', ['http', 'https']);

        if (!is_array($value)) {
            return ['http', 'https'];
        }

        $schemes = [];

        foreach ($value as $scheme) {
            if (is_string($scheme) && $scheme !== '') {
                $schemes[] = strtolower($scheme);
            }
        }

        return $schemes === [] ? ['http', 'https'] : array_values(array_unique($schemes));
    }

    /**
     * The private/loopback/link-local/reserved CIDR ranges an outbound webhook must
     * NOT resolve into (§2.11 / N2). Closed by default; a host tightens or replaces it.
     *
     * @return list<string>
     */
    public static function webhookBlockedIpRanges(): array
    {
        return self::ipRanges('vaulter.webhooks.delivery.blocked_ip_ranges', self::DEFAULT_BLOCKED_IP_RANGES);
    }

    /**
     * The CIDR ranges a host EXPLICITLY re-opens for a trusted internal receiver
     * (§2.11 / N2). Empty by default — the guard's default is closed.
     *
     * @return list<string>
     */
    public static function webhookAllowedIpRanges(): array
    {
        return self::ipRanges('vaulter.webhooks.delivery.allowed_ip_ranges', []);
    }

    /**

    public static function webhookConnectTimeout(): int
    {
        $value = config('vaulter.webhooks.delivery.connect_timeout', 2);

    /**
     * The hard ceiling (bytes) on a receiver's response body (§2.11 / N2 / F-P1.7-06).
     * Delivery needs only the status, so a larger body is refused. Floored at 0
     * (0 disables the check); default 64 KiB.
     */
    public static function webhookMaxResponseBytes(): int
    {
        $value = config('vaulter.webhooks.delivery.max_response_bytes', 65536);

        $bytes = is_numeric($value) ? (int) $value : 65536;

        return max($bytes, 0);
    }

    /**
     * The claim window (seconds) a due retry's next_retry_at is bumped forward before
     * dispatch (§2.11 / F-P1.7-05) — the visibility timeout that keeps re-dispatch a
     * single owner. Floored at 1, default 60.
     */
    public static function webhookRetryClaimSeconds(): int
    {
        $value = config('vaulter.webhooks.retry_claim_seconds', 60);

        $seconds = is_numeric($value) ? (int) $value : 60;

        return max($seconds, 1);
    }

    /**
     * Read a config key of CIDR strings, falling back to $default when unset/!array.
     *
     * @param  list<string> $default
     * @return list<string>
     */
    private static function ipRanges(string $key, array $default): array
    {
        $value = config($key, $default);

        if (!is_array($value)) {
            return $default;
        }

        $ranges = [];

        foreach ($value as $range) {
            if (is_string($range) && $range !== '') {
                $ranges[] = $range;
            }
        }

        return $ranges;
    }

    /**
     * The hard ceiling (in bytes) on a resumable upload's declared total size
     * (§2.8 / M3a). A session whose total exceeds this is rejected at initiate; a
     * tus stream that overruns it is rejected at PATCH. 0 = unlimited.
     */
    public static function uploadMaxBytes(): int
    {
        $value = config('vaulter.uploads.max_bytes', 5_368_709_120); // 5 GiB

        $bytes = is_numeric($value) ? (int) $value : 5_368_709_120;

        return max($bytes, 0);
    }

    /**
     * The advertised default chunk size (in bytes) for a resumable upload (§2.8) —
     * a hint surfaced to clients; the server still accepts any PATCH/part size up to
     * the remaining bytes. Floored at 1.
     */
    public static function uploadChunkSize(): int
    {
        $value = config('vaulter.uploads.chunk_size', 8_388_608); // 8 MiB

        $bytes = is_numeric($value) ? (int) $value : 8_388_608;

        return max($bytes, 1);
    }

    /**
     * The hard ceiling (in bytes) on a SINGLE tus PATCH / part body (§2.8 / F-P1.4-04):
     * a memory/IO DoS lever kept DISTINCT from the chunk_size HINT so capping a request
     * never inflates the chunk size advertised to clients.
     *
     * It SHIPS ENABLED at 64 MiB (VLT-REMED P5.2 review): the default used to be 0 —
     * "cap disabled" — next to a 5 GiB max_bytes, so out of the box ONE authorized PATCH
     * could hand the worker a 5 GiB body. A ceiling that is only a ceiling when the host
     * remembers to switch it on is not a ceiling. Floored at 0 (never 1) so an explicit
     * 0 is still a real disable, not a 1-byte cap.
     */
    public static function uploadMaxChunkBytes(): int
    {
        $value = config('vaulter.uploads.max_chunk_bytes', 67_108_864); // 64 MiB

        $bytes = is_numeric($value) ? (int) $value : 67_108_864;

        return max($bytes, 0);
    }

    /**
     * The session TTL in hours (§2.8): a session not committed within this window is
     * swept (its staged temp + S3 multipart reclaimed, status → expired). The
     * initiate path sets expires_at = now + this. Floored at 1.
     */
    public static function uploadSessionTtlHours(): int
    {
        $value = config('vaulter.uploads.session_ttl_hours', 24);

        $hours = is_numeric($value) ? (int) $value : 24;

        return max($hours, 1);
    }

     * The hard cap on how many OPEN (initiated|uploading) sessions a single actor

    /**
     * The closed allow-list of resumable-upload metadata keys the server accepts
     * (§2.8 / F-P1.4-08): any key outside this list is dropped by the controller

    /**
     * The driver-key → FQCN map for the host-role drivers (H.2). Only valid

    public static function permissionDrivers(): array
    {

            return [];

        return $drivers;
    }

    /** @return 'string'|'bigint'|'uuid'|'ulid' */
    public static function hostKeyType(): string
    {
        $value = config('vaulter.ids.host_keys', 'string');

        if (!is_string($value) || !in_array($value, ['string', 'bigint', 'uuid', 'ulid'], true)) {
            $label = is_scalar($value) || $value === null ? (string) $value : get_debug_type($value);

            throw new \InvalidArgumentException('[Vaulter] Unknown vaulter.ids.host_keys ['.$label.']; expected string|bigint|uuid|ulid.');
        }

        return $value;
    }

    /**
     * The active id-strategy key (ulid|uuid7|bigint), default ulid (D9).
     *
     * Backward-compat: when ids.default is not explicitly set, derive it from
     * the legacy id_type (id->bigint, ulid->ulid). When both are present,
     * ids.default wins.
     */
    public static function idStrategy(): string
    {
        $explicit = config('vaulter.ids.default');

        if (is_string($explicit) && $explicit !== '') {
            return $explicit;
        }

        return self::idStrategyFromLegacyType();
    }

    /**
     * @return array<string, class-string<IdStrategy>>
     */
    public static function idStrategies(): array
    {
        $value = config('vaulter.ids.strategies', []);

        if (!is_array($value)) {
            return [];
        }

        $strategies = [];

        foreach ($value as $key => $class) {
            if (is_string($key) && is_string($class) && is_a($class, IdStrategy::class, allow_string: true)) {
                $strategies[$key] = $class;
            }
        }

        /** @var array<string, class-string<IdStrategy>> $strategies */
        return $strategies;
    }

    /**
     * Legacy id_type values still drive published migrations and host models.
     * usesUlids() reflects the resolved strategy so it keeps working whether the
     * host configures id_type=ulid or the newer ids.default=ulid.
     */
    public static function usesUlids(): bool
    {
        return self::idStrategy() === 'ulid';
    }

    /**
     * Map the legacy id_type (id|ulid) onto an id-strategy key.
     */
    private static function idStrategyFromLegacyType(): string
    {
        return self::idType() === 'ulid' ? 'ulid' : 'bigint';
    }

    /**
     * The two-phase GC grace window in hours (H.3), floored at 1h so a tombstone
     * can never be swept before an in-flight multipart upload could resurrect it.

    public static function gcGraceHours(int $override = 0): int
    {
        $value = $override > 0 ? $override : config('vaulter.gc.grace_hours', 24);

        $hours = is_numeric($value) ? (int) $value : 24;

        return max($hours, 1);
    }

    /**
     * The orphan-object grace window in hours (H.3) — how old a bytes-without-a-row
     * object must be before the disk-walk treats it as a deletable orphan. An
     * in-flight commit promotes its bytes BEFORE its row is durable, so a fresh
     * object may be a commit-in-progress, not an orphan; this grace is deliberately
     * generous (a resumable upload can promote then commit much later). Defaults to
     * the GC grace, floored at 1h.
     */
    public static function orphanGraceHours(int $override = 0): int
    {
        $default = config('vaulter.gc.grace_hours', 24);

        $value = $override > 0 ? $override : config('vaulter.gc.orphan_grace_hours', $default);

        $hours = is_numeric($value) ? (int) $value : 24;

        return max($hours, 1);
    }

    /**

    }

    /**
     * The node id a collaboration room name resolves back to — the inverse of
     * {@see collaborationRoom()}. The webhook endpoints accept either the bare node id
     * or the full prefixed room and normalise through here so the Node hub may send
     * whichever it holds. Returns the input unchanged when it carries no prefix.
     */
    public static function nodeIdFromRoom(string $room): string
    {
        $prefix = self::channelPrefix().'.';

        if (str_starts_with($room, $prefix)) {
            return substr($room, strlen($prefix));
        }

        return $room;
    }

    /**
     * The shared secret the Node collaboration hub presents on the server-to-server
     * webhook endpoints (collab/authenticate, collab/store). Set via
     * VAULTER_COLLAB_WEBHOOK_SECRET. As of VLT-REMED P3.2 (F-P1.6-02) this key is ALSO
     * the HMAC key every webhook call's body-signature is verified against — null/empty
     * therefore means the webhook surface accepts NOTHING AT ALL (never open): neither
     * the secret-header path nor a JWT-bearer call can produce a valid signature
     * without it. See UPGRADE.md (breaking).

    public static function collaborationWebhookSecret(): ?string
    {
        $value = config('vaulter.collaboration.webhook_secret');

        return is_string($value) && $value !== '' ? $value : null;
    }

    /**

     * 300 — VLT-REMED P3.2 / F-P1.6-02, N2). Also doubles as the nonce TTL: a
     * signature seen again within this window is refused as a replay. Floored at 1.

    public static function collaborationWebhookTimestampTolerance(): int

    /**
     * The closed allow-list of MIME types a download may serve inline as-is
     * (P1.1 / F-P1.3-04, F-P1.11-03) — every entry lower-cased. A declared
     * `mime_type` outside this set is served as `application/octet-stream`
     * regardless of what the uploader claimed. Deliberately narrow and WITHOUT
     * any active-content type (`text/html`, `image/svg+xml`, `application/*+xml`):
     * those stay off the default so a stored file can never render as HTML/JS on
     * the app's own origin. Host-overridable via
     * config('vaulter.downloads.inline_mime_whitelist').
     *
     * @return list<string>
     */
    public static function downloadInlineMimeWhitelist(): array
    {
        $default = self::DEFAULT_DOWNLOAD_INLINE_MIME_WHITELIST;
        $configured = self::stringList(config('vaulter.downloads.inline_mime_whitelist', $default), $default);

        $mimes = [];

        foreach ($configured as $mime) {
            if ($mime !== '') {
                $mimes[] = strtolower($mime);
            }
        }

        return $mimes === [] ? $default : array_values(array_unique($mimes));
    }

    /**
     * The trash retention window in days (D17 / §2.10) before a trashed node's
     * subtree is permanently purged. Default 30, floored at 0 (0 = purge as soon
     * as a node is trashed).

    public static function trashRetentionDays(): int
    {
        $value = config('vaulter.trash.retention_days', 30);

        $days = is_numeric($value) ? (int) $value : 30;

        return max($days, 0);
    }

    /**
     * The registered document handler FQCNs (config('vaulter.handlers')) — the
     * format-extensibility registry source (§4.5 / H.5). Only valid FileHandler
     * subclasses are returned; the config stays FQCN-only (cache-safe — no closures),
     * so a runtime-registered format works with no migration and no core change.
     *
     * @return list<class-string<FileHandler>>
     */
    public static function documentHandlers(): array
    {
        $value = config('vaulter.handlers', []);

        if (!is_array($value)) {
            return [];
        }

        $handlers = [];

        foreach ($value as $class) {
            if (is_string($class) && is_a($class, FileHandler::class, allow_string: true)) {
                $handlers[] = $class;
            }
        }

        /** @var list<class-string<FileHandler>> $handlers */
        return $handlers;
    }

    /**
     * @return array<string, class-string<DocumentExporter>>
     */
    public static function exporters(): array
    {
        $value = config('vaulter.exporters', []);

        if (!is_array($value)) {
            return [];
        }

        $exporters = [];

        foreach ($value as $format => $class) {
            if (is_string($format) && is_string($class) && is_a($class, DocumentExporter::class, allow_string: true)) {
                $exporters[$format] = $class;
            }
        }

        /** @var array<string, class-string<DocumentExporter>> $exporters */
        return $exporters;
    }

    /**
     * Extra TipTap node types a host's own editor extensions produce
     * (config('vaulter.tiptap.extra_nodes'), VLT-REMED D27/D28). ADDITIVE: they are added
     * to the canon shipped in TipTapContent, never replace it — a host that could delete
     * `doc`/`text` from the allow-list would silently break every save.
     *
     * @return list<string>
     */
    public static function tiptapExtraNodes(): array
    {
        return self::stringList(config('vaulter.tiptap.extra_nodes', []), []);
    }

    /**
     * Extra TipTap mark types (config('vaulter.tiptap.extra_marks')). Additive — see
     * {@see tiptapExtraNodes()}.
     *
     * @return list<string>
     */
    public static function tiptapExtraMarks(): array
    {
        return self::stringList(config('vaulter.tiptap.extra_marks', []), []);
    }

    /**
     * Extra per-type TipTap attributes (config('vaulter.tiptap.extra_attributes')), keyed
     * by node/mark type. Additive — merged with the canon for that type, never replacing
     * it. Whatever a host adds here, the URL-bearing attributes among them stay
     * scheme-checked — see {@see tiptapUrlAttributes()}: extending the allow-list is host
     * taste, sanitising a URL is not (D28).
     *
     * @return array<string, list<string>>
     */
    public static function tiptapExtraAttributes(): array
    {
        return self::tiptapAttributeMap('extra_attributes');
    }

    /**
     * The per-type attributes a host declares as URL-BEARING
     * (config('vaulter.tiptap.url_attributes'), VLT-REMED P5.2 / R-11). Every attribute
     * named here goes through LinkSchemeValidator at store time AND on the JSON read path,
     * exactly like the package's own `link.href` / `image.src`.
     *
     * It exists because the extension seam (`extra_nodes` + `extra_attributes`) lets a host
     * declare attributes the package has never heard of, and the package cannot guess which
     * of them a browser will treat as a URL. It only has to be reached for attributes whose
     * NAME does not give them away — TipTapContent already infers the obvious ones (`src`,
     * `href`, …) so that a host which forgets this key still fails CLOSED.
     *
     * @return array<string, list<string>>
     */
    public static function tiptapUrlAttributes(): array
    {
        return self::tiptapAttributeMap('url_attributes');
    }

    /**
     * A `type => [attribute, …]` map from the tiptap config, with the non-string junk
     * dropped rather than trusted.
     *
     * @return array<string, list<string>>
     */
    private static function tiptapAttributeMap(string $key): array
    {
        $value = config('vaulter.tiptap.'.$key, []);

        if (!is_array($value)) {
            return [];
        }

        $attributes = [];

        foreach ($value as $type => $keys) {
            if (!is_string($type)) {
                continue;
            }
            if (!is_array($keys)) {
                continue;
            }
            $attributes[$type] = array_values(array_filter($keys, is_string(...)));
        }

        return $attributes;
    }

    /**
     * The registered storage panel provider FQCNs (config('vaulter.panels')).
     * Only valid ProfileProvider subclasses are returned; the config stays
     * FQCN-only (cache-safe — no closures).
     *
     * @return list<class-string<ProfileProvider>>
     */
    public static function panels(): array
    {
        $value = config('vaulter.panels', []);

        if (!is_array($value)) {
            return [];
        }

        $providers = [];

        foreach ($value as $class) {
            if (is_string($class) && is_a($class, ProfileProvider::class, allow_string: true)) {
                $providers[] = $class;
            }
        }

        /** @var list<class-string<ProfileProvider>> $providers */
        return $providers;
    }

    /**
     * The default storage panel provider FQCN (config('vaulter.default_panel')),
     * falling back to the built-in DefaultProfile.
     *
     * @return class-string<ProfileProvider>
     */
    public static function defaultPanel(): string
    {
        $class = config('vaulter.default_panel', DefaultProfile::class);

        if (is_string($class) && is_a($class, ProfileProvider::class, allow_string: true)) {
            return $class;
        }

        return DefaultProfile::class;
    }

    /**
     * Whether a global feature is enabled (config('vaulter.features.{name}')).
     * When a panel name is given, the panel's own resolution wins (panel override
     * → panel feature defaults), so a panel may enable/disable a feature locally.
     */
    public static function featureEnabled(string $feature, ?string $panel = null): bool
    {
        if ($panel !== null) {
            return app(ProfileRegistry::class)->get($panel)->featureEnabled($feature);
        }

        $value = config('vaulter.features.'.$feature);

        return is_bool($value) && $value;
    }

    /**
     * The max length bound for a Drive node name ({@see \Vaulter\Support\
     * DriveNameRules}, §2.2, P4.5 / F-P3.1-01). Reads
     * config('vaulter.drive.name_rules.max_length'), falling back to the
     * pre-P4.5 hardcoded default (255) when absent or non-numeric.
     */
    public static function driveNameMaxLength(): int
    {
        $value = config('vaulter.drive.name_rules.max_length', 255);

        return is_numeric($value) ? (int) $value : 255;
    }

    /**
     * The reject pattern (no `regex:` prefix) for a Drive node name — any name
     * matching this negated pattern fails validation ({@see \Vaulter\Support\
     * DriveNameRules}, §2.2, P4.5 / F-P3.1-01). Reads
     * config('vaulter.drive.name_rules.no_separators_pattern'), falling back to
     * the pre-P4.5 hardcoded default (reject forward/back slash) when absent or
     * non-string.
     */
    public static function driveNameSeparatorsPattern(): string
    {
        $value = config('vaulter.drive.name_rules.no_separators_pattern', '/^[^\/\\\\]+$/');

        return is_string($value) ? $value : '/^[^\/\\\\]+$/';
    }

    /**
     * @param  list<string> $default
     * @return list<string>
     */
    private static function stringList(mixed $value, array $default): array
    {
        if (!is_array($value)) {
            return $default;
        }

        $strings = [];

        foreach ($value as $item) {
            if (is_string($item)) {
                $strings[] = $item;
            }
        }

        return $strings;
    }
}

<<<D FILE packages/core/src/Testing/FakeAzgardGuard.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Testing;

use Vaulter\Contracts\Access\AzgardGuard;

/**
 * A configurable in-memory {@see AzgardGuard} so consumers (and this package's own
 * tests) can exercise the {@see AzgardPermissionDriver}
 * WITHOUT installing azguard/corex (master plan §6 / H.5 — the src/Testing seam). It
 * lives in src/Testing/ (not tests/) so hosts can reference it from their own suites.
 *
 * It models the three AzGuard answers as plain data:
 *   - a super-admin flag (the SuperAdmin wildcard);
 *   - a set of (entity-key, permission) scoped grants (the per-resource lane);
 *   - a set of (contextType, contextId, permission) workspace grants (the
 *     hasPermissionIn lane the resolver actually drives, since AccessScope is node-blind).
 *
 * Grant a permission "globally" by passing it to a workspace check the resolver runs;
 * grant SuperAdmin to short-circuit everything.
 */
final class FakeAzgardGuard implements AzgardGuard
{
    /**
     * @param bool                                    $superAdmin      the SuperAdmin wildcard
     * @param list<array{string, string}>             $scopedGrants    [entityKey, permission] pairs for the per-resource lane
     * @param list<array{string, int|string, string}> $workspaceGrants [contextType, contextId, permission] triples
     */
    public function __construct(
        private readonly bool $superAdmin = false,
        private readonly array $scopedGrants = [],
        private readonly array $workspaceGrants = [],
    ) {}

    public function hasScopedPermission(string $permission, object $entity): bool
    {
        if ($this->superAdmin) {
            return true;
        }

        $key = $this->entityKey($entity);

        foreach ($this->scopedGrants as [$grantedEntity, $grantedPermission]) {
            if ($grantedEntity === $key && $grantedPermission === $permission) {
                return true;
            }
        }

        return false;
    }

    public function hasPermissionIn(string $contextType, int|string $contextId, string $permission): bool
    {
        if ($this->superAdmin) {
            return true;
        }

        foreach ($this->workspaceGrants as [$grantedType, $grantedId, $grantedPermission]) {
            if (
                $grantedType === $contextType
                && (string) $grantedId === (string) $contextId
                && $grantedPermission === $permission
            ) {
                return true;
            }
        }

        return false;
    }

    public function isSuperAdmin(): bool
    {
        return $this->superAdmin;
    }

    /**
     * A fresh guard granting one workspace permission (the common "this actor may X in
     * this workspace" fixture), kept terse for table-driven tests.
     */
    public static function grantingWorkspace(string $contextType, int|string $contextId, string $permission): self
    {
        return new self(workspaceGrants: [[$contextType, $contextId, $permission]]);
    }

    /**
     * A fresh super-admin guard (the override fixture).
     */
    public static function superAdmin(): self
    {
        return new self(superAdmin: true);
    }

    /**
     * The stable key a scoped grant is matched on — the host's entity reduced to a
     * morph-style "<class>:<key>" string when it exposes getMorphClass()/getKey(),
     * else its spl object hash. Keeps the per-resource lane checkable without coupling
     * to a concrete model type.
     */
    private function entityKey(object $entity): string
    {
        if (method_exists($entity, 'getMorphClass') && method_exists($entity, 'getKey')) {
            /** @var string $morph */
            $morph = $entity->getMorphClass();
            /** @var int|string|null $key */
            $key = $entity->getKey();

            return $morph.':'.(string) $key;
        }

        return spl_object_hash($entity);
    }
}

<<<M FILE packages/core/src/Testing/NullPermissionDriver.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Testing;

use Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Access\Authorizable;
use Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\AccessScope;
use Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\Decision;
use Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\Subject;
use Vaulter\Contracts\Access\NonEnumeratingPermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Contracts\Access\NonProductionPermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Effect;

/**
 * The fail-loud OPEN host-role driver (master plan H.2 / D6″). It grants every
 * actor full access through an absolute Allow override, so a consumer can boot and
 * exercise Vaulter WITHOUT wiring a real role system.
 *
 * It is selectable ONLY outside production: the PermissionDriverManager rejects it
 * (MissingPermissionDriverException) when the app is in production, so it can never
 * silently open a production install. It lives in src/Testing/ (not tests/) so
 * consumers can reference it from their own test suites.
 */
final class NullPermissionDriver implements NonEnumeratingPermissionDriver, NonProductionPermissionDriver
{
    public function resolve(Subject $subject, Authorizable $actor, AccessScope $scope): ?Decision
    {
        // The open grant is expressed through the absolute override below, so the
        // per-subject role lane has nothing to add.
        return null;
    }

    public function override(Authorizable $actor, AccessScope $scope): ?Effect
    {
        // Absolute open: every actor is treated as a super-admin in non-prod, so the
        // ACL/role walk is short-circuited entirely (H.2 step 1).
        return Effect::Allow;
    }

    /**
     * @return list<Subject>
     */
    public function subjectsFor(Authorizable $actor): array
    {
        return [];
    }

    public function canCreateInWorkspace(Authorizable $actor, string $workspaceType, int|string $workspaceId): bool
    {
        return true;
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Illuminate\Support\Carbon;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Storage as StorageFacade;
use Vaulter\Access\PermissionDriverManager;
use Vaulter\Drive\Http\Resources\DriveResource;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Effect;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\GrantLevel;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\GrantScope;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Node;
use Vaulter\Repositories\Drive\NodeReadRepository;
use Vaulter\Tests\Access\AccessTestHelpers;
use Vaulter\Tests\Fixtures\Access\RoleSubjectGrantDriver;
use Vaulter\Tests\Fixtures\TestUser;

/**
 * Repository candidate prefilters and exact HTTP visibility are separate seams.
 * HTTP listings evaluate candidate pages through the batch ACL resolver and expose
 * a signed cursor without totals, including for the cross-storage shared endpoint.
 */
beforeEach(function (): void {
    StorageFacade::fake('local');
    // The standalone, grant-authoritative lane: v_node_grants is the sole authority,
    // so the listing may narrow to the candidate set.
    config()->set('vaulter.drivers.permission', 'database');
    $this->actingAs((new TestUser)->forceFill(['id' => 1]));
});

/**
 * Swap the active host-role driver to a fixture instance: bind it under a 'stub' key,
 * point config at it, and drop the memoised manager so the next resolve picks it up.
 */
function useListingDriver(object $driver): void
{
    app()->instance($driver::class, $driver);
    config()->set('vaulter.permission_drivers.stub', $driver::class);
    config()->set('vaulter.drivers.permission', 'stub');
    app()->forgetInstance(PermissionDriverManager::class);
    app()->forgetInstance(NodeReadRepository::class);
}

function nodeRepo(): NodeReadRepository
{
    return app(NodeReadRepository::class);
}

/**
 * Drop the acting user the beforeEach set, so the next HTTP request resolves
 * $request->user() === null (a genuine guest) — the no-actor path the controller /
 * resource guard against.
 */
function actAsGuest(): void
{
    auth()->guard()->forgetUser();
    auth()->forgetGuards();
}

// ── 1. index = the candidate set: subtree-anchor descendants in, an un-granted sibling out.
it('index lists the subtree-anchor descendants and hides an un-granted sibling', function (): void {
    $storage = AccessTestHelpers::storage();

    // A subtree grant on the ANCHOR folder (no direct grant on its children) reaches
    // every descendant; the SIBLING tree has no grant at all. An ITEM grant on the
    // root makes the root itself viewable (so the index View-guard on the parent passes)
    // WITHOUT seeding the root's whole subtree as candidates — only the anchor lane is.
    $root = $storage->rootNode()->first();
    $anchor = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'anchor');
    $child = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, $anchor, 'child');
    $sibling = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'sibling');

    AccessTestHelpers::grant($root, GrantLevel::Reader, scope: GrantScope::Item);
    AccessTestHelpers::grant($anchor, GrantLevel::Reader, scope: GrantScope::Subtree);

    // Listing the anchor's children surfaces the descendant (reached via the ancestor
    // subtree anchor, no direct grant of its own).
    $this->getJson('api/vaulter/storages/'.$storage->getKey().'/nodes?parent_id='.$anchor->getKey())
        ->assertOk()
        ->assertJsonCount(1, 'data')
        ->assertJsonPath('data.0.id', $child->getKey());

    // Listing the ROOT surfaces the anchor (a candidate), but NOT the un-granted sibling.
    $rootIds = collect($this->getJson('api/vaulter/storages/'.$storage->getKey().'/nodes')->assertOk()->json('data'))
        ->pluck('id')->all();

    expect($rootIds)->toContain($anchor->getKey())
        ->and($rootIds)->not->toContain($sibling->getKey());
});

// ── 2. an item-scoped anchor yields zero candidate children; the folder itself still opens.
it('lists zero children for an item-scoped folder grant while the folder itself still views', function (): void {
    $storage = AccessTestHelpers::storage();
    $folder = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'item-only');
    $child = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, $folder, 'inside');

    // ITEM scope = that node ONLY: the folder is a candidate, its child is not.
    AccessTestHelpers::grant($folder, GrantLevel::Reader, scope: GrantScope::Item);

    // The folder's children listing is EMPTY (the child is no candidate)…
    $this->getJson('api/vaulter/storages/'.$storage->getKey().'/nodes?parent_id='.$folder->getKey())
        ->assertOk()
        ->assertJsonCount(0, 'data');

    // …yet View/show of the folder ITSELF works (it is the item-scoped candidate).
    $this->getJson('api/vaulter/nodes/'.$folder->getKey())
        ->assertOk()
        ->assertJsonPath('data.id', $folder->getKey());

    expect($child)->not->toBeNull(); // (the child exists; it is simply not a candidate)
});

// ── 3. GET shared: cross-storage allow-grants both appear.
it('returns cross-storage allow-grants in the shared view', function (): void {
    $storageA = AccessTestHelpers::storage();
    $folderA = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storageA, null, 'in-a');
    AccessTestHelpers::grant($folderA, GrantLevel::Reader, scope: GrantScope::Item);

    $storageB = AccessTestHelpers::storage();
    $folderB = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storageB, null, 'in-b');
    AccessTestHelpers::grant($folderB, GrantLevel::Reader, scope: GrantScope::Item);

    $ids = collect($this->getJson('api/vaulter/shared')->assertOk()->json('data'))->pluck('id')->all();

    expect($ids)->toContain($folderA->getKey())
        ->and($ids)->toContain($folderB->getKey());
});

// ── 4. GET shared is EXACT: a nearer deny removes a row; an expired allow is excluded.
it('excludes a deny-revoked row and an expired allow from the shared view (exact)', function (): void {
    $storage = AccessTestHelpers::storage();

    // A subtree allow on the parent flows to the child… but a nearer deny on the child
    // revokes it (the exact re-resolution drops the child, keeps the parent).
    $parent = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'parent');
    $child = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, $parent, 'child');
    AccessTestHelpers::grant($parent, GrantLevel::Reader, scope: GrantScope::Subtree);
    AccessTestHelpers::grant($child, GrantLevel::Reader, effect: Effect::Deny, scope: GrantScope::Item);

    // An EXPIRED allow never reaches the shared view (read-time expiry).
    $expired = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'expired');
    AccessTestHelpers::grant(
        $expired,
        GrantLevel::Reader,
        scope: GrantScope::Item,
        expiresAt: Carbon::now()->subHour(),
    );

    $ids = collect($this->getJson('api/vaulter/shared')->assertOk()->json('data'))->pluck('id')->all();

    expect($ids)->toContain($parent->getKey())
        ->and($ids)->not->toContain($child->getKey())
        ->and($ids)->not->toContain($expired->getKey());
});

// ── 5. GET shared unauthenticated ⇒ empty (not 500); the envelope is a bounded page.
it('returns an empty bounded page for an unauthenticated shared request', function (): void {
    // A grant exists for user 1, but THIS request has no actor — so the shared view
    // must see nothing (the no-actor path), never error, never leak the granted node.
    $storage = AccessTestHelpers::storage();
    AccessTestHelpers::grant(
        AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'secret'),
        GrantLevel::Reader,
        scope: GrantScope::Item,
    );

    actAsGuest();

    $this->getJson('api/vaulter/shared')
        ->assertOk()
        ->assertJsonCount(0, 'data')
        // No actor means no continuation cursor or hidden-node total.
        ->assertJsonPath('meta.next_cursor', null)
        ->assertJsonMissingPath('meta.total');
});

it('wraps the shared view in an exact cursor envelope', function (): void {
    $storage = AccessTestHelpers::storage();
    $folder = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'shared-one');
    AccessTestHelpers::grant($folder, GrantLevel::Reader, scope: GrantScope::Item);

    $this->getJson('api/vaulter/shared')
        ->assertOk()
        ->assertJsonPath('meta.next_cursor', null)
        ->assertJsonMissingPath('meta.total')
        ->assertJsonCount(1, 'data');
});

it('GET shared advertises a cursor envelope without offset totals', function (): void {
    $storage = AccessTestHelpers::storage();
    $folder = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'offset-contract');
    AccessTestHelpers::grant($folder, GrantLevel::Reader, scope: GrantScope::Item);

    $response = $this->getJson('api/vaulter/shared')->assertOk();

    expect($response->json('meta'))
        ->toHaveKeys(['next_cursor', 'prev_cursor', 'per_page', 'scanned'])
        ->not->toHaveKey('total')
        ->not->toHaveKey('current_page');
});

// ── 6. The public repository seam: queryForUser + constrainToAccessible.
it('constrains an item anchor to only its own node via the repository seam', function (): void {
    $storage = AccessTestHelpers::storage();
    $folder = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'item');
    AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, $folder, 'descendant'); // not a candidate (item scope)
    AccessTestHelpers::grant($folder, GrantLevel::Reader, scope: GrantScope::Item);

    $ids = nodeRepo()->queryForUser(AccessTestHelpers::user())->pluck('id')->all();

    expect($ids)->toBe([$folder->getKey()]);
});

it('constrains a subtree anchor to the anchor plus all its descendants', function (): void {
    $storage = AccessTestHelpers::storage();
    $anchor = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'anchor');
    $childA = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, $anchor, 'a');
    $grandchild = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, $childA, 'a-1');
    $outside = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'outside');

    AccessTestHelpers::grant($anchor, GrantLevel::Reader, scope: GrantScope::Subtree);

    $ids = nodeRepo()->queryForUser(AccessTestHelpers::user())->pluck('id')->all();

    expect($ids)->toContain($anchor->getKey(), $childA->getKey(), $grandchild->getKey())
        ->and($ids)->not->toContain($outside->getKey())
        ->and($ids)->toHaveCount(3);
});

it('forces an empty result (not the whole table) when the actor reaches no candidate', function (): void {
    $storage = AccessTestHelpers::storage();
    AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'unreachable'); // exists, but no grant

    // constrainToAccessible on a raw live-nodes base → empty, NOT the full table.
    $base = Node::query()->whereNull('trashed_at');
    $ids = nodeRepo()->constrainToAccessible($base, AccessTestHelpers::user())->pluck('id')->all();

    expect($ids)->toBe([]);
});

// ── 7. Subject breadth: a grant addressed to the actor's ROLE subject is included.
it('includes a grant addressed to the actor role subject in the candidate set', function (): void {
    $storage = AccessTestHelpers::storage();
    $roleFolder = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'role-granted');
    $userFolder = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'user-granted');

    // A grant addressed to the ROLE subject (type 'role', id 7) — NOT the user directly.
    AccessTestHelpers::grant(
        $roleFolder,
        GrantLevel::Reader,
        scope: GrantScope::Item,
        subjectId: 7,
        subjectType: 'role',
    );
    // A control grant addressed to the user directly.
    AccessTestHelpers::grant($userFolder, GrantLevel::Reader, scope: GrantScope::Item);

    // The driver expands the actor into [user, role:7] — both grants are candidates.
    useListingDriver(new RoleSubjectGrantDriver(roleType: 'role', roleId: 7));

    $ids = nodeRepo()->queryForUser(AccessTestHelpers::user())->pluck('id')->all();

    expect($ids)->toContain($roleFolder->getKey())
        ->and($ids)->toContain($userFolder->getKey());
});

// ── 9. Per-node ACTION gating stays EXACT even though the node lists (candidate superset).
it('refuses the action on a deny-vetoed node that still appears in the candidate listing', function (): void {
    $storage = AccessTestHelpers::storage();
    $parent = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'subtree');
    $child = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, $parent, 'vetoed');

    // A subtree allow on the parent makes BOTH parent and child candidates (the listing
    // is a superset); a nearer deny on the child revokes its exact access.
    AccessTestHelpers::grant($parent, GrantLevel::Reader, scope: GrantScope::Subtree);
    AccessTestHelpers::grant($child, GrantLevel::Reader, effect: Effect::Deny, scope: GrantScope::Item);

    // The child IS in the candidate listing (superset — deny not applied in listing SQL).
    $listed = nodeRepo()->queryForUser(AccessTestHelpers::user())->pluck('id')->all();
    expect($listed)->toContain($child->getKey());

    // …but the per-ACTION gate is EXACT: show on the deny-vetoed child is refused (403).
    $this->getJson('api/vaulter/nodes/'.$child->getKey())->assertStatus(403);

    // The non-vetoed parent still shows (sanity — only the vetoed node is gated).
    $this->getJson('api/vaulter/nodes/'.$parent->getKey())->assertOk();
});

// ── 10. DriveResource.abilities mirror the resolver (view-only, create gate, null actor).
it('exposes view-only storage abilities for a reader on the root', function (): void {
    $storage = AccessTestHelpers::storage();
    $root = $storage->rootNode()->first();

    // Reader on the root: view true, create_folder/upload/manage false.
    AccessTestHelpers::grant($root, GrantLevel::Reader, scope: GrantScope::Subtree);

    $this->getJson('api/vaulter/storages/'.$storage->getKey())
        ->assertOk()
        ->assertJsonPath('data.abilities.view', true)
        ->assertJsonPath('data.abilities.create_folder', false)
        ->assertJsonPath('data.abilities.upload', false)
        ->assertJsonPath('data.abilities.manage', false);
});

it('refuses the storage show for an unauthenticated request on a rooted storage', function (): void {
    $storage = AccessTestHelpers::storage();
    // An Owner grant for user 1 WOULD flip every flag true — but THIS request has no
    // actor, so the controller's View-guard on the rooted storage's root refuses it
    // (no actor ⇒ no grant ⇒ 403). The storage meta must never reach a guest, so there
    // is no `data` body to inspect — the all-false-abilities CONTRACT for a null actor
    // is pinned at the Resource layer below (it can no longer be reached through the
    // guarded controller on a rooted storage).
    AccessTestHelpers::grant($storage->rootNode()->first(), GrantLevel::Owner, scope: GrantScope::Subtree);

    actAsGuest();

    $this->getJson('api/vaulter/storages/'.$storage->getKey())
        ->assertStatus(403);
});

// ── 10b. The all-false-abilities CONTRACT for a NULL actor, re-expressed at the layer
// that still reaches it: DriveResource resolves every flag false when the request has
// no acting user, regardless of an Owner grant on the root. (The controller guard now
// 403s a guest on a rooted storage BEFORE the Resource renders — see the test above —
// so this contract lives at the Resource seam, not behind the controller.)
it('renders all-false storage abilities for a null actor at the Resource layer', function (): void {
    $storage = AccessTestHelpers::storage();
    // An Owner grant for user 1 WOULD flip every flag true for THAT actor — but a request
    // with no user must yield the read-only-shell default (all false), the SAFE default.
    AccessTestHelpers::grant($storage->rootNode()->first(), GrantLevel::Owner, scope: GrantScope::Subtree);

    // A bare request resolves $request->user() === null — the no-actor path.
    $abilities = DriveResource::make($storage->refresh())->toArray(Request::create('/'))['abilities'];

    expect($abilities)->toBe([
        'view' => false,
        'create_folder' => false,
        'upload' => false,
        'manage' => false,
    ]);
});

// ── 11. Driver-aware gate: a non-GrantAuthoritativeDriver keeps the listing OPEN.
it('keeps grantFilteringApplies true on the database driver and false on the null driver', function (): void {
    // database driver carries the GrantAuthoritativeDriver marker ⇒ filtering applies.
    expect(nodeRepo()->grantFilteringApplies())->toBeTrue();

    // The null driver does NOT carry the marker ⇒ filtering does not apply.
    config()->set('vaulter.drivers.permission', 'null');
    app()->forgetInstance(PermissionDriverManager::class);
    app()->forgetInstance(NodeReadRepository::class);

    expect(nodeRepo()->grantFilteringApplies())->toBeFalse();
});

it('keeps the listing OPEN (every node) on the null driver', function (): void {
    $storage = AccessTestHelpers::storage();
    $a = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'a');
    $b = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'b');
    // No grants at all — on the open driver the listing must still return every node.

    config()->set('vaulter.drivers.permission', 'null');
    app()->forgetInstance(PermissionDriverManager::class);
    app()->forgetInstance(NodeReadRepository::class);

    // queryForUser is a no-op on the open driver: the un-granted nodes are all present.
    $ids = nodeRepo()->queryForUser(AccessTestHelpers::user())->pluck('id')->all();

    expect($ids)->toContain($a->getKey())
        ->and($ids)->toContain($b->getKey());

    // The HTTP children listing is also open — both root folders list with no grant.
    $rootIds = collect(
        $this->getJson('api/vaulter/storages/'.$storage->getKey().'/nodes')->assertOk()->json('data'),
    )->pluck('id')->all();

    expect($rootIds)->toContain($a->getKey(), $b->getKey());
});

// ── 12. Scale/chunking smoke: a modest fan-out lists complete through whereIn chunking.
it('lists a whole modest subtree fan-out through the chunked whereIn path', function (): void {
    $storage = AccessTestHelpers::storage();
    $anchor = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'anchor');

    $expected = [$anchor->getKey()];

    // ~30 descendants under the subtree anchor — proves the chunked whereIn descent is
    // complete without building a pathological (>999) tree.
    for ($i = 0; $i < 30; $i++) {
        $expected[] = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, $anchor, 'leaf-'.$i)->getKey();
    }

    AccessTestHelpers::grant($anchor, GrantLevel::Reader, scope: GrantScope::Subtree);

    $ids = nodeRepo()->queryForUser(AccessTestHelpers::user())->pluck('id')->all();

    sort($ids);
    sort($expected);

    expect($ids)->toBe($expected);
});

it('returns the shared view as a paginated envelope from the controller', function (): void {
    $storage = AccessTestHelpers::storage();
    AccessTestHelpers::grant(
        AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'one'),
        GrantLevel::Reader,
        scope: GrantScope::Item,
    );

    $this->getJson('api/vaulter/shared')
        ->assertOk()
        ->assertJsonStructure(['data', 'meta' => ['next_cursor', 'per_page', 'scanned']]);
});
