<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use Illuminate\Foundation\Auth\User;
use Vaulter\Access\AccessResolver;
use Vaulter\Access\Drivers\AzgardPermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\AccessScope;
use Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\Subject;
use Vaulter\Contracts\Access\AzgardGuard;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Ability;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Effect;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\GrantLevel;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\GrantScope;
use Vaulter\Support\AzgardConfig;
use Vaulter\Testing\FakeAzgardGuard;
use Vaulter\Tests\Access\AccessTestHelpers;

/**
 * The AzGuard host-role driver (§6 / H.2 / ADR-0007). It talks ONLY to the Vaulter-
 * owned AzgardGuard seam, so these tests bind a FakeAzgardGuard — NO azguard/corex is
 * installed. Real-ecosystem integration (binding a real AzgardGuard adapter delegating
 * to AzGuard hasScopedPermission / Corex ContextGuard hasPermissionIn, plus ulid morph
 * alignment) is a HOST step; this slice proves the driver logic against the seam.
 *
 * Covered: the Ability→permission map; hasPermissionIn gating the workspace-scoped role
 * lane; hasPermissionIn gating create; the SuperAdmin override; the composite order
 * (a workspace role grant raises access when no node-ACL row exists; a node-ACL deny
 * still vetoes through the AccessResolver, since the driver only RAISES access).
 */
beforeEach(function (): void {
    config()->set('vaulter.drivers.permission', 'azgard');
});

/**
 * Bind a FakeAzgardGuard as the host's AzgardGuard adapter (the container path the
 * driver falls to when the actor itself does not implement the seam).
 */
function bindAzgardGuard(AzgardGuard $guard): void
{
    app()->instance(AzgardGuard::class, $guard);
}

it('maps abilities to AzGuard permissions with the master-plan defaults', function (): void {
    expect(AzgardConfig::permissionFor(Ability::View))->toBe('documents.view')
        ->and(AzgardConfig::permissionFor(Ability::Download))->toBe('documents.download')
        ->and(AzgardConfig::permissionFor(Ability::Comment))->toBe('documents.comment')
        ->and(AzgardConfig::permissionFor(Ability::Edit))->toBe('documents.update')
        ->and(AzgardConfig::permissionFor(Ability::Create))->toBe('documents.create')
        ->and(AzgardConfig::permissionFor(Ability::Move))->toBe('documents.update')
        ->and(AzgardConfig::permissionFor(Ability::Copy))->toBe('documents.update')
        ->and(AzgardConfig::permissionFor(Ability::Trash))->toBe('documents.delete')
        ->and(AzgardConfig::permissionFor(Ability::Delete))->toBe('documents.delete')
        ->and(AzgardConfig::permissionFor(Ability::Share))->toBe('documents.manage')
        ->and(AzgardConfig::permissionFor(Ability::Manage))->toBe('documents.manage');
});

it('honours a host override of the ability map', function (): void {
    config()->set('vaulter.azgard.permissions', ['edit' => 'host.docs.write']);

    expect(AzgardConfig::permissionFor(Ability::Edit))->toBe('host.docs.write');
});

it('grants an absolute override from an AzGuard super-admin', function (): void {
    bindAzgardGuard(FakeAzgardGuard::superAdmin());

    $driver = app(AzgardPermissionDriver::class);
    $scope = new AccessScope(panel: 'default', workspaceType: 'project', workspaceId: 9);

    expect($driver->override(AccessTestHelpers::user(), $scope))->toBe(Effect::Allow);
});

it('defers (no override) when the actor is not a super-admin', function (): void {
    bindAzgardGuard(new FakeAzgardGuard);

    $driver = app(AzgardPermissionDriver::class);
    $scope = new AccessScope(panel: 'default', workspaceType: 'project', workspaceId: 9);

    expect($driver->override(AccessTestHelpers::user(), $scope))->toBeNull();
});

it('lets a super-admin see every node through the AccessResolver', function (): void {
    bindAzgardGuard(FakeAzgardGuard::superAdmin());

    $storage = AccessTestHelpers::storage();
    $folder = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'azgard-super');

    // No ACL grant at all, yet the super override short-circuits to full access.
    expect(app(AccessResolver::class)->can(AccessTestHelpers::user(), Ability::Manage, $folder))->toBeTrue();
});

it('maps a workspace-scoped AzGuard permission to a role-grant level', function (): void {
    // The host grants documents.update in this workspace → the actor gets a Writer
    // decision (Writer is gated by the Edit ability → documents.update).
    bindAzgardGuard(FakeAzgardGuard::grantingWorkspace('project', 1, 'documents.update'));

    $driver = app(AzgardPermissionDriver::class);
    $actor = AccessTestHelpers::user();
    $scope = new AccessScope(panel: 'default', workspaceType: 'project', workspaceId: 1);

    $decision = $driver->resolve(Subject::ofModel($actor), $actor, $scope);

    expect($decision)->not->toBeNull()
        ->and($decision->level)->toBe(GrantLevel::Writer)
        ->and($decision->isAllow())->toBeTrue();
});

it('composite order: a workspace role grant raises access when NO node-ACL row exists', function (): void {
    // documents.view granted in the workspace; there is no v_node_grants row, so the
    // access comes purely from the role lane (composite step 2, no step 1 ACL row).
    $storage = AccessTestHelpers::storage();
    $folder = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'role-only');

    // The guard's workspace grant must match THIS storage's owner morph (the workspace
    // coordinates the AccessScope derives from the storage owner) so hasPermissionIn hits.
    bindAzgardGuard(FakeAzgardGuard::grantingWorkspace($storage->owner_type, $storage->owner_id, 'documents.view'));

    $resolver = app(AccessResolver::class);

    expect($resolver->can(AccessTestHelpers::user(), Ability::View, $folder))->toBeTrue()
        // …but an ability the workspace never granted (edit) stays denied.
        ->and($resolver->can(AccessTestHelpers::user(), Ability::Edit, $folder))->toBeFalse();
});

it('composite order: a node-ACL deny still vetoes a workspace role grant via the AccessResolver', function (): void {
    $storage = AccessTestHelpers::storage();
    $parent = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'parent');
    $child = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, $parent, 'child');

    // The workspace role lane grants edit everywhere in this workspace…
    bindAzgardGuard(FakeAzgardGuard::grantingWorkspace($storage->owner_type, $storage->owner_id, 'documents.update'));

    // …but an explicit node-ACL deny on the child must veto it (H.2 step 5 — the role
    // lane can only RAISE access, never resurrect a denied bit).
    AccessTestHelpers::grant(
        $child,
        GrantLevel::Writer,
        effect: Effect::Deny,
        scope: GrantScope::Item,
    );

    $resolver = app(AccessResolver::class);

    expect($resolver->can(AccessTestHelpers::user(), Ability::Edit, $parent))->toBeTrue()
        ->and($resolver->can(AccessTestHelpers::user(), Ability::Edit, $child))->toBeFalse();
});

it('gates workspace creation through hasPermissionIn with the create permission', function (): void {
    bindAzgardGuard(FakeAzgardGuard::grantingWorkspace('project', 5, 'documents.create'));

    $driver = app(AzgardPermissionDriver::class);
    $actor = AccessTestHelpers::user();

    expect($driver->canCreateInWorkspace($actor, 'project', 5))->toBeTrue()
        ->and($driver->canCreateInWorkspace($actor, 'project', 6))->toBeFalse();
});

it('returns no role decision when the workspace grants nothing (pass-through with a guard)', function (): void {
    bindAzgardGuard(new FakeAzgardGuard);

    $driver = app(AzgardPermissionDriver::class);
    $actor = AccessTestHelpers::user();
    $scope = new AccessScope(panel: 'default', workspaceType: 'project', workspaceId: 1);

    expect($driver->resolve(Subject::ofModel($actor), $actor, $scope))->toBeNull()
        ->and($driver->override($actor, $scope))->toBeNull();
});

it('is a safe pass-through (no fatal) when no AzgardGuard is bound', function (): void {
    $driver = app(AzgardPermissionDriver::class);
    $actor = AccessTestHelpers::user();
    $scope = new AccessScope(panel: 'default', workspaceType: 'project', workspaceId: 1);

    expect($driver->resolve(Subject::ofModel($actor), $actor, $scope))->toBeNull()
        ->and($driver->override($actor, $scope))->toBeNull()
        ->and($driver->canCreateInWorkspace($actor, 'project', 1))->toBeFalse();
});

it('returns no role decision for a node-blind scope with no workspace coordinates', function (): void {
    bindAzgardGuard(FakeAzgardGuard::grantingWorkspace('project', 1, 'documents.view'));

    $driver = app(AzgardPermissionDriver::class);
    $actor = AccessTestHelpers::user();
    $scope = new AccessScope(panel: 'default'); // no workspaceType/workspaceId

    expect($driver->resolve(Subject::ofModel($actor), $actor, $scope))->toBeNull();
});

it('exposes only the actor in its subject-set (AzGuard enumerates no role subjects)', function (): void {
    $driver = app(AzgardPermissionDriver::class);
    $subjects = $driver->subjectsFor(AccessTestHelpers::user(id: 3));

    expect($subjects)->toHaveCount(1)
        ->and($subjects[0]->id)->toBe(3);
});

it('uses the actor itself as the guard when the actor implements the AzgardGuard seam', function (): void {
    // The cleaner duck-typed path: an actor that IS an AzgardGuard is used directly,
    // with no container binding. A super-admin actor short-circuits the override.
    $actor = new class extends User implements AzgardGuard
    {
        public $timestamps = false;

        protected $guarded = [];

        public function hasScopedPermission(string $permission, object $entity): bool
        {
            return false;
        }

        public function hasPermissionIn(string $contextType, int|string $contextId, string $permission): bool
        {
            return $permission === 'documents.create';
        }

        public function isSuperAdmin(): bool
        {
            return true;
        }
    };
    $actor->forceFill(['id' => 7]);
    $actor->exists = true;

    $driver = app(AzgardPermissionDriver::class);
    $scope = new AccessScope(panel: 'default', workspaceType: 'project', workspaceId: 1);

    expect($driver->override($actor, $scope))->toBe(Effect::Allow)
        ->and($driver->canCreateInWorkspace($actor, 'project', 1))->toBeTrue();
});

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Access\Authorizable;
use Vaulter\Access\Drivers\DatabasePermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Access\PermissionDriverManager;
use Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\Subject;
use Vaulter\Contracts\Access\NonEnumeratingPermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Exceptions\Access\MissingPermissionDriverException;
use Vaulter\Testing\NullPermissionDriver;

class ActorOnlyBoundaryDriver extends DatabasePermissionDriver implements NonEnumeratingPermissionDriver
{
    public function subjectsFor(Authorizable $actor): array
    {
        return parent::subjectsFor($actor);
    }
}

it('retains actor-only classification without naming an optional bridge', function (): void {
    $manager = app(PermissionDriverManager::class);

    expect($manager->enumeratesRoleSubjects(new ActorOnlyBoundaryDriver))->toBeFalse()
        ->and($manager->enumeratesRoleSubjects(new class extends ActorOnlyBoundaryDriver {}))->toBeFalse()
        ->and($manager->enumeratesRoleSubjects(new class extends ActorOnlyBoundaryDriver
        {
            public function subjectsFor(Authorizable $actor): array
            {
                return [...parent::subjectsFor($actor), new Subject(type: 'role', id: 9)];
            }
        }))->toBeTrue()
        ->and($manager->enumeratesRoleSubjects(new NullPermissionDriver))->toBeFalse();
});

it('rejects the open testing driver in production through a neutral contract', function (): void {
    config()->set('vaulter.permission_drivers.open', NullPermissionDriver::class);
    $manager = new PermissionDriverManager(container: app(), isProduction: true);

    expect(fn () => $manager->driver('open'))->toThrow(MissingPermissionDriverException::class);
});

it('rejects an uninstalled bridge driver as unknown', function (): void {
    $manager = app(PermissionDriverManager::class);

    expect(fn () => $manager->driver('azgard'))->toThrow(MissingPermissionDriverException::class);
});

<<<M FILE packages/core/tests/Access/PermissionDriverContractTest.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use Vaulter\Access\AccessResolver;
use Vaulter\Access\Drivers\DatabasePermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Access\Drivers\GatePermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Access\Drivers\SpatiePermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Access\PermissionDriverManager;
use Vaulter\Contracts\Access\PermissionDriver;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Ability;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Effect;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\GrantLevel;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\GrantScope;
use Vaulter\Tests\Access\AccessTestHelpers;
use Vaulter\Tests\Fixtures\Access\RoleStubDriver;

/**
 * The PermissionDriver contract test (master plan §12 / H.2): ANY driver that only
 * contributes the actor to the subject-set and adds no roles/override MUST yield
 * the SAME AccessResolver decision on a shared ACL fixture. This is the stub M2b's
 * Gate/Spatie/Azgard drivers reuse — pointing the resolver at each driver over one
 * fixture and asserting identical results.
 *
 * The fixture: a Writer subtree allow on a parent, a deny on a child. Every
 * "pass-through" driver (no override, no extra subjects, no role decision) must
 * agree: parent editable, child denied.
 */
function bindDriver(PermissionDriver $driver): AccessResolver
{
    app()->instance($driver::class, $driver);
    config()->set('vaulter.permission_drivers.contract', $driver::class);
    config()->set('vaulter.drivers.permission', 'contract');
    app()->forgetInstance(PermissionDriverManager::class);
    app()->forgetInstance(AccessResolver::class);

    return app(AccessResolver::class);
}

/**
 * @return array<string, bool>
 */
function decisionsOver(AccessResolver $resolver): array
{
    $actor = AccessTestHelpers::user();
    $storage = AccessTestHelpers::storage();
    $parent = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, null, 'parent');
    $child = AccessTestHelpers::folder($storage, $parent, 'child');

    AccessTestHelpers::grant($parent, GrantLevel::Writer, scope: GrantScope::Subtree);
    AccessTestHelpers::grant(
        $child,
        GrantLevel::Writer,
        effect: Effect::Deny,
        scope: GrantScope::Item,
    );

    return [
        'parent.edit' => $resolver->can($actor, Ability::Edit, $parent),
        'child.view' => $resolver->can($actor, Ability::View, $child),
        'child.edit' => $resolver->can($actor, Ability::Edit, $child),
    ];
}

/**
 * The shared truth the algorithm dictates on the fixture: parent editable, child
 * denied (deny-wins). EVERY pass-through driver must agree.
 */
function sharedFixtureTruth(): array
{
    return [
        'parent.edit' => true,
        'child.view' => false,
        'child.edit' => false,
    ];
}

it('yields identical decisions across pass-through host-role drivers on a shared fixture', function (): void {
    // The real standalone database driver…
    $databaseDecisions = decisionsOver(bindDriver(new DatabasePermissionDriver));

    // …and a stub driver that ALSO contributes only the actor, no roles/override.
    $stubDecisions = decisionsOver(bindDriver(new RoleStubDriver(
        roleLevel: null,
        overrideEffect: null,
        includeActor: true,
    )));

    expect($stubDecisions)->toBe($databaseDecisions)
        ->and($databaseDecisions)->toBe(sharedFixtureTruth());
});

/**
 * H.2 hardening: the SAME contract harness against EACH real M2b driver in
 * pass-through mode (no super ability/permission granted, no role-mapped abilities
 * granted, no spatie roles). Every driver must contribute only the actor to the
 * subject-set and add no role decision — so the AccessResolver decision is byte-for-
 * byte identical to the database lane on the shared ACL fixture.
 */
dataset('pass-through drivers', [
    'gate' => fn (): PermissionDriver => new GatePermissionDriver,
    'spatie' => fn (): PermissionDriver => new SpatiePermissionDriver,

]);

it('yields the shared-fixture truth for each real driver in pass-through', function (PermissionDriver $driver): void {
    expect(decisionsOver(bindDriver($driver)))->toBe(sharedFixtureTruth());
})->with('pass-through drivers');

arch('all package code declares strict types')

    ->toUseStrictTypes();

/**
 * E5.1 / F-P4.3-01 — declarative form kept for discoverability/grep (`toUse('App')`).
 * `App\*` never exists as an autoloadable class in the package's own dev/test
 * environment, so this namespace-graph check can never observe a real "uses" edge
 * (PestArch has nothing to resolve `App\*` against) — proven by the file-scan test
 * directly below, which is the test that ACTUALLY enforces the invariant (red-before
 * verified against an injected `use App\...;` fixture).
 */
arch('the package never depends on the host application (E5.1)')
    ->expect('Vaulter')
    ->not->toUse('App');

/**
 * E5.1 / F-P4.3-01 — vaulter-core is an embeddable Laravel package: it must never
 * reach into the HOST application's namespace. A stray `App\*` import (e.g.
 * copy-pasted from the consuming app while building a feature) breaks installability
 * in a clean host that does not carry that class.
 *
 * `Console/MakeProfileCommand.php` is a deliberate, allow-listed exception: it is a
 * scaffolding command (`make:vaulter-panel`) that EMITS the string `App\Vaulter\Panels`
 * as the target namespace for code it generates INTO the host application — the
 * package itself never imports or executes anything under `App\*`.
 */
test('non-test src never references the host App namespace (E5.1, F-P4.3-01)', function (): void {
    $src = __DIR__.'/../../src';
    $offenders = [];

    // Scaffolding commands legitimately emit `App\*` as a STRING (the namespace of
    // generated host code), never as a real import/dependency of the package itself.
    $allowlist = [
        'Console/MakeProfileCommand.php',
    ];

    /** @var Iterator<SplFileInfo> $files */
    $files = new RegexIterator(
        new RecursiveIteratorIterator(new RecursiveDirectoryIterator($src)),
        '/\.php$/',
    );

    foreach ($files as $file) {
        $relative = str_replace($src.'/', '', $file->getPathname());

        if (in_array($relative, $allowlist, true)) {
            continue;
        }

        $contents = file_get_contents($file->getPathname());

        if ($contents === false) {
            continue;
        }

        $code = '';

        foreach (token_get_all($contents) as $token) {
            if (is_array($token) && in_array($token[0], [T_COMMENT, T_DOC_COMMENT], true)) {
                continue;
            }

            $code .= is_array($token) ? $token[1] : $token;
        }

        if (preg_match('/\\bApp\\\\/', $code) === 1) {
            $offenders[] = $file->getPathname();
        }
    }

    expect($offenders)->toBe([]);
});

/**
 * Layering: HTTP controllers must never touch an Eloquent model STATICALLY
 * (Model::query/create/where/all/find/…) — persistence goes through repositories
 * and Actions (M1c-http note). Controllers may still type-hint a model for
 * route-model binding; this bans the static query/persistence entry points only.
 *
 * The model set is the concrete v_* models; the scan strips comments/docblocks so
 * the rule fires on real code, and anchors on `Model::<verb>(` so unrelated static
 * calls (Config::table(), NodeKind::File, …) never trip it.
 */
test('no HTTP controller statically queries an Eloquent model (M1c-http)', function (): void {
    $controllers = __DIR__.'/../../src/Http/Controllers';

    // Models now live under per-domain subfolders (Models/Drive, Models/Cas, …)
    // plus the cross-model Models/Concerns/ traits — recurse and keep the leaf
    // class names (the Concerns traits ride along harmlessly, they are never a
    // static-query target).
    /** @var Iterator<SplFileInfo> $modelFiles */
    $modelFiles = new RegexIterator(
        new RecursiveIteratorIterator(
            new RecursiveDirectoryIterator(__DIR__.'/../../src/Models'),
        ),
        '/\.php$/',
    );

    $models = collect(iterator_to_array($modelFiles))
        ->map(fn (SplFileInfo $f): string => $f->getBasename('.php'))
        ->unique()
        ->values()
        ->all();

    expect($models)->not->toBe([]);

    $verbs = 'query|create|where|all|find|findOrFail|firstOrFail|first|firstWhere|'
        .'insert|update|destroy|updateOrCreate|firstOrCreate|firstOrNew';
    $names = implode('|', array_map('preg_quote', $models));
    $pattern = "/\\b({$names})::({$verbs})\\s*\\(/";

    $offenders = [];

    /** @var Iterator<SplFileInfo> $files */
    $files = new RegexIterator(
        new RecursiveIteratorIterator(new RecursiveDirectoryIterator($controllers)),
        '/\.php$/',
    );

    foreach ($files as $file) {
        $contents = file_get_contents($file->getPathname());

        if ($contents === false) {
            continue;
        }

        // Strip comments + docblocks so the ban only fires on real code.
        $code = '';

        foreach (token_get_all($contents) as $token) {
            if (is_array($token) && in_array($token[0], [T_COMMENT, T_DOC_COMMENT], true)) {
                continue;
            }

            $code .= is_array($token) ? $token[1] : $token;
        }

        if (preg_match($pattern, $code) === 1) {
            $offenders[] = $file->getPathname();
        }
    }

    expect($offenders)->toBe([]);
});

/**
 * Domain-subfolder boundary (structural refactor): the previously-flat technical
 * roots are now split by domain — every class lives under a domain subfolder, with
 * a SHORT, explicit allow-list of cross-cutting classes that legitimately sit at
 * the technical root (the base exception, the cross-cutting IdStrategy contract,
 * the cross-model Concerns traits, and the swappable-models base namespace).
 *
 * The check: for each split root, every *.php directly in the root dir (depth 0)
 * must be an allowed root-citizen; everything else has been pushed one level down
 * into a domain folder.
 */
test('split technical roots keep classes in domain subfolders', function (): void {
    $src = __DIR__.'/../../src';

    // root => list of bare class names allowed to remain at the flat root.
    $rootsWithAllowed = [
        'Enums' => [],
        'Events' => [],
        'Models' => [], // Concerns/ is a subdir, not a depth-0 file.
        'Exceptions' => ['VaulterException'],
        'Repositories' => [],
        'Contracts' => ['IdStrategy'],
        // Revived in Phase D2 (P2 #5), kind-neutral naming in VLT-CANON P0.1: the
        // handler extensibility-seam VOs (FileDescriptor/ContentCapabilities/ViewerDescriptor/
        // NodePresentation) are kernel-shared — core's own Contracts\Handlers\*
        // interfaces type against them — so they live at Vaulter\ValueObjects\Handlers\*,
        // not in the extracted documents package. TipTapContent/LinkSchemeValidator/
        // OpaqueDocumentContent moved to Vaulter\Documents\ValueObjects\* (VLT-CANON
        // P0.3) — core no longer knows TipTap's shape.
        'ValueObjects' => [],
    ];

    $offenders = [];

    foreach ($rootsWithAllowed as $root => $allowed) {
        $dir = "{$src}/{$root}";

        foreach (scandir($dir) ?: [] as $entry) {
            if (!str_ends_with($entry, '.php')) {
                continue;
            }

            $class = substr($entry, 0, -4);

            if (!in_array($class, $allowed, true)) {
                $offenders[] = "{$root}/{$entry}";
            }
        }
    }

    expect($offenders)->toBe([]);
});

/**
 * ADR-0017 / VLT-REMED P4.9 — Canon A, Law 1 (layer-first placement).
 *
 * A recognized technical-layer directory (Actions/Models/Repositories/Enums/
 * Events/Data/Contracts/Http) must live as the FIRST namespace segment under the
 * package root — NEVER nested inside a domain module folder. `core` is the canon
 * reference and passes GREEN. The formerly-divergent `drive` layout (`Uploads/Actions`,
 * `Uploads/Models`, …) was the same rule; P4.10 discharged it (the layer subtrees
 * were dissolved into `Actions/Uploads`, `Models/Uploads`, …) and removed the
 * `->todo()` in drive's ArchTest.
 *
 * (Law 2 — "layers group by a domain sub-namespace, not flat" — is enforced by
 * the `split technical roots keep classes in domain subfolders` test above; the
 * formerly-flat `documents` layout was that rule, discharged by P4.10 with the
 * `->todo()` removed in documents.)
 *
 * `Http` sub-layers (Controllers/Requests/Resources/Middleware/Support) are
 * structural, not domains, so only `Http` itself is a layer segment here.
 */
test('technical layers are never nested under a domain module (ADR-0017 Law 1)', function (): void {
    $nested = layersNestedUnderDomain(__DIR__.'/../../src');

    // The public error contract intentionally lives alongside its exception family.
    expect(array_values(array_diff($nested, ['Exceptions/Contracts', 'Enums/Events'])))->toBe([])
        ->and(scandir(__DIR__.'/../../src/Exceptions/Contracts'))->toBe(['.', '..', 'ProblemException.php'])
        ->and(scandir(__DIR__.'/../../src/Enums/Events'))->toBe(['.', '..', 'EventType.php']);
});

/**
 * Walks $src and returns every layer-named directory that sits BELOW depth 0
 * (i.e. nested under a domain folder) — the Canon A / ADR-0017 Law 1 offenders.
 * Shared verbatim by the drive canon `->todo()` test.
 *
 * @return list<string> relative directory paths, e.g. "Uploads/Actions"
 */
function layersNestedUnderDomain(string $src): array
{
    $layers = ['Actions', 'Models', 'Repositories', 'Enums', 'Events', 'Data', 'Contracts', 'Http'];
    $offenders = [];

    // SELF_FIRST so DIRECTORIES are yielded (the default LEAVES_ONLY mode only
    // yields files, which would make this dir-structure check an inert no-op).
    /** @var Iterator<SplFileInfo> $dirs */
    $dirs = new RecursiveIteratorIterator(
        new RecursiveDirectoryIterator($src, FilesystemIterator::SKIP_DOTS),
        RecursiveIteratorIterator::SELF_FIRST,
    );

    foreach ($dirs as $dir) {
        if (!$dir->isDir()) {
            continue;
        }

        $relative = str_replace($src.'/', '', $dir->getPathname());
        $segments = explode('/', $relative);

        foreach ($segments as $index => $segment) {
            if ($index > 0 && in_array($segment, $layers, true)) {
                $offenders[] = $relative;
                break;
            }
        }
    }

    sort($offenders);

    return array_values(array_unique($offenders));
}

/**
 * The split domains live under the canonical domain set. Spot-check one class per
 * (root × domain) cell so a regression that drops a class back into a flat root —
 * or into a non-canonical domain name — trips here with a clear message naming the
 * exact FQCN that drifted.
 */
test('split classes resolve under their canonical domain namespace', function (): void {
    // String literals (NOT ::class) so the check is independent of imports: each
    // class MUST exist at exactly this canonical per-domain FQCN. A regression that
    // leaves a class flat or under a wrong domain makes class_exists() false here.
    $expected = [
        'Vaulter\Models\Drive\Node',
        'Vaulter\Models\Cas\Blob',
        'Vaulter\Models\Access\NodeGrant',
        'Vaulter\Models\Sharing\NodeShare',
        'Vaulter\Drive\Models\Uploads\UploadSession',
        'Vaulter\Models\Activity\Activity',
        'Vaulter\Documents\Models\Revisions\DocumentRevision',
        'Vaulter\Enums\Drive\NodeKind',
        'Vaulter\Enums\Access\Ability',
        'Vaulter\Events\Sharing\NodeShareCreated',
        'Vaulter\Drive\Exceptions\Nodes\NodeCycleException',
        'Vaulter\Exceptions\Schema\UnknownIdStrategyException',
        'Vaulter\Exceptions\Profiles\UnknownProfileException',
        'Vaulter\Repositories\Drive\NodeReadRepository',
        'Vaulter\Contracts\Cas\BlobStore',
        'Vaulter\Contracts\Access\PermissionDriver',
        'Vaulter\Documents\ValueObjects\TipTapContent',
        'Vaulter\Access\ValueObjects\NodeAbilities',
    ];

    $missing = array_values(array_filter(
        $expected,
        fn (string $fqcn): bool => !class_exists($fqcn) && !interface_exists($fqcn),
    ));

    expect($missing)->toBe([]);
});

/**
 * H.4 arch-ban: recursive descendant aggregation in request paths is fatal on
 * MariaDB (no correlated CTEs) and degrades on Postgres. No non-test src file may
 * call whereHas('descendants') or withCount('descendants'); subtree work goes
 * through NodeReadRepository (withMaxDepth) or direct EXISTS / denorm counters.
 */
test('non-test src never uses whereHas/withCount on descendants (H.4)', function (): void {
    $src = __DIR__.'/../../src';
    $offenders = [];

    /** @var Iterator<SplFileInfo> $files */
    $files = new RegexIterator(
        new RecursiveIteratorIterator(new RecursiveDirectoryIterator($src)),
        '/\.php$/',
    );

    foreach ($files as $file) {
        $contents = file_get_contents($file->getPathname());

        if ($contents === false) {
            continue;
        }

        // Strip comments + docblocks so the ban only fires on real code (the H.4
        // rule is about query calls, not prose explaining the rule).
        $code = '';

        foreach (token_get_all($contents) as $token) {
            if (is_array($token) && in_array($token[0], [T_COMMENT, T_DOC_COMMENT], true)) {
                continue;
            }

            $code .= is_array($token) ? $token[1] : $token;
        }

        if (preg_match("/(whereHas|withCount)\\(\\s*['\"]descendants['\"]/", $code) === 1) {
            $offenders[] = $file->getPathname();
        }
    }

    expect($offenders)->toBe([]);
});

/**
 * P2 #5 / ADR-0015 — package dependency direction. The physical package split keeps
 * ONE direction: satellites depend on core, core depends on NOTHING in the Vaulter
 * ecosystem. This guards that the extracted vaulter-media package (its CAS engine
 * under Vaulter\Media) is NEVER referenced back from core (or any other Vaulter code
 * except media itself) — a leak would recreate the cycle the extraction avoided.
 *
 * The drive (D1) and documents (D2) extractions landed as file-scan guards below
 * instead of this `->ignoring(...)` shape — see `coreReferencesTo()` for why.
 */
arch('core (and all Vaulter code) never depends on the extracted vaulter-media package')
    ->expect('Vaulter')
    ->not->toUse('Vaulter\Media')
    ->ignoring('Vaulter\Media');

/**
 * Scans packages/core/src for a `Vaulter\<root>\` reference OUTSIDE comments/docblocks
 * (the ActivityRecorder/OutboxRecorder/VaulterManager docblocks legitimately name
 * extracted-package classes in prose explaining the seam split). This is a file scan
 * (NOT `expect('Vaulter')->not->toUse(...)`) so it enforces core⊥<package> WITHOUT an
 * ->ignoring exclusion: each satellite is a require-dev sibling autoloaded into the
 * core test run, so the namespace-graph form would need ->ignoring('Vaulter\<root>')
 * to skip the satellite's own internal self-references — this form instead asserts the
 * precise invariant (zero references from CORE SOURCE) and self-updates as new core
 * files are added. `Vaulter\<root>\` matches the package root only; the kernel
 * DATA-domain namespaces (Vaulter\Models\Drive, Vaulter\Repositories\Drive, …) do not
 * start with that prefix and are correctly ignored. Shared by the drive (D1) and
 * documents (D2) dependency-direction guards below.
 *
 * @return list<string>
 */
function coreReferencesTo(string $root): array
{
    $src = __DIR__.'/../../src';
    $offenders = [];

    /** @var Iterator<SplFileInfo> $files */
    $files = new RegexIterator(
        new RecursiveIteratorIterator(new RecursiveDirectoryIterator($src)),
        '/\.php$/',
    );

    $pattern = '/\\bVaulter\\\\'.preg_quote($root, '/').'\\\\/';

    foreach ($files as $file) {
        $contents = file_get_contents($file->getPathname());

        if ($contents === false) {
            continue;
        }

        $code = '';

        foreach (token_get_all($contents) as $token) {
            if (is_array($token) && in_array($token[0], [T_COMMENT, T_DOC_COMMENT], true)) {
                continue;
            }

            $code .= is_array($token) ? $token[1] : $token;
        }

        if (preg_match($pattern, $code) === 1) {
            $offenders[] = $file->getPathname();
        }
    }

    return $offenders;
}

test('core source never references the extracted vaulter-drive package (P2 #5 / D1)', function (): void {
    expect(coreReferencesTo('Drive'))->toBe([]);
});

/**
 * P2 #5 / ADR-0015, Phase D2 — vaulter-documents is now PHYSICALLY extracted (its code
 * lives in packages/documents, namespace Vaulter\Documents\*). The transitional seams
 * are cut: the 7 Contracts\Handlers extensibility VOs + UnknownExportFormatException/
 * UnsupportedDocumentContentException moved to core (kernel-shared, T6/D2 finding);
 * TipTapContent/LinkSchemeValidator/OpaqueDocumentContent/TiptapExtensions/
 * InvalidDocumentContentException moved BACK to documents (VLT-CANON P0.3 — TipTap
 * isolation, core never knew their shape beyond the DocumentContent contract); the
 * FileHandlerRegistry/NodePresenter contracts + `Vaulter::handlers()->register()` resolve
 * the documents package's bindings without naming its classes; HostUserResolver
 * (default + binding) moved to that package entirely; the upload/comment/
 * document-version Config defaults inverted; the document/comment/collab routes + the
 * handler/broadcast provider wiring moved to its own provider. Same file-scan form as
 * the drive guard above.
 */
test('core source never references the extracted vaulter-documents package (P2 #5 / D2)', function (): void {
    expect(coreReferencesTo('Documents'))->toBe([]);
});

/**
 * The optional permission bridge owns its complete guard seam and driver.
 * Core source has no dependency on the bridge package.
 */
test('core source never references the vaulter-azgard package (P2.1)', function (): void {
    expect(coreReferencesTo('Azgard'))->toBe([]);
});

/**
 * VLT-CANON P0.3/P3.2 — TipTap is fully isolated behind the opaque
 * {@see DocumentContent} seam; core must never name a
 * concrete TipTap CLASS (`TipTapContent`, `TiptapExtensions`, `InvalidDocumentContentException`,
 * …) in real code. Matches the CamelCase class-name spelling only — the lower-case
 * `vaulter.tiptap.*` config keys (Support/Config.php) are a deliberate, documented
 * pass-through for a host's own TipTap extensions (VLT-REMED D27/D28) and are NOT a
 * class coupling, so they never trip this pattern. Prose mentions of "TipTap" in
 * comments/docblocks (e.g. DocumentContent/DocumentExporter explaining the seam) are
 * legitimate and stripped the same way `coreReferencesTo()` strips them.
 */
test('core source never references a concrete TipTap class (VLT-CANON P0.3)', function (): void {
    $src = __DIR__.'/../../src';
    $offenders = [];

    /** @var Iterator<SplFileInfo> $files */
    $files = new RegexIterator(
        new RecursiveIteratorIterator(new RecursiveDirectoryIterator($src)),
        '/\.php$/',
    );

    foreach ($files as $file) {
        $contents = file_get_contents($file->getPathname());

        if ($contents === false) {
            continue;
        }

        $code = '';

        foreach (token_get_all($contents) as $token) {
            if (is_array($token) && in_array($token[0], [T_COMMENT, T_DOC_COMMENT], true)) {
                continue;
            }

            $code .= is_array($token) ? $token[1] : $token;
        }

        if (preg_match('/\bTipTap[A-Za-z]+\b/', $code) === 1) {
            $offenders[] = $file->getPathname();
        }
    }

    expect($offenders)->toBe([]);
});

/**
 * VLT-CANON P0.1/D7/P3.2 — the engine-extensibility contract is kind-neutral
 * (`FileHandler`, not `DocumentHandler`): it describes ANY file, editable or not, so
 * it must never depend on the extracted vaulter-documents package (TipTap/Univer are
 * one KIND of handler among many — preview/download are not "engines"). This is the
 * final-canon guard for D7: a regression that re-couples the contract seam to a
 * specific document engine trips here, not just the broader core⊥documents guard
 * above (which only scans `src/`, not the namespace-graph form PestArch offers for a
 * single sub-namespace).
 */
arch('the FileHandler contract seam is kind-neutral and never depends on vaulter-documents (D7)')
    ->expect('Vaulter\Contracts\Handlers')
    ->not->toUse('Vaulter\Documents');

arch('DB facade only in Database and Schema (AD25)')
    ->expect('Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB')
    ->toOnlyBeUsedIn(['Vaulter\Database', 'Vaulter\Schema'])
    ->ignoring(['Vaulter\Tests', 'Vaulter\Load']);

arch('domain exceptions implement the HTTP problem contract')
    ->expect('Vaulter\Exceptions')
    ->classes()
    ->toImplement('Vaulter\Exceptions\Contracts\ProblemException')
    ->ignoring([
        'Vaulter\Exceptions\VaulterException',
        'Vaulter\Exceptions\Access\MissingPermissionDriverException',

        'Vaulter\Exceptions\Schema\UnknownIdStrategyException',
        'Vaulter\Exceptions\Support\MissingPackageException',
        'Vaulter\Exceptions\Tenancy\TenancyMisconfiguredException',
        'Vaulter\Exceptions\Webhooks\WebhookResponseTooLargeException',
    ]);

arch('production source never imports testing helpers (D35)')

    ->ignoring(['Vaulter\Testing', 'Vaulter\Tests']);

/**
 * D23: retain exactly these live collaboration keys until P2.5. Each allowed
 * line must occur once in its named file; imports, prose and duplicates fail.
 *
 * @return list<string>
 */
function coreBridgeImplementationNameViolations(string $path, string $contents): array
{
    $allowList = [
        'src/Support/Config.php' => [
            "        \$value = config('vaulter.collaboration.driver', 'hocuspocus');" => 1,
            "        return is_string(\$value) ? \$value : 'hocuspocus';" => 1,
            "        \$value = config('vaulter.collaboration.drivers.hocuspocus.secret');" => 1,
            "        \$value = config('vaulter.collaboration.drivers.hocuspocus.token_ttl', 3600);" => 1,
            "        \$value = config('vaulter.collaboration.drivers.hocuspocus.url');" => 1,
        ],
        'config/vaulter.php' => [
            "        'driver' => env('VAULTER_COLLAB_DRIVER', 'hocuspocus')," => 1,
            "            'hocuspocus' => [" => 1,
        ],
    ];
    $allowed = $allowList[$path] ?? [];
    $counts = array_fill_keys(array_keys($allowed), 0);
    $offenders = [];

    foreach (explode("\n", $contents) as $index => $line) {
        if (preg_match('/azgard|hocuspocus|filament/i', $line) !== 1) {
            continue;
        }

        if (isset($allowed[$line])) {
            $counts[$line]++;

            if ($counts[$line] <= $allowed[$line]) {
                continue;
            }
        }

        $offenders[] = $path.':'.($index + 1).': '.$line;
    }

    foreach ($allowed as $line => $expected) {
        if ($counts[$line] !== $expected) {
            $offenders[] = $path.': expected '.$expected.' occurrence of '.$line.', got '.$counts[$line];
        }
    }

    return $offenders;
}

test('core source and configuration contain no bridge implementation names (P2.4)', function (): void {
    $offenders = [];
    $package = dirname(__DIR__, 2);

    foreach ([$package.'/src', $package.'/config'] as $directory) {
        $files = new RegexIterator(
            new RecursiveIteratorIterator(new RecursiveDirectoryIterator($directory)),
            '/\.php$/',
        );

        foreach ($files as $file) {
            $contents = file_get_contents($file->getPathname());
            expect($contents)->not->toBeFalse();
            $path = substr($file->getPathname(), strlen($package) + 1);
            $offenders = [...$offenders, ...coreBridgeImplementationNameViolations($path, $contents)];
        }
    }

    expect($offenders)->toBe([]);
});

test('the bridge-name guard rejects imports and duplicate runtime exceptions', function (): void {
    $path = 'src/Support/Config.php';
    $contents = file_get_contents(__DIR__.'/../../'.$path);
    expect($contents)->not->toBeFalse();

    foreach ([
        'use Vaulter\\Azgard\\AzgardPermissionDriver;',
        'use Vaulter\\Filament\\VaulterPlugin;',
        'use Vaulter\\Documents\\Collaboration\\HocuspocusDriver;',
        "        \$value = config('vaulter.collaboration.driver', 'hocuspocus');",
    ] as $extraLine) {
        expect(coreBridgeImplementationNameViolations($path, $contents."\n".$extraLine))->not->toBe([]);
    }
});

use Illuminate\Console\Events\CommandFinished;
use Illuminate\Contracts\Queue\Job;
use Illuminate\Queue\Events\JobFailed;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Artisan;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Bus;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Http;
use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Queue;
use Illuminate\Support\Str;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Input\ArrayInput;
use Symfony\Component\Console\Output\BufferedOutput;
use Vaulter\Contracts\Observability\MetricsRecorder;
use Vaulter\Contracts\Webhooks\OutboundUrlGuard;
use Vaulter\Enums\Events\EventType;
use Vaulter\Jobs\Webhooks\DeliverWebhook;
use Vaulter\Load\Listeners\RecordCommandPeakMemory;
use Vaulter\Load\Listeners\RecordFailedJob;
use Vaulter\Load\Observability\LoadStateMetrics;
use Vaulter\Testing\FakeMetricsRecorder;
use Vaulter\Tests\Webhooks\WebhookTestHelpers;
use Vaulter\Webhooks\OutboxRecorder;
use Vaulter\Webhooks\OutboxRelay;
use Vaulter\Webhooks\WebhookRetryDispatcher;
use Vaulter\Webhooks\WebhookSigner;

beforeEach(function (): void {
    config()->set('vaulter.observability.enabled', true);
    config()->set('vaulter.observability.recorder', FakeMetricsRecorder::class);
    $this->app->forgetInstance(MetricsRecorder::class);
});

it('records vaulter_outbox_backlog from pending outbox rows', function (): void {
    WebhookTestHelpers::outbox(['status' => 'pending']);
    WebhookTestHelpers::outbox(['status' => 'dispatched']);

    app(LoadStateMetrics::class)->observeOutboxBacklog();

    app(MetricsRecorder::class)->assertGauge(name: 'vaulter_outbox_backlog');
});

it('records vaulter_outbox_stage_duration_seconds when staging a new row', function (): void {
    app(OutboxRecorder::class)->stage(
        event: EventType::GrantCreated,
        eventId: (string) Str::ulid(),
        panel: 'default',
        topic: 'node-1',
        payload: ['grant_id' => 'g-1'],
        actorId: 1,
    );

    app(MetricsRecorder::class)->assertHistogram(name: 'vaulter_outbox_stage_duration_seconds');
});

it('records outbox relay metrics for a pending row', function (): void {
    Queue::fake();

    WebhookTestHelpers::endpoint();
    WebhookTestHelpers::endpoint(['events' => ['grant.created'], 'url' => 'https://hooks.test/other']);
    WebhookTestHelpers::outbox();

    app(OutboxRelay::class)->process();

    $recorder = app(MetricsRecorder::class);
    $recorder->assertHistogram(name: 'vaulter_outbox_relay_duration_seconds');
    $recorder->assertCounter(name: 'vaulter_outbox_relayed_total');
    $recorder->assertCounter(name: 'vaulter_outbox_endpoints_scanned_total');

    $scanned = collect($recorder->emissions())
        ->where('name', 'vaulter_outbox_endpoints_scanned_total')
        ->sum('value');

    expect($scanned)->toBe(1);
});

it('records webhook retry tick and lockset metrics', function (): void {
    Bus::fake();

    WebhookTestHelpers::delivery(
        WebhookTestHelpers::endpoint(),
        ['status' => 'failed', 'next_retry_at' => now()->subSecond()],
    );

    app(WebhookRetryDispatcher::class)->redispatchDue();

    $recorder = app(MetricsRecorder::class);
    $recorder->assertHistogram(name: 'vaulter_webhook_retry_tick_seconds');
    $recorder->assertHistogram(name: 'vaulter_webhook_retry_lockset_rows');
});

it('records webhook delivery metrics on successful deliver', function (): void {
    Http::fake(['https://hooks.test/*' => Http::response('', 200)]);

    $delivery = WebhookTestHelpers::delivery(WebhookTestHelpers::endpoint());

    (new DeliverWebhook(deliveryId: (string) $delivery->getKey()))
        ->handle(app(WebhookSigner::class), app(OutboundUrlGuard::class));

    $recorder = app(MetricsRecorder::class);
    $recorder->assertHistogram(name: 'vaulter_webhook_queue_wait_seconds', labels: ['outcome' => 'success']);
    $recorder->assertHistogram(name: 'vaulter_webhook_delivery_duration_seconds', labels: ['outcome' => 'success']);
    $recorder->assertCounter(name: 'vaulter_webhook_delivered_total', labels: ['outcome' => 'success']);
});

it('records vaulter_failed_jobs_total on job failed event', function (): void {
    $exception = new RuntimeException('job failed hard');
    $job = Mockery::mock(Job::class);

    app(RecordFailedJob::class)->handle(new JobFailed(connectionName: 'redis', job: $job, exception: $exception));

    app(MetricsRecorder::class)->assertCounter(name: 'vaulter_failed_jobs_total', labels: ['outcome' => 'failure']);
});

it('records vaulter_command_peak_memory_bytes for vaulter artisan commands', function (): void {
    $commands = [
        'vaulter:sweep-uploads',
        'vaulter:blobs:gc',
        'vaulter:blobs:reconcile',
        'vaulter:purge-trash',
        'vaulter:prune-webhooks',
        'vaulter:retry-webhooks',
        'vaulter:relay-outbox',
    ];

    foreach ($commands as $command) {
        app(RecordCommandPeakMemory::class)->handle(new CommandFinished(
            command: $command,
            input: new ArrayInput([]),
            output: new BufferedOutput,
            exitCode: 0,
        ));

        app(MetricsRecorder::class)->assertGauge(
            name: 'vaulter_command_peak_memory_bytes',
            labels: ['command' => $command],
        );
    }
});

it('records prune webhook metrics when rows are reclaimed', function (): void {
    config()->set('vaulter.features.reliability', true);
    config()->set('vaulter.webhooks.retention_days', 0);

    $threshold = now()->subDay();
    WebhookTestHelpers::outbox([
        'status' => 'dispatched',
        'dispatched_at' => $threshold,
    ]);

    Artisan::call('vaulter:prune-webhooks');

    $recorder = app(MetricsRecorder::class);
    $recorder->assertHistogram(name: 'vaulter_prune_duration_seconds');
    $recorder->assertCounter(name: 'vaulter_prune_rows_total');
});

it('exposes vaulter_pg_lock_wait_seconds from the harness collector script', function (): void {
    $script = dirname(__DIR__, 5).'/load/scripts/collect-postgres-lock-waits.sh';

    expect(is_file($script))->toBeTrue()
        ->and(file_get_contents($script))->toContain('vaulter_pg_lock_wait_seconds');
});

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// The documents package is strict-typed end to end.
arch('strict types')
    ->expect('Vaulter\Documents')
    ->toUseStrictTypes();

// T6 — documents requires ONLY core in production; it never depends on drive or
// media (both are optional siblings over the same kernel, not peers of documents).
arch('documents never depends on drive or media (T6 — documents requires only core)')
    ->expect('Vaulter\Documents')
    ->not->toUse(['Vaulter\Drive', 'Vaulter\Media']);

// E5.1 / F-P4.3-01 — declarative form kept for discoverability/grep (`toUse('App')`);
// see the file-scan test below (and core's ArchTest.php) for why this namespace-graph
// form cannot itself observe a real "uses" edge in this dev/test environment.
arch('the package never depends on the host application (E5.1)')
    ->expect('Vaulter\Documents')
    ->not->toUse('App');

/**
 * E5.1 / F-P4.3-01 — vaulter-documents is an embeddable Laravel package: it must never
 * reach into the HOST application's namespace. File scan (not
 * `expect(...)->not->toUse('App')`) because `App\*` is never an autoloadable class in
 * the package's own dev/test environment (red-before proven on core's ArchTest.php).
 */
test('non-test src never references the host App namespace (E5.1, F-P4.3-01)', function (): void {
    $src = __DIR__.'/../../src';
    $offenders = [];

    /** @var Iterator<SplFileInfo> $files */
    $files = new RegexIterator(
        new RecursiveIteratorIterator(new RecursiveDirectoryIterator($src)),
        '/\.php$/',
    );

    foreach ($files as $file) {
        $contents = file_get_contents($file->getPathname());

        if ($contents === false) {
            continue;
        }

        $code = '';

        foreach (token_get_all($contents) as $token) {
            if (is_array($token) && in_array($token[0], [T_COMMENT, T_DOC_COMMENT], true)) {
                continue;
            }

            $code .= is_array($token) ? $token[1] : $token;
        }

        if (preg_match('/\\bApp\\\\/', $code) === 1) {
            $offenders[] = $file->getPathname();
        }
    }

    expect($offenders)->toBe([]);
});

/**
 * E3.1 / F-P4.3-02 — documents HAS its own package sub-namespace, so the public-API
 * boundary is enforceable at full strength here: `Repositories/`/`Support/` are
 * internal implementation detail and must never be referenced from outside
 * `Vaulter\Documents` itself (verified: no other package currently references
 * `Vaulter\Documents\Repositories`/`Vaulter\Documents\Support`).
 */
arch('internal namespaces are not used outside the package (E3.1)')
    ->expect(['Vaulter\Documents\Repositories', 'Vaulter\Documents\Support'])
    ->toOnlyBeUsedIn('Vaulter\Documents');

/**
 * ADR-0017 / VLT-REMED P4.9 + P4.10 — Canon A, Law 2 (domain sub-namespace within layers).
 *
 * `documents` was DIVERGENT: its layers were layer-first (Law 1 ✅) but FLAT — classes
 * sat directly in the layer root with no domain sub-namespace, unlike core's
 * `Actions/Sharing`, `Enums/Webhooks`, … . P4.10 DISCHARGED it: the flat classes were
 * grouped under domain sub-namespaces (`Actions/Comments`, `Actions/Documents`,
 * `Actions/Revisions`, `Actions/Collaboration`, `Enums/Export`, `Models/Revisions`, …).
 * This test now asserts the CANON (no non-allow-listed class flat at a layer root)
 * and passes GREEN; the `->todo()` was removed by P4.10.
 *
 * Mirrors core's green `split technical roots keep classes in domain subfolders`
 * test. Red-before proven (P4.9): before the move, this body failed with offenders
 * in Actions (9), Data (6), Events (6), Enums (4), Repositories (4), Models (2).
 */
test('layers group classes under a domain sub-namespace, not flat (ADR-0017 Law 2)', function (): void {
    $src = __DIR__.'/../../src';

    // layer root => bare class names allowed to remain flat at the root (canon
    // cross-cutting citizens; documents currently declares none).
    $rootsWithAllowed = [
        'Actions' => [],
        'Models' => [],
        'Repositories' => [],
        'Enums' => [],
        'Events' => [],
        'Data' => [],
    ];

    $offenders = [];

    foreach ($rootsWithAllowed as $root => $allowed) {
        $dir = "{$src}/{$root}";

        if (!is_dir($dir)) {
            continue;
        }

        foreach (scandir($dir) ?: [] as $entry) {
            if (!str_ends_with($entry, '.php')) {
                continue;
            }

            $class = substr($entry, 0, -4);

            if (!in_array($class, $allowed, true)) {
                $offenders[] = "{$root}/{$entry}";
            }
        }
    }

    expect($offenders)->toBe([]);
});

arch('DB facade is routed through VaulterDatabase (AD25)')
    ->expect('Vaulter\Documents')
    ->not->toUse('Illuminate\Support\Facades\DB');

arch('domain exceptions implement the HTTP problem contract')
    ->expect('Vaulter\Documents\Exceptions')
    ->classes()
    ->toImplement('Vaulter\Exceptions\Contracts\ProblemException')
    ->ignoring([
        'Vaulter\Documents\Exceptions\CollaborationConfigException',
    ]);

arch('production source never imports testing helpers (D35)')
    ->expect('Vaulter\Documents')
    ->not->toUse('Vaulter\Documents\Testing')
    ->ignoring(['Vaulter\Documents\Testing', 'Vaulter\Documents\Tests']);

<<<M FILE packages/drive/src/Http/Controllers/Drives/ShowDriveController.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Drive\Http\Controllers\Drives;

use Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Access\Authorizable;
use Illuminate\Http\Request;
use Vaulter\Access\AccessResolver;
use Vaulter\Drive\Http\Resources\DriveResource;
use Vaulter\Enums\Access\Ability;
use Vaulter\Exceptions\Access\PermissionDeniedException;
use Vaulter\Http\Controllers\Controller;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Drive;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Node;
use Vaulter\Repositories\Drive\NodeReadRepository;

/**
 * Read surface for a storage container (§2.1): its meta, the root node the client
 * opens into, and the used/quota accounting. Thin — the storage arrives
 * route-model resolved (swappable model bound in the provider); the Resource
 * shapes the response.
 *
 * Authorization (M2a / H.2): a storage's "view" maps to View on its ROOT node, so
 * show() guards Ability::View on the storage root through the AccessResolver before
 * returning the meta (mirroring NodeController's per-ACTION guarding); a denial 403s
 * via PermissionDeniedException. The root is resolved READ-ONLY (the BelongsTo on
 * root_node_id, never the provisioning StorageManager — a read endpoint must never
 * write), exactly as the admin drive resource resolves it for its ability flags.
 */
final class ShowDriveController extends Controller
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly AccessResolver $access,
        private readonly NodeReadRepository $nodes,
    ) {}

    /**
     * Guard View on the storage root before exposing the meta. Edge cases (matched to
     * NodeController's semantics):
     *
     *   - No root node (root_node_id null / the row missing): a storage is ALWAYS
     *     provisioned with its root folder in one transaction (StorageManager::provision),
     *     so a missing root is a corrupt/transient state with no node to authorize against.
     *     It 404s for EVERYONE — never leaking the meta (name, owner, quota) to a grantless
     *     actor — matching the package's deny-on-missing-root convention (ActivityController
     *     "a miss is a corrupt state and 404s" / DocumentNodeController::driveRoot abort(404)).
     *   - Null actor (unauthenticated): denied on a rooted storage — no actor ⇒ no grant
     *     ⇒ 403 (exactly NodeController::guard); on a rootless storage the 404 above fires
     *     first, so the meta never reaches an actor-less caller either way.
     *   - Open drivers (gate/spatie/azgard/null): $access->can delegates to the active
     *     host-role driver, so an open driver decides exactly as it does for the node
     *     listings — the database driver is never hard-coded here.
     */
    public function __invoke(Request $request, Drive $storage): DriveResource
    {
        $root = $this->root($storage);

        if (!$root instanceof Node) {
            // No root folder to gate View on. Provisioning is transactional (the root is
            // born with the storage), so this is a corrupt/transient row, not a viewable
            // "unrooted shell": 404 for everyone rather than serving the meta ungated.
            abort(404);
        }

        $this->guard($request, Ability::View, $root);

        return DriveResource::make($storage);
    }

    /**
     * The storage root node, resolved READ-ONLY through the read repository (never the
     * provisioning StorageManager — a read endpoint must not write). Null when the
     * storage has no root_node_id yet, or the row is missing — matching how
     * the admin drive resource resolves the root for its ability flags.
     */
    private function root(Drive $storage): ?Node
    {
        if ($storage->root_node_id === null) {
            return null;
        }

        return $this->nodes->find($storage->root_node_id);
    }

    /**
     * Authorize an ability on a node through the AccessResolver (H.2), throwing a
     * 403 PermissionDeniedException when denied. An unauthenticated request is also
     * denied (no actor ⇒ no grant). Mirrors NodeController::guard.
     */
    private function guard(Request $request, Ability $ability, Node $node): void
    {
        $actor = $this->authorizable($request);

        if ($actor === null || !$this->access->can($actor, $ability, $node)) {
            throw PermissionDeniedException::forAbility($ability->value);
        }
    }

    /**
     * The acting authorizable for the request, or null when unauthenticated.
     */
    private function authorizable(Request $request): ?Authorizable
    {
        $user = $request->user();

        return $user instanceof Authorizable ? $user : null;
    }
}

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

// The drive package is strict-typed end to end.
arch('strict types')
    ->expect('Vaulter\Drive')
    ->toUseStrictTypes();

// T11 — drive and documents are independent siblings over core: nothing under
// Vaulter\Drive may reach into the documents engine. The Drive node read shape that
// embedded the document handler descriptor moved to core (Http\Resources\Drive\
// NodeResource) precisely so this stays true.
arch('drive never depends on documents')
    ->expect('Vaulter\Drive')
    ->not->toUse('Vaulter\Documents');

// E5.1 / F-P4.3-01 — declarative form kept for discoverability/grep (`toUse('App')`);
// see the file-scan test below (and core's ArchTest.php) for why this namespace-graph
// form cannot itself observe a real "uses" edge in this dev/test environment.
arch('the package never depends on the host application (E5.1)')
    ->expect('Vaulter\Drive')
    ->not->toUse('App');

/**
 * E5.1 / F-P4.3-01 — vaulter-drive is an embeddable Laravel package: it must never
 * reach into the HOST application's namespace. File scan (not
 * `expect(...)->not->toUse('App')`) because `App\*` is never an autoloadable class in
 * the package's own dev/test environment (red-before proven on core's ArchTest.php).
 */
test('non-test src never references the host App namespace (E5.1, F-P4.3-01)', function (): void {
    $src = __DIR__.'/../../src';
    $offenders = [];

    /** @var Iterator<SplFileInfo> $files */
    $files = new RegexIterator(
        new RecursiveIteratorIterator(new RecursiveDirectoryIterator($src)),
        '/\.php$/',
    );

    foreach ($files as $file) {
        $contents = file_get_contents($file->getPathname());

        if ($contents === false) {
            continue;
        }

        $code = '';

        foreach (token_get_all($contents) as $token) {
            if (is_array($token) && in_array($token[0], [T_COMMENT, T_DOC_COMMENT], true)) {
                continue;

            $code .= is_array($token) ? $token[1] : $token;

        }
    }

    expect($offenders)->toBe([]);

/**
 * ADR-0017 / VLT-REMED P4.9 + P4.10 — Canon A, Law 1 (layer-first placement).
 *
 * `drive` was DIVERGENT: the `Uploads/` module carried its own nested layer tree
 * (`Uploads/Actions`, `Uploads/Models`, `Uploads/Repositories`, `Uploads/Http`,
 * `Uploads/Enums`, `Uploads/Data`, `Uploads/Contracts`) — a layer nested UNDER a
 * domain, the inverse of the core canon. P4.10 DISCHARGED it: those layer
 * subtrees were dissolved into the package-root layers with an `Uploads` domain
 * sub-namespace (`Actions/Uploads`, `Models/Uploads`, `Repositories/Uploads`,
 * `Enums/Uploads`, `Data/Uploads`, `Contracts/Uploads`, `Http/<sub>/Uploads`); the
 * flat upload service classes stayed as the `Uploads/` domain-service folder
 * (mirrors `core/src/Sharing`). This test now asserts the CANON and passes GREEN;
 * the `->todo()` was removed by P4.10.
 *
 * Red-before proven (P4.9): before the move, this body failed with offenders
 * `Uploads/Actions`, `Uploads/Contracts`, `Uploads/Data`, `Uploads/Enums`,
 * `Uploads/Http`, `Uploads/Http/Controllers`, `Uploads/Http/Requests`,
 * `Uploads/Http/Resources`, `Uploads/Models`, `Uploads/Repositories`.
 *
 * VLT-CANON P2.3 further split the `Uploads/` domain-service folder by role:
 * `*Handler`/`*Manager` orchestrators (`TusUploadHandler`, `S3MultipartHandler`,
 * `UploadSessionManager`) stayed; the pure helpers (`MagicByteSniffer`,
 * `StagedUpload`, `UploadModels`) moved to `Support/Uploads` — still outside the
 * `$layers` list below, so this test is unaffected.
 */
test('technical layers are never nested under a domain module (ADR-0017 Law 1)', function (): void {
    $src = __DIR__.'/../../src';
    $layers = ['Actions', 'Models', 'Repositories', 'Enums', 'Events', 'Data', 'Contracts', 'Http'];
    $offenders = [];

    // SELF_FIRST so DIRECTORIES are yielded (the default LEAVES_ONLY mode only
    // yields files, which would make this dir-structure check an inert no-op).
    /** @var Iterator<SplFileInfo> $dirs */
    $dirs = new RecursiveIteratorIterator(
        new RecursiveDirectoryIterator($src, FilesystemIterator::SKIP_DOTS),
        RecursiveIteratorIterator::SELF_FIRST,
    );

    foreach ($dirs as $dir) {
        if (!$dir->isDir()) {
            continue;
        }

        $relative = str_replace($src.'/', '', $dir->getPathname());
        $segments = explode('/', $relative);

        foreach ($segments as $index => $segment) {
            if ($index > 0 && in_array($segment, $layers, true)) {
                $offenders[] = $relative;
                break;
            }
        }
    }

    expect(array_values(array_unique($offenders)))->toBe([]);
});

<<<M FILE packages/drive/tests/Concurrency/QuotaRaceTest.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

use Illuminate\Support\Facades\Storage;
use Vaulter\Drive\Exceptions\Quota\QuotaExceededException;
use Vaulter\Models\Cas\Blob;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\File;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\FileRevisionBlob;
use Vaulter\Tests\Concurrency\ForkRace;
use Vaulter\Tests\Concurrency\RaceOutcome;
use Vaulter\Tests\Drive\DriveTestHelpers;

it('V02 admits exactly one 8 MiB upload into 10 MiB of free quota', function (): void {
    ForkRace::skipUnlessSupported($this);
    Storage::fake('local');
    $drive = DriveTestHelpers::drive();
    $drive->model()->forceFill(['quota_bytes' => 10 * 1024 * 1024])->save();
    // Different parents prevent the destination lock from hiding a broken quota UPDATE.
    $parents = [$drive->createFolder('A'), $drive->createFolder('B')];
    $outcomes = ForkRace::run(array_map(
        static fn (int $i): Closure => static fn (): string => (string) $drive->upload(
            DriveTestHelpers::streamFor(str_repeat((string) $i, 8 * 1024 * 1024)),
            into: $parents[$i], originalName: $i.'.bin',
        )->getKey(),
        [0, 1],
    ));
    $won = array_values(array_filter($outcomes, static fn (RaceOutcome $o): bool => $o->ok));
    $lost = array_values(array_filter($outcomes, static fn (RaceOutcome $o): bool => !$o->ok));
    expect($won)->toHaveCount(1)->and($lost)->toHaveCount(1);
    expect($lost[0]->failedWith(QuotaExceededException::class))->toBeTrue($lost[0]->message ?? '');
    expect($drive->model()->refresh()->used_bytes)->toBe(8 * 1024 * 1024)
        ->and((int) File::query()->sum('size_bytes'))->toBe(8 * 1024 * 1024)
        ->and(Blob::query()->count())->toBe(1)
        ->and(FileRevisionBlob::query()->count())->toBe(1);
    $blob = Blob::query()->sole();
    // Age the actual disk object, not Carbon: orphan grace uses filesystem mtime.
    touch(Storage::disk('local')->path($blob->storage_key), time() - 48 * 3600);
    $this->artisan('vaulter:blobs:reconcile', ['--orphans' => true, '--prune' => true, '--orphan-grace' => 24])->assertSuccessful();
    Storage::disk('local')->assertExists($blob->storage_key);
    expect(hash_file('sha256', Storage::disk('local')->path($blob->storage_key)))->toBe($blob->sha256);
});

<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Filament\Resources;

use BackedEnum;
use Filament\Infolists\Components\TextEntry;
use Filament\Resources\Pages\PageRegistration;
use Filament\Resources\Resource;
use Filament\Schemas\Components\Section;
use Filament\Schemas\Schema;
use Filament\Tables\Columns\TextColumn;
use Filament\Tables\Table;

use Override;
use UnitEnum;
use Vaulter\Filament\Resources\DriveResource\Pages\ListDrives;
use Vaulter\Filament\Resources\DriveResource\Pages\ViewDrive;
use Vaulter\Filament\Support\PanelAccessScope;
use Vaulter\Models\Drive\Drive;
use Vaulter\Support\Config;

/**
 * The drive admin surface (master plan §2.1 / §3): a read-mostly view of
 * the ownable, polymorphic disk roots — owner, disk, used/quota accounting and
 * status. Drives are provisioned by the DriveProvisioner (get-or-create on a
 * host entity), never minted from the panel, so this resource never creates/edits a
 * row; it lists and inspects.
 *
 * The model resolves through {@see Config::storageModel()} so a host that swaps the
 * Drive model still gets governed here.
 */
final class DriveResource extends Resource
{
    protected static ?string $model = Drive::class;

    protected static BackedEnum|string|null $navigationIcon = 'heroicon-o-circle-stack';

    protected static string|UnitEnum|null $navigationGroup = 'Vaulter';

    protected static ?string $recordTitleAttribute = 'name';

    #[Override]
    public static function getModel(): string
    {
        return Config::storageModel();
    }

    /**
     * Access-aware listing (F-P1.10-01): narrow to drives whose root node is in
     * the acting admin's grant-reachable candidate set — mirrors
     * {@see NodeResource::getEloquentQuery()}. A drive
     * has no other grant anchor of its own (a grant addresses a NODE), so "may see
     * this drive" reduces to "may reach its root". Empty candidate set (no actor,
     * or an actor with zero grants) ⇒ empty table, never an open listing.
     */
    #[Override]
    public static function getEloquentQuery(): Builder
    {
        $query = parent::getEloquentQuery();

        $nodeIds = PanelAccessScope::candidateNodeIds();

        if ($nodeIds === null) {
            // The active driver doesn't narrow by grant (host roles govern).
            return $query;
        }

        if ($nodeIds === []) {
            // `whereIn([], ...)` below is also empty; keep the explicit fail-closed branch readable.
            return $query->whereRaw('1 = 0'); // @pest-mutate-ignore: RemoveEarlyReturn
        }

        return $query->whereIn('root_node_id', $nodeIds);
    }

    #[Override]
    public static function infolist(Schema $schema): Schema
    {
        return $schema->components([
            Section::make('Drive')->schema([
                TextEntry::make('name'),
                TextEntry::make('profile')->badge(),
                TextEntry::make('disk'),
                TextEntry::make('storage_type')->label('Type'),
                TextEntry::make('status')->badge(),
            ])->columns(2),

            Section::make('Owner')->schema([
                TextEntry::make('owner_type')->label('Type'),
                TextEntry::make('owner_id')->label('Id'),
            ])->columns(2),

            Section::make('Usage')->schema([
                TextEntry::make('used_bytes')
                    ->label('Used')
                    ->formatStateUsing(fn (int $state): string => self::humanBytes($state)),
                TextEntry::make('quota_bytes')
                    ->label('Quota')
                    ->placeholder('Unlimited')
                    ->formatStateUsing(fn (?int $state): string => $state === null ? '∞' : self::humanBytes($state)),
            ])->columns(2),
        ]);
    }

    #[Override]
    public static function table(Table $table): Table
    {
        return $table
            ->columns([
                TextColumn::make('name')
                    ->searchable()
                    ->sortable(),

                TextColumn::make('owner_type')
                    ->label('Owner')
                    ->formatStateUsing(fn (string $state, Drive $record): string => $state.' #'.$record->owner_id)
                    ->toggleable(),

                TextColumn::make('disk')
                    ->badge()
                    ->toggleable(),

                TextColumn::make('used_bytes')
                    ->label('Used')
                    ->formatStateUsing(fn (int $state): string => self::humanBytes($state))
                    ->sortable(),

                TextColumn::make('quota_bytes')
                    ->label('Quota')
                    ->placeholder('∞')
                    ->formatStateUsing(fn (?int $state): string => $state === null ? '∞' : self::humanBytes($state))
                    ->toggleable(),

                TextColumn::make('status')
                    ->badge()
                    ->sortable(),

                TextColumn::make('created_at')
                    ->dateTime('d.m.Y H:i')
                    ->sortable()
                    ->toggleable(),
            ])
            ->defaultSort('created_at', 'desc');
    }

    #[Override]
    public static function canCreate(): bool
    {
        // Drives are provisioned by the DriveProvisioner, never from the panel.
        return false;
    }

    /**
     * @return array<string, PageRegistration>
     */
    #[Override]
    public static function getPages(): array
    {
        return [
            'index' => ListDrives::route('/'),
            'view' => ViewDrive::route('/{record}'),
        ];
    }

    /**
     * A compact, dependency-free human byte size for the usage columns.
     */
    private static function humanBytes(int $bytes): string
    {
        if ($bytes <= 0) {
            return '0 B';
        }

        $units = ['B', 'KB', 'MB', 'GB', 'TB', 'PB'];
        $power = (int) min(floor(log($bytes, 1024)), count($units) - 1);
        $value = $bytes / (1024 ** $power);

        return sprintf('%s %s', rtrim(rtrim(number_format($value, 2), '0'), '.'), $units[$power]);
    }
}

<<<M FILE packages/filament/src/VaulterPlugin.php>>>
<?php

declare(strict_types=1);

namespace Vaulter\Filament;

use Filament\Contracts\Plugin;
use Filament\Panel;
use Override;
use Vaulter\Filament\Resources\ActivityResource;
use Vaulter\Filament\Resources\DriveResource;
use Vaulter\Filament\Resources\NodeGrantResource;
use Vaulter\Filament\Resources\NodeResource;
use Vaulter\Filament\Resources\NodeShareResource;
use Vaulter\Support\Config;

/**
 * Vaulter Filament plugin (Filament 5).
 *
 * Register it in your PanelProvider:
 *
 *   $panel->plugins([ VaulterPlugin::make() ]);
 *
 * It registers the Drive/permissions resources (Drive, Node, NodeGrant,
 * NodeShare, Activity), each toggleable through
 * config('vaulter-filament.resources.*').
 *
 * Resources resolve their model through Vaulter\Support\Config::*Model(), so a host
 * that swaps a model keeps being governed by these resources.
 */
final class VaulterPlugin implements Plugin
{
    public static function make(): static
    {
        return new self;
    }

    /**
     * Localize the unsafe getPlugin() cast (H.5 / Filament 5): the panel's
     * getPlugin() returns the Plugin contract, so a caller that needs the concrete
     * plugin (its config, its toggles) gets a single typed accessor instead of an
     * inline cast scattered across the codebase.
     */
    public static function current(Panel $panel): self
    {
        /** @var self $plugin */
        $plugin = $panel->getPlugin('vaulter');

        return $plugin;
    }

    #[Override]
    public function getId(): string
    {
        return 'vaulter';
    }

    #[Override]
    public function register(Panel $panel): void
    {
        $panel->resources($this->enabledResources());
    }

    #[Override]
    public function boot(Panel $panel): void
    {
        //
    }

    /**
     * The resource classes to register, each gated by its OWN config toggle
     * (default on — the Drive/permissions domain over the unified v_nodes tree) AND,
     * where the resource's schema is behind a core SUBSYSTEM feature flag (one that a
     * host may disable independently of its own resource toggle), that flag too
     * (VLT-REMED P3.1 / F-P1.10-03, D13). Only `activity` qualifies today: `drive`/
     * `node` have no corresponding feature (drives/nodes are the unconditional
     * schema roots), and `grant`/`share` map to `grants`/`share_links` — both
     * consulted by `SchemaBuilder::entityEnabled()` for DYNAMICALLY-built
     * per-panel schemas, but the package's OWN static migrations always create
     * `v_node_grants`/`v_node_shares` unconditionally (only the ROUTES/UI are
     * feature-gated for them) — gating those two resources here would hide them by
     * default (`share_links` defaults `false`) with no missing-table risk to guard
     * against, which is not this finding's failure mode.
     *
     * @return array<int, class-string>
     */
    private function enabledResources(): array
    {
        $candidates = [
            // key => [resource class, core feature flag the schema needs (null = none)]
            'drive' => [DriveResource::class, null],
            'node' => [NodeResource::class, null],
            'grant' => [NodeGrantResource::class, null],
            'share' => [NodeShareResource::class, null],
            'activity' => [ActivityResource::class, 'activity'],
        ];

        $resources = [];

        foreach ($candidates as $key => [$class, $feature]) {
            if ($this->resourceEnabled($key, $feature)) {
                $resources[] = $class;
            }
        }

        return $resources;
    }

    /**
     * Whether a resource is enabled: its OWN config toggle
     * (config('vaulter-filament.resources.{key}'), default true) AND — when the
     * resource's schema is behind a core feature flag — that flag
     * (`Config::featureEnabled()`). Without the AND-condition, a host that disabled
     * the `activity` subsystem but left `ActivityResource`'s own default-on toggle
     * untouched would keep the resource registered against a subsystem it turned
     * off, turning a legitimate "subsystem off" configuration into a broken
     * navigation entry instead of the resource simply not appearing (F-P1.10-03,
     * D13: optional subsystems must degrade, not crash).
     */
    private function resourceEnabled(string $key, ?string $feature): bool
    {
        $value = config("vaulter-filament.resources.{$key}", true);
        $toggledOn = is_bool($value) ? $value : true;

        if (!$toggledOn) {
            return false;
        }

        return $feature === null || Config::featureEnabled($feature);
    }
}
